chinese: 苏格拉底：昨天，我与阿里斯通的儿子格劳孔一起下到比雷埃夫斯，向女神〔本狄斯〕礼拜，也想看看他们怎样举行这场节庆，因为这是头一次举办。我觉得本城公民的行列十分壮观，不过色雷斯人的队伍行进起来，也毫不逊色。
english: I went down yesterday to the Peiraeus with Glaucon, the son of Ariston, to pay my devotions to the Goddess, and also because I wished to see how they would conduct the festival since this was its inauguration. I thought the procession of the citizens very fine, but it was no better than the show, made by the marching of the Thracian contingent.

chinese:
祈祷完毕，也看过庆典，我们正要回城。克法洛斯的儿子玻勒马霍斯远远看见我们急着往家走，就叫他的童仆跑来，要我们等他。那孩子从后面拉住我的外衣，说：“玻勒马霍斯请你们等一等。”我转过身来，问他的主人在哪里。“就在你们后面，”他说，“正往这边来。等他一下。”
“我们会等的。”格劳孔说，
english: After we had said our prayers and seen the spectacle we were starting for town when Polemarchus, the son of Cephalus, caught sight of us from a distance as we were hastening homeward and ordered his boy run and bid us to wait for him, and the boy caught hold of my himation from behind and said, “Polemarchus wants you to wait.” And I turned around and asked where his master was. “There he is,” he said, “behind you, coming this way. Wait for him.” “So we will,” said Glaucon,

chinese:
不一会儿，玻勒马霍斯赶来了，同行的还有格劳孔的兄弟阿德曼托斯、尼基阿斯的儿子尼刻拉托斯，以及另外几个人，看样子也是从游行队伍那里过来的。玻勒马霍斯便说：“苏格拉底，看起来你们已经朝着城里，准备离开我们了。”
“猜得不错。”我说。
“可你也看见我们有多少人吧？”他说。
“当然。”
“那么，你们要么证明比我们更有力量，要么留下。”
“怎么，”我说，“难道没有另一条路，让我们说服你们应该放我们走吗？”
“可是，”他说，“假如我们不肯听，你们能说服我们吗？”
“不能。”格劳孔说。
“那我们就不听，你们也不妨就此拿定主意。”
“难道说，”阿德曼托斯插话道，
english:
and shortly after Polemarchus came up and Adeimantus, the brother of Glaucon, and Niceratus, the son of Nicias, and a few others apparently from the procession. Whereupon Polemarchus said, “Socrates, you appear to have turned your faces townward and to be going to leave us.” “Not a bad guess,” said I. “But you see how many we are?” he said. “Surely.” “You must either then prove yourselves the better men or stay here.” “Why, is there not left,” said I, “the alternative of our persuading you that you ought to let us go?” “But could you persuade us,” said he, “if we refused to listen?” “Nohow,” said Glaucon. “Well, we won’t listen, and you might as well make up your minds to it.”

“Do you mean to say,” interposed Adeimantus,

chinese:
“你们还没听说，今晚要举行骑马的火炬赛来敬奉女神吗？”
“骑马？”我说，“这可新鲜。他们是一边策马竞赛，一边拿着火炬相互传递，还是怎样？”
“正是这样，”玻勒马霍斯说，“而且还有值得一看的夜间庆典。吃过晚饭，我们就起身出去看热闹，在那里见见许多年轻人，好好谈一谈。所以留下来，答应我们吧。”
english: “that you haven’t heard that there is to be a torchlight race this evening on horseback in honor of the Goddess?” “On horseback?” said I. “That is a new idea. Will they carry torches and pass them along to one another as they race with the horses, or how do you mean?” “That’s the way of it,” said Polemarchus, “and, besides, there is to be a night festival which will be worth seeing. For after dinner we will get up and go out and see the sights and meet a lot of the lads there and have good talk. So stay and do as we ask.”

chinese:
“看来我们只好留下了。”格劳孔说。“好吧，”我说，“既然如此，就这样吧。”
于是，我们随他们去了玻勒马霍斯家。在那里，我们见到他的兄弟利西阿斯和欧绪德谟，还有卡尔刻冬的色拉叙马霍斯、派阿尼亚区的卡尔曼提德斯，以及阿里斯托纽摩斯的儿子克勒托丰。玻勒马霍斯的父亲克法洛斯也在家。我觉得他苍老了许多，
english:
“It looks as if we should have to stay,” said Glaucon. “Well,” said I, “if it so be, so be it.”

So we went with them to Polemarchus’s house, and there we found Lysias and Euthydemus, the brothers of Polemarchus, yes, and Thrasymachus, too, of Chalcedon, and Charmantides of the deme of Paeania, and Kleitophon the son of Aristonymus. And the father of Polemarchus, Cephalus, was also at home.

And I thought him much aged,

chinese: 因为我已经很久没见到他了。他坐在一张铺着软垫的长榻上，头戴花冠，因为刚刚在庭院里献过祭。我们走过去，在他身旁坐下，那里摆着一圈座位。克法洛斯一看见我，就招呼道：“苏格拉底，你不是常客啊。你不常下到比雷埃夫斯来看我们。这可不应该。假如我还能轻松地上城里去，就不必让你到这儿来，
english: for it was a long time since I had seen him. He was sitting on a sort of couch with cushions and he had a chaplet on his head, for he had just finished sacrificing in the court. So we went and sat down beside him, for there were seats there disposed in a circle. As soon as he saw me Cephalus greeted me and said, “You are not a very frequent visitor, Socrates. You don’t often come down to the Peiraeus to see us. That is not right. For if I were still able to make the journey up to town easily there would be no need of your resorting hither,

chinese:
我们会去看你的。可是如今，你来我们这里，就不该隔得太久。你要知道，对我来说，身体的满足越是衰减，我对美好交谈的渴望，以及从中得到的快乐，就越是增加。所以别推辞，要亲自做这些年轻人的伙伴，常来我们家，把我们当作你十分亲密的好友。”
“正是，克法洛斯，”我说，“而且我很喜欢与年纪很大的人交谈。
english: but we would go to visit you. But as it is you should not space too widely your visits here. For I would have you know that, for my part, as the satisfactions of the body decay, in the same measure my desire for the pleasures of good talk and my delight in them increase. Don’t refuse then, but be yourself a companion to these lads and make our house your resort and regard us as your very good friends and intimates.” “Why, yes, Cephalus,” said I, “and I enjoy talking with the very aged.

chinese:
在我看来，我们应该向他们请教，就像向先行的旅人打听一条我们自己也可能终有一天要走的路：它究竟怎样，是崎岖难行，还是平坦愉快。因此，现在你的年岁已经到了诗人所谓的‘老年门槛’，我很想听听你对这件事的看法。老年是人生中难以承受的一段，还是你有别的体会可以告诉我们？”
“当然，苏格拉底，”他说，“我会告诉你我自己的感受。
english:
For to my thinking we have to learn of them as it were from wayfarers who have preceded us on a road on which we too, it may be, must some time fare—what it is like—is it rough and hard going or easy and pleasant to travel. And so now I would fain learn of you what you think of this thing, now that your time has come to it, the thing that the poets call ‘the threshold of old age.’ Is it a hard part of life to bear or what report have you to make of it?”

“Yes, indeed, Socrates,” he said, “I will tell you my own feeling about it.

chinese: 我们这些年纪相仿的老人时常聚在一起，印证了那句同类相聚的老话。每逢这种聚会，大多数人都在哀叹，想念已经失去的青春欢乐，回忆饮酒、男女之乐、宴饮，以及与这些相连的种种事情。他们懊恼，觉得最重要的东西已被夺走，从前才叫生活，如今根本不能算活着。还有一些人
english: For it often happens that some of us elders of about the same age come together and verify the old saw of like to like. At these reunions most of us make lament, longing for the lost joys of youth and recalling to mind the pleasures of wine, women, and feasts, and other things thereto appertaining, and they repine in the belief that the greatest things have been taken from them and that then they lived well and now it is no life at all. And some of them

chinese: 抱怨朋友和亲属对老人的怠慢，把归咎于老年的种种不幸，一桩桩凄苦地说个不停。但在我看来，苏格拉底，他们没有责怪真正的原因。假如原因真在老年，那么就年老这一点说，我也应该有同样的感受，其他所有走到这个年纪的人也该如此。可事实上，我以前就遇到过另一些人，他们并不这么感受。我尤其记得，有人迎上诗人索福克勒斯，问道：
english: complain of the indignities that friends and kinsmen put upon old age and thereto recite a doleful litany of all the miseries for which they blame old age. But in my opinion, Socrates, they do not put the blame on the real cause. For if it were the cause I too should have had the same experience so far as old age is concerned, and so would all others who have come to this time of life. But in fact I have ere now met with others who do not feel in this way, and in particular I remember hearing Sophocles the poet greeted by a fellow who asked,

chinese: ‘索福克勒斯，你侍奉阿佛洛狄忒的情形如何——你的精力还没有衰退吗？’他回答：‘别说了，老兄！能摆脱你说的那件事，我高兴极了，简直像逃离了一个暴怒而凶残的主人。’当时我就觉得回答得好，如今更觉得如此。因为说实在的，在这些事情上，老年确实带来了极大的宁静和可喜的解脱。当激情与欲望的猛烈紧绷松弛下来，索福克勒斯的话就得到印证，
english: ‘How about your service of Aphrodite, Sophocles—is your natural force still unabated?’ And he replied, ‘Hush, man, most gladly have I escaped this thing you talk of, as if I had run away from a raging and savage beast of a master.’ I thought it a good answer then and now I think so still more. For in very truth there comes to old age a great tranquillity in such matters and a blessed release. When the fierce tensions of the passions and desires relax, then is the word of Sophocles approved,

chinese:
我们摆脱了许多疯狂的主人。不过，苏格拉底，至于那些抱怨，以及与亲属朋友相处的问题，原因只有一个，不在老年，而在人的性情。人若节制而开朗，即使老年也不过是适度的负担；倘若性情相反，那么苏格拉底，无论老年还是青年，对这种人都很艰难。”
听了这些话，我对这位老人十分钦佩，也想再听下去，便试着引他说得更多。我说：“我想，
english:
and we are rid of many and mad masters. But indeed in respect of these complaints and in the matter of our relations with kinsmen and friends there is just one cause, Socrates—not old age, but the character of the man. For if men are temperate and cheerful even old age is only moderately burdensome. But if the reverse, old age, Socrates, and youth are hard for such dispositions.”

And I was filled with admiration for the man by these words, and desirous of hearing more I tried to draw him out and said, “I fancy,

chinese:
克法洛斯，大多数人听你这样说，恐怕并不信服。他们认为你之所以能轻松承受老年，不是因为性情，而是因为财富。他们说，‘有钱人有许多慰藉。’”
“你说得对，”他说，“他们不接受我的看法；他们的反对也有一些道理，只是没有自己以为的那么多。忒弥斯托克勒斯的一句回话，用在这里正合适。有个来自塞里福斯小岛的人辱骂他，说他的声名不是得自本人，
english:
Cephalus, that most people, when they hear you talk in this way, are not convinced but think that you bear old age lightly not because of your character but because of your wealth. ‘For the rich,’ they say, ‘have many consolations.’”

“You are right,” he said. “They don’t accept my view and there is something in their objection, though not so much as they suppose. But the retort of Themistocles comes in pat here, who, when a man from the little island of Seriphus grew abusive and told him that he owed his fame not to himself

chinese:
而是得自出身的城邦；他回答，假如自己生在塞里福斯，也不会成名，但那个人即便生在雅典，也同样不会成名。这道理也十分适用于那些因为不富有而难忍老年的人：明理的人若又老又穷，也不会觉得完全容易忍受；而不明理的人，即使得到了财富，也决不会因此获得自足和愉快的心情。”
“克法洛斯，我可以问问吗？”我说，“你的财产大多是继承来的，还是自己挣来的？”
english: but to the city from which he came, replied that neither would he himself ever have made a name if he had been born in Seriphus nor the other if he had been an Athenian. And the same principle applies excellently to those who not being rich take old age hard; for neither would the reasonable man find it altogether easy to endure old age conjoined with poverty, nor would the unreasonable man by the attainment of riches ever attain to self-contentment and a cheerful temper.” “May I ask, Cephalus,” said I, “whether you inherited most of your possessions or acquired them yourself?”

chinese:
“挣来的，嗯？”他说，“就挣钱而言，我在祖父和父亲之间，差不多居于中间。与我同名的祖父继承了一份与我如今财产相仿的家业，又把它增加了许多倍；我的父亲里撒尼阿斯却把家产减少到比现在还少。我只要能把产业留给这些孩子，不少于自己继承的，稍稍再多一点，就满意了。”
“我之所以这样问，”我说，“是因为你在我看来并不过分爱钱。
english: “Acquired, eh?” he said. “As a moneymaker, I hold a place somewhere halfway between my grandfather and my father. For my grandfather and namesake inherited about as much property as I now possess and multiplied it many times, my father Lysanias reduced it below the present amount, and I am content if I shall leave the estate to these boys not less but by some slight measure more than my inheritance.” “The reason I asked,” I said, “is that you appear to me not to be over-fond of money.

chinese: 没有亲手挣来财富的人通常如此。可是亲自获得财富的人，与别人相比，爱钱有双重理由。诗人欣赏自己的诗，父亲珍爱自己的儿子，挣来财富的人也这样把钱看作自己的创造，认真看待它；同时，他们也和其他人一样，珍视钱的用途。所以，他们很难交谈，因为除了财富，他们不愿称赞别的东西。”
english: And that is generally the case with those who have not earned it themselves. But those who have themselves acquired it have a double reason in comparison with other men for loving it. For just as poets feel complacency about their own poems and fathers about their own sons, so men who have made money take this money seriously as their own creation and they also value it for its uses as other people do. So they are hard to talk to since they are unwilling to commend anything except wealth.”

chinese:
“你说得对。”他答道。“我确实说得对，”我说，“不过，请再告诉我这一点：在你看来，拥有财产给你带来的最大益处是什么？”
“有一件事，”他说，“说出来恐怕不容易让许多人相信。苏格拉底，我告诉你，”他说，“一个人开始意识到自己将要死去时，就会对以前从未想到的事情充满忧虑和关切。关于地下世界的传说，说在这里做了不正义之事的人必须到那里受罚，他过去即使曾经嘲笑这些传说，
english: “You are right,” he replied. “I assuredly am,” said I. “But tell me further this. What do you regard as the greatest benefit you have enjoyed from the possession of property?” “Something,” he said, “which I might not easily bring many to believe if I told them. For let me tell you, Socrates,” he said, “that when a man begins to realize that he is going to die, he is filled with apprehensions and concern about matters that before did not occur to him. The tales that are told of the world below and how the men who have done wrong here must pay the penalty there, though he may have laughed them down hitherto,

chinese: 这时也会因怀疑它们可能有些真实，而使灵魂受到折磨。除此之外，他本人也许由于老年的衰弱，也许由于如今离彼岸的事情更近，对它们的认识便略微清楚一些。无论如何，他满怀疑虑、猜测和惊恐，开始清点和考虑自己有没有亏待过谁。假如翻开自己一生的账簿，发现记着许多恶行，他就会像孩子一样，再三从梦中惊醒；白天也被将有更坏事情发生的预感纠缠。但自知没有做过不正义之事的人，
english:
then begin to torture his soul with the doubt that there may be some truth in them. And apart from that the man himself either from the weakness of old age or possibly as being now nearer to the things beyond has a somewhat clearer view of them. Be that as it may, he is filled with doubt, surmises, and alarms and begins to reckon up and consider whether he has ever wronged anyone.”

Now he to whom the ledger of his life shows an account of many evil deeds starts up even from his dreams like children again and again in affright and his days are haunted by anticipations of worse to come. But on him who is conscious of no wrong

chinese:
身旁总有甜美的希望相随，做他老年的好保姆，正如品达所说。苏格拉底，那诗人说，一个人若以正义和虔敬度过一生，
‘便有甜美的伴侣随行，鼓舞他的心，照料他的晚年：
那就是希望，她最能支配凡人变幻不定的心思。’
这真是美好而令人赞叹的话。我因此才说，拥有财富最有价值之处在于这里，
english:
that he has done a sweet hope ever attends and a goodly to be nurse of his old age, as Pindar too says. For a beautiful saying it is, Socrates, of the poet that when a man lives out his days in justice and piety ‘
sweet companion with him, to cheer his heart and nurse his old age, accompanies
Hope, who chiefly rules the changeful mind of mortals. ’ That is a fine saying and an admirable. It is for this, then, that I affirm that the possession of wealth is of most value

chinese:
这也许并非对每个人如此，但对好人是如此。不欺骗任何人，哪怕是无意的；不对人失信；不因欠神一场祭献，或欠人一笔钱，而心怀恐惧地离开，去往另一个世界——拥有财产，对做到这些帮助很大。财富也有许多其他用途。但把一项项好处相互衡量，苏格拉底，我认为对明理的人来说，这就是财富最大的用处。”
“说得好，克法洛斯。”我说。
english: not it may be to every man but to the good man. Not to cheat any man even unintentionally or play him false, not remaining in debt to a god for some sacrifice or to a man for money, so to depart in fear to that other world—to this result the possession of property contributes not a little. It has also many other uses. But, setting one thing against another, I would lay it down, Socrates, that for a man of sense this is the chief service of wealth.” “An admirable sentiment, Cephalus,” said I.

chinese: “不过，既然谈到正义，我们能不能毫无限定地说，正义就是讲真话，把从别人那里接受的东西还给他？还是说，这些行动本身有时正义，有时又不正义？譬如，我想人人都会承认：如果有人从神志清醒的朋友那里收下武器，后来那朋友发了狂，要求拿回去，那么这种情况下我们不该归还，归还的人也不是在做正义的事；同样，对一个处在这种状态的人坚持只讲真话，也不是正义的。”
english: “But speaking of this very thing, justice, are we to affirm thus without qualification that it is truth-telling and paying back what one has received from anyone, or may these very actions sometimes be just and sometimes unjust? I mean, for example, as everyone I presume would admit, if one took over weapons from a friend who was in his right mind and then the lender should go mad and demand them back, that we ought not to return them in that case and that he who did so return them would not be acting justly—nor yet would he who chose to speak nothing but the truth to one who was in that state.”

chinese:
“你说得对。”他答道。“那么，讲真话、归还所收下的东西，就不是正义的定义。”
“不，苏格拉底，这就是，”玻勒马霍斯插话说，“只要我们还相信西摩尼德斯的话。”
“好吧，”克法洛斯说，“我确实把整场讨论交给你们了，我该去照看祭事了。”
“好啊，”我说，“玻勒马霍斯不也是你所有东西的继承人吗？”
“当然。”他笑着说，同时出去参加祭礼了。
english: “You are right,” he replied. “Then this is not the definition of justice: to tell the truth and return what one has received.” “Nay, but it is, Socrates,” said Polemarchus breaking in, “if indeed we are to put any faith in Simonides.” “Very well,” said Cephalus, “indeed I make over the whole argument to you. For it is time for me to attend the sacrifices.” “Well,” said I, “is not Polemarchus the heir of everything that is yours?” “Certainly,” said he with a laugh, and at the same time went out to the sacred rites.

chinese:
“那么，你这位论证的继承人，请告诉我，你说西摩尼德斯对正义说了什么，而且说得正确？”
“把各人应得的给他，就是正义。”他答道，“我认为他说得好。”
“我得承认，”我说，“不相信西摩尼德斯并不容易，因为他是个智慧而有神灵启发的人。但他这样说究竟是什么意思，玻勒马霍斯，你无疑知道，我却不知道。他显然不是指我们刚才谈的那件事：不管是谁要求取回寄存物，哪怕他神志失常，也照样归还。然而，一个人存下的东西，在某种意义上，不正是欠着他、应当给他的吗？”
english:
“Tell me, then, you the inheritor of the argument, what it is that you affirm that Simonides says and rightly says about justice.” “That it is just,” he replied, “to render to each his due. In saying this I think he speaks well.”

“I must admit,” said I, “that it is not easy to disbelieve Simonides. For he is a wise and inspired man. But just what he may mean by this you, Polemarchus, doubtless know, but I do not. Obviously he does not mean what we were just speaking of, this return of a deposit to anyone whatsoever even if he asks it back when not in his right mind. And yet what the man deposited is due to him in a sense, is it not?”

chinese:
“是的。”
“但他在神志失常时要求取回，无论如何也不该还给他。”
“确实。”他说。“看来，西摩尼德斯说把应得之物还给人就是正义，意思一定不是这一种。”
“确实另有所指，”他答道，“因为他认为朋友对朋友所欠的是好处，不是坏处。”
“明白了，”我说，“你是说，把寄存的金子还回去，并不就算偿还了应得或所欠之物，
english: “Yes.” “But rendered to him it ought not to be by any manner of means when he demands it not being his right mind.” “True,” said he. “It is then something other than this that Simonides must, as it seems, mean by the saying that it is just to render back what is due.” “Something else in very deed,” he replied, “for he believes that friends owe it to friends to do them some good and no evil.” “I see,” said I; “you mean that he does not render what is due or owing who returns a deposit of gold

chinese:
如果归还与接受反而有害，而且归还者与接受者是朋友。你说西摩尼德斯的意思，不正是这样吗？”
“正是。”
“那么再看这一点：难道不该把敌人应得的给他吗？”
“当然应该，”他说，“要给他们应得和所欠的东西。而一个敌人欠另一个敌人的，也正是适合他的东西，那就是某种坏处。”
“那么，西摩尼德斯是以诗人的方式，给正义下了一个谜语般的定义。因为看来，他的意思
english:
if this return and the acceptance prove harmful and the returner and the recipient are friends. Isn’t that what you say Simonides means?” “Quite so.” “But how about this—should one not render to enemies what is their due?” “By all means,” he said, “what is due and owing to them, and there is due and owing from an enemy to an enemy what also is proper for him, some evil.”

“It was a riddling definition of justice, then, that Simonides gave after the manner of poets; for while his meaning,

chinese:
是正义就是把适合每个人的东西给他，却把它称作‘应得之物’。”
“不然你认为是什么呢？”他说。“天哪！”我说，“假如有人这样问他：‘西摩尼德斯，请告诉我，把什么适合而应得的东西给予什么对象的技艺，叫作医术？’你觉得他会怎样回答？”
“显然，”他说，“就是把药物、食物和饮料给予身体的技艺。”
“那么，把什么适合而应得的东西给予什么对象的技艺，又叫作烹饪呢？”
english: it seems, was that justice is rendering to each what befits him, the name that he gave to this was ‘the due.’” “What else do you suppose?” said he. “In heaven’s name!” said I, “suppose someone had questioned him thus: ‘Tell me, Simonides, the art that renders what that is due and befitting to what is called the art of medicine.’ What do you take it would have been his answer?” “Obviously,” he said, “the art that renders to bodies drugs, foods, and drinks.” “And the art that renders to what things what that is due and befitting is called the culinary art?”

chinese:
“把调味品加到肉食上。”
“好。照同样的方式，请告诉我：把什么给予什么人的技艺，才称得上正义？”
“苏格拉底，如果沿着前面的例子说，那就是把好处给予朋友、把坏处给予敌人的技艺。”
“那么，在他看来，帮助朋友、伤害敌人就是正义？”
“我想是的。”
“那么，在朋友和敌人生病时，论疾病和健康，谁最有能力帮助朋友、伤害敌人？”
“医生。”
english: “Seasoning to meats.” “Good. In the same way tell me the art that renders what to whom would be denominated justice.” “If we are to follow the previous examples, Socrates, it is that which renders benefits and harms to friends and enemies.” “To do good to friends and evil to enemies, then, is justice in his meaning?” “I think so.” “Who then is the most able when they are ill to benefit friends and harm enemies in respect to disease and health?” “The physician.”

chinese:
“遇到海上危险时，谁对航海者最有这样的能力？”
“舵手。”
“那么，正义者在什么行动、什么事务上，最能帮助朋友、伤害敌人？”
“我想是作战和结盟。”
“很好。但是，朋友玻勒马霍斯，人若没有生病，医生对他们就没有用。”
“是的。”
“对不在海上的人，舵手也一样。”
“是的。”
“我们是否也要说，对不在战争中的人，正义者没有用？”
“决不能这么说。”
“那么，即使在和平时期，正义也有用？”
english:
“And who navigators in respect of the perils of the sea?” “The pilot.” “Well then, the just man, in what action and for what work is he the most competent to benefit friends and harm enemies?” “In making war and as an ally, I should say.” “Very well. But now if they are not sick, friend Polemarchus, the physician is useless to them.” “True.” “And so to those who are not at sea the pilot.” “Yes.” “Shall we also say this that for those who are not at war the just man is useless?”

“By no means.” “There is a use then even in peace for justice?”

chinese:
“是的，有用。”
“农业也有用，不是吗？”
“是的。”
“它的用处在于取得收成？”
“是的。”
“鞋匠的技艺也一样？”
“是的。”
“我想，你会说，是为了得到鞋子。”
“当然。”
“那么，请告诉我：在和平时期，正义对什么事务、对取得什么东西有用？”
“对契约和交易有用，苏格拉底。”
“你说交易，是指共同交往、合伙，还是别的什么？”
“当然是共同交往。”
“那么，在下棋时，正义者
english: “Yes, it is useful.” “But so is agriculture, isn’t it?” “Yes.” “Namely, for the getting of a harvest?” “Yes.” “But likewise the cobbler’s art?” “Yes.” “Namely, I presume you would say, for the getting of shoes.” “Certainly.” “Then tell me, for the service and getting of what would you say that justice is useful in time of peace?” “In engagements and dealings, Socrates.” “And by dealings do you mean associations, partnerships, or something else?” “Associations, of course.” “Is it the just man,

chinese:
是更好、更有用的同伴和搭档，还是棋手？”
“棋手。”
“砌砖垒石时，正义者比建筑匠是更有用、更好的同伴吗？”
“决不是。”
“那么，哪一种合伙需要正义者胜过琴师，就像弹奏琴弦时琴师胜过正义者一样？”
“我想是钱财上的交往。”
“玻勒马霍斯，不过，倘若是使用金钱共同购买
english: then, who is a good and useful associate and partner in the placing of draughts or the draught-player?” “The player.” “And in the placing of bricks and stones is the just man a more useful and better associate than the builder?” “By no means.” “Then what is the association in which the just man is a better partner than the harpist as an harpist is better than the just man for striking the chords?” “For money-dealings, I think.” “Except, I presume, Polemarchus, for the use of money when there is occasion to buy in common

chinese:
或出售一匹马，恐怕就得例外。我想这时候该找懂马的人，不是吗？”
“看来如此。”
“再者，若买卖的是船，就该找造船匠或舵手。”
“似乎是。”
“那么，怎样共同使用金钱，正义者才是更好的合伙人？”
“当钱要寄存起来、安全保管时，苏格拉底。”
“你是说，不去使用它，只让它闲放着的时候？”
“正是。”
“那么，是在钱不被使用的时候，正义才对它有用？”
english: or sell a horse. Then, I take it, the man who knows horses, isn’t it so?” “Apparently.” “And again, if it is a vessel, the shipwright or the pilot.” “It would seem so.” “What then is the use of money in common for which a just man is the better partner?” “When it is to be deposited and kept safe, Socrates.” “You mean when it is to be put to no use but is to lie idle?” “Quite so.” “Then it is when money is useless that justice is useful in relation to it?”

chinese:
“看来是这样。”
“同样，一把镰刀要安全保管时，正义对公私双方都有用；但要使用它时，有用的就是葡萄种植者的技艺？”
“看来如此。”
“所以，你也得说，一面盾、一把琴只要收存而不使用，正义就有用；要使用时，有用的就是军事技艺和音乐。”
“必然如此。”
“其他所有东西也都一样：使用它们时，正义没有用；不使用它们时，正义倒有用？”
“看来如此。”
english: “It looks that way.” “And similarly when a scythe is to be kept safe, then justice is useful both in public and private. But when it is to be used, the vinedresser’s art is useful?” “Apparently.” “And so you will have to say that when a shield and a lyre are to be kept and put to no use, justice is useful, but when they are to be made use of, the military art and music.” “Necessarily.” “And so in all other cases, in the use of each thing, justice is useless but in its uselessness useful?” “It looks that way.”

chinese:
“那么，朋友，正义若只对不使用、闲置的东西有用，就不是什么价值很大的东西了。不过，让我们考虑这一点：在搏斗中，无论拳击还是别的情形，最善于击打、打出一拳的人，不也最善于防备打来的拳头吗？”
“当然。”
“最懂得防止疾病的人，不也最善于暗中使人染病而不被察觉吗？”
“我想是的。”
“再者，
english:
“Then, my friend, justice cannot be a thing of much worth if it is useful only for things out of use and useless. But let us consider this point. Is not the man who is most skilful to strike or inflict a blow in a fight, whether as a boxer or elsewhere, also the most wary to guard against a blow?” “Assuredly.” “Is it not also true that he who best knows how to guard against disease is also most cunning to communicate it and escape detection?” “I think so.”

“But again

chinese:
善于摸清敌人的计谋及一般行动、出其不意加以袭击的人，也正是善于保卫军队的人。”
“当然。”
“那么，一个人善于守护什么，也就善于偷窃什么？”
“似乎如此。”
“如果正义者是保管金钱的行家，也就是偷窃金钱的行家。”
“论证确实指向这个结论。”
“这样看来，正义者竟成了某种窃贼。你这种想法，大概是从荷马那里得到的。因为他欣赏奥德修斯的
english: the very same man is a good guardian of an army who is good at stealing a march upon the enemy in respect of their designs and proceedings generally.” “Certainly.” “Of whatsoever, then, anyone is a skilful guardian, of that he is also a skilful thief?” “It seems so.” “If then the just man is an expert in guarding money he is an expert in stealing it.” “The argument certainly points that way.” “A kind of thief then the just man it seems has turned out to be, and it is likely that you acquired this idea from Homer. For he regards with complacency Autolycus,

chinese:
外祖父奥托吕科斯，说他‘偷窃和发假誓的天赋超过所有人’。（《奥德赛》19.395）因此，照你、荷马和西摩尼德斯的说法，正义似乎就是某种偷窃，只不过要加上一个限定：为了帮助朋友、伤害敌人。你的意思不就是这个吗？”
“不，凭宙斯起誓！”他答道，“我已经不知道自己原先是什么意思了。不过，这一点我仍然相信：正义帮助朋友，伤害敌人。”
english: the maternal uncle of Odysseus, and says ‘he was gifted beyond all men in thievery and perjury.’ So justice, according to you and Homer and Simonides, seems to be a kind of stealing, with the qualification that it is for the benefit of friends and the harm of enemies. Isn’t that what you meant?” “No, by Zeus,” he replied. “I no longer know what I did mean. Yet this I still believe, that justice benefits friends and harms enemies.”

chinese:
“我可以问问吗？你所谓朋友，是一个人认为值得亲近的人，还是实际上值得亲近的人，哪怕看起来不是？敌人也同样区分吗？”
“人们大概会爱他们认为好的人，厌恶他们认为坏的人。”他说。
“人在这件事上不会出错吗？以为许多人是好人，其实不是；反过来也一样。”
“会出错。”
“那么，对那些判断错误的人来说，好人是敌人，坏人是朋友？”
“当然。”
“可是这样一来，对他们而言，帮助坏人、伤害好人也仍是正义的吗？”
english: “May I ask whether by friends you mean those who seem to a man to be worthy or those who really are so, even if they do not seem, and similarly of enemies?” “It is likely,” he said, “that men will love those whom they suppose to be good and dislike those whom they deem bad.” “Do not men make mistakes in this matter so that many seem good to them who are not and the reverse?” “They do.” “For those, then, who thus err the good are their enemies and the bad their friends?” “Certainly.” “But all the same is then just for them to benefit the bad and injure the good?”

chinese:
“看来是这样。”
“不过，好人是正义的，不会做不正义的事。”
“是的。”
“那么，根据你的论证，亏待不做不正义之事的人，反倒是正义。”
“不，不，苏格拉底，”他说，“这论证不能是对的。”
“那么，”我说，“伤害不正义者、帮助正义者，才是正义。”
“这个结论似乎比刚才那个好。”
“那么，玻勒马霍斯，对许多判断错了人的人来说，结果就会是：伤害自己的朋友是正义的，
english: “It would seem so.” “But again the good are just and incapable of injustice.” “True.” “On your reasoning then it is just to wrong those who do no injustice.” “Nay, nay, Socrates,” he said, “the reasoning can’t be right.” “Then,” said I, “it is just to harm the unjust and benefit the just.” “That seems a better conclusion than the other.” “It will work out, then, for many, Polemarchus, who have misjudged men that it is just to harm their friends,

chinese:
因为他们的朋友是坏人；帮助自己的敌人也是正义的，因为那些敌人是好人。这样一来，我们就会说出与我们所认定的西摩尼德斯之意完全相反的话。”
“确实如此，”他说，“结果是这样。不过，让我们改变立足点吧，因为看来我们对朋友和敌人的理解出了错。”
“哪一种理解，玻勒马霍斯？”
“把我们看来是好人的，当成朋友。”
“那么现在要改成怎样？”我问。“看起来是好人，而且实际也是好人的，才是朋友；至于看起来
english:
for they have got bad ones, and to benefit their enemies, for they are good. And so we shall find ourselves saying the very opposite of what we affirmed Simonides to mean.” “Most certainly,” he said, “it does work out so. But let us change our ground; for it looks as if we were wrong in the notion we took up about the friend and the enemy.” “What notion, Polemarchus?” “That the man who seems to us good is the friend.” “And to what shall we change it now?” said I.

“That the man who both seems and is good is the friend, but that he who seems

chinese:
是好人，实际却不是的，那人只是看起来是朋友，并不真是朋友。敌人也应该作同样的理解。”
“那么，照这种看法，朋友似乎就是好人，坏人就是敌人。”
“是的。”
“所以，你要我们给从前对正义者的理解加上一项限定。从前我们说，帮助朋友、伤害敌人是正义；如今则要加上：朋友若是好人，帮助他才正义；敌人若是坏人，伤害他才正义？”
english: but is not really so seems but is not really the friend. And there will be the same assumption about the enemy.” “Then on this view it appears the friend will be the good man and the bad the enemy.” “Yes.” “So you would have us qualify our former notion of the just man by an addition. We then said it was just to do good to a friend and evil to an enemy, but now we are to add that it is just to benefit the friend if he is good and harm the enemy if he is bad?”

chinese:
“当然，”他说，“我想这样说就对了。”
“那么，”我说，“一个好人应当伤害任何人吗？”
“当然应当，”他答道，“一个人应该伤害那些既坏、又是自己敌人的人。”
“马受到伤害，会变得更好，还是更坏？”
“更坏。”
“是狗的优良能力或德性变坏，还是马的？”
“马的。”
“那么，狗受到伤害，不也是狗的德性变坏，而不是马的德性变坏吗？”
“必然如此。”
english:
“By all means,” he said, “that, I think, would be the right way to put it.”

“Is it then,” said I, “the part of a good man to harm anybody whatsoever?” “Certainly it is,” he replied; “a man ought to harm those who are both bad and his enemies.” “When horses are harmed does it make them better or worse?” “Worse.” “In respect of the excellence or virtue of dogs or that of horses?” “Of horses.” “And do not also dogs when harmed become worse in respect of canine and not of equine virtue?” “Necessarily.”

chinese:
“朋友，说到人，我们不也必须说，人受到伤害，是在人特有的优良品质或德性上变坏吗？”
“当然。”
“正义不正是人特有的德性吗？”
“这也必须承认。”
“那么，朋友，也必须承认，受到伤害的人会变得更加不正义。”
“看来如此。”
“那么，乐师会凭音乐技艺，使人不懂音乐吗？”
“不可能。”
“骑手会凭骑术，使人不善于驾驭马吗？”
“不会。”
“那么，正义者会凭正义使人不正义，
english: “And men, my dear fellow, must we not say that when they are harmed it is in respect of the distinctive excellence or virtue of man that they become worse?” “Assuredly.” “And is not justice the specific virtue of man?” “That too must be granted.” “Then it must also be admitted, my friend, that men who are harmed become more unjust.” “It seems so.” “Do musicians then make men unmusical by the art of music?” “Impossible.” “Well, do horsemen by horsemanship unfit men for dealing with horses?” “No.” “By justice then do the just make men unjust,

chinese:
或者总而言之，好人会凭德性使人变坏吗？”
“不，那不可能。”
“我想，使东西变冷不是热的作用，而是热的反面的作用。”
“是的。”
“使东西变湿也不是干燥的作用，而是它的反面的作用。”
“当然。”
“同样，造成伤害也不是好的作用，而是它的反面的作用。”
“看来如此。”
“但正义者是好的？”
“当然。”
“那么，玻勒马霍斯，伤害朋友或任何别人，都不是正义者的作用，而是与他相反的人的作用。”
“我认为你说得完全正确，
english: or in sum do the good by virtue make men bad?” “Nay, it is impossible.” “It is not, I take it, the function of heat to chill but of its opposite.” “Yes.” “Nor of dryness to moisten but of its opposite.” “Assuredly.” “Nor yet of the good to harm but of its opposite.” “So it appears.” “But the just man is good?” “Certainly.” “It is not then the function of the just man, Polemarchus, to harm either friend or anyone else, but of his opposite.” “I think you are altogether right,

chinese:
苏格拉底。”
“那么，如果有人断言，把各人应得的给他就是正义，他所指的是正义者欠敌人的为损害与伤害，欠朋友的为好处，那么说这话的人就不是真正的智者。因为他的意思不真实：我们已经弄清，在任何情况下伤害任何人，都不是正义。”
“我承认。”他说。“那么，”我说，“如果有人说西摩尼德斯、比阿斯、庇塔库斯，或任何别的智慧而有福的人，说过这种话，你我就一起拿起武器反对他。”
“就我而言，”他说，“我准备好与你并肩作战了。”
english: Socrates.” “If, then, anyone affirms that it is just to render to each his due and he means by this, that injury and harm is what is due to his enemies from the just man and benefits to his friends, he was no truly wise man who said it. For what he meant was not true. For it has been made clear to us that in no case is it just to harm anyone.” “I concede it,” he said. “We will take up arms against him, then,” said I, “you and I together, if anyone affirms that either Simonides or Bias or Pittacus or any other of the wise and blessed said such a thing.” “I, for my part,” he said, “am ready to join in the battle with you.”

chinese:
“你知道吗，”我说，“我认为‘帮助朋友、伤害敌人是正义’这话，是谁说的？”
“谁？”他说。“我想是佩里安德罗斯、佩尔狄卡斯、薛西斯，或底比斯的伊斯墨尼阿斯，或其他某个自以为很有权势的富人说的。”
“太对了。”他回答。“很好，”我说，“既然已经明白，这也不是正义和正义之事，那么我们还能说正义是什么呢？”
english: “Do you know,” said I, “to whom I think the saying belongs—this statement that it is just to benefit friends and harm enemies?” “To whom?” he said. “I think it was the saying of Periander or Perdiccas or Xerxes or Ismenias the Theban or some other rich man who had great power in his own conceit.” “That is most true,” he replied. “Very well,” said I, “since it has been made clear that this too is not justice and the just, what else is there that we might say justice to be?”

chinese: 我们谈话时，色拉叙马霍斯已经几次想插进来，夺过话头，只是被坐在他旁边、想把论证听完的人拦住了。可我说完这话，谈话停顿下来，他再也忍不住沉默。他像一头猛兽，绷起身子向我们扑来，仿佛要把我们撕成碎片。我和玻勒马霍斯受惊，慌忙向两边退开。他在我们中间大声吼道：
english: Now Thrasymachus, even while we were conversing, had been trying several times to break in and lay hold of the discussion but he was restrained by those who sat by him who wished to hear the argument out. But when we came to a pause after I had said this, he couldn’t any longer hold his peace. But gathering himself up like a wild beast he hurled himself upon us as if he would tear us to pieces. And Polemarchus and I were frightened and fluttered apart, and he bawled out into our midst,

chinese: “你们说的这些都是什么胡话？你们这些傻瓜，为什么彼此迁就、互相退让？苏格拉底，你若真想知道正义是什么，就不要只会提问，也不要因驳倒别人给出的任何答案而自鸣得意——你的聪明已经看出，提问比回答容易——你该亲自回答，说出
english: “What balderdash is this that you have been talking, and why do you Simple Simons truckle and give way to one another? But if you really wish, Socrates, to know what the just is, don’t merely ask questions or plume yourself upon controverting any answer that anyone gives—since your acumen has perceived that it is easier to ask questions than to answer them, but do you yourself answer and tell

chinese: 你认为正义是什么。别告诉我正义就是应该做的，或有益的、有利的、获益的、有好处的，而要清清楚楚、准确地说出你的意思。我不接受你那些废话！”听了他的话，我十分惊惶，望着他，满心恐惧。我相信，假如不是我先看见他，而是他先看见我，我准会说不出话。可是当时，正当他开始对论证的进展恼怒时，
english: what you say the just is. And don’t you be telling me that it is that which ought to be, or the beneficial or the profitable or the gainful or the advantageous, but express clearly and precisely whatever you say. For I won’t take from you any such drivel as that!” And I, when I heard him, was dismayed, and looking upon him was filled with fear, and I believe that if I had not looked at him before he did at me I should have lost my voice. But as it is, at the very moment when he began to be exasperated by the course of the argument

chinese: 我先瞥见了他，因此还能够回答，便带着轻微的颤抖说：“色拉叙马霍斯，不要苛责我们。如果我和朋友在考察问题时犯了错误，你要相信，我们不是故意的。你一定不能认为：假如我们找的是金子，就决不会故意相互迁就、在寻找中让步，以至于毁掉找到金子的机会；而现在寻找的是正义，是比许多纯金更宝贵的东西，我们反而会愚蠢地彼此退让，不认真竭力把它找出来。朋友，你一定不要这样想。可是你看，问题在于我们没有这种能力。所以，与其责怪我们，我们更有理由得到的，
english:
I glanced at him first, so that I became capable of answering him and said with a light tremor: “Thrasymachus, don’t be harsh with us. If I and my friend have made mistakes in the consideration of the question, rest assured that it is unwillingly that we err. For you surely must not suppose that while if our quest were for gold we would never willingly truckle to one another and make concessions in the search and so spoil our chances of finding it, yet that when we are searching for justice, a thing more precious than much fine gold, we should then be so foolish as to give way to one another and not rather do our serious best to have it discovered.”

You surely must not suppose that, my friend. But you see it is our lack of ability that is at fault. It is pity then that we should far more reasonably receive

chinese:
是像你这样聪明的人的怜悯，而非苛责。”
他听了，放声大笑，带着讥讽说：“诸神啊！这就是大家熟悉的苏格拉底式装糊涂。我早知道，也早预言过，一轮到你回答，你就会推辞、掩饰，什么都肯做，就是不肯回答别人问你的任何问题。”
“这是因为你很聪明，色拉叙马霍斯。所以你很清楚，假如你问一个人，怎样组成十二，
english:
from clever fellows like you than severity.”

And he on hearing this gave a great guffaw and laughed sardonically and said, “Ye gods! here we have the well-known irony of Socrates, and I knew it and predicted that when it came to replying you would refuse and dissemble and do anything rather than answer any question that anyone asked you.” “That’s because you are wise, Thrasymachus, and so you knew very well that if you asked a man how many are twelve,

chinese: 提问时又警告他：‘老兄，别告诉我十二是二乘六、三乘四、六乘二或四乘三，我不接受你用这类废话作答。’我想，你显然知道，用这种方式发问，没有人能回答。假如那人对你说：‘色拉叙马霍斯，你是什么意思？任何一个被禁止的答案我都不能说吗？你的意思是，即使实际答案正是其中一个，也不许说，而必须说与事实不同的话，
english: and in putting the question warned him: don’t you be telling me, fellow, that twelve is twice six or three times four or six times two or four times three, for I won’t accept any such drivel as that from you as an answer—it was obvious I fancy to you that no one could give an answer to a question framed in that fashion. Suppose he had said to you, ‘Thrasymachus, what do you mean? Am I not to give any of the prohibited answers, not even, do you mean to say, if the thing really is one of these, but must I say something different from the truth,

chinese:
还是别的意思？’你会怎样回答他？”
“哼！”他说，“这两种情况还真像啊！”
“没有什么不容许它们相像，”我说，“即使承认它们并不相像，只要被问的人觉得相像，你以为，无论我们禁止不禁止，他就会不照自己的看法回答吗？”
“那么，”他说，“你也准备这样做？你要给出一个已经被禁止的答案？”
“如果经过思考，那就是我的看法，”我说，“我这样回答，也没什么奇怪。”
“那么，”
english: or what do you mean?’ What would have been your answer to him?” “Humph!” said he, “how very like the two cases are!” “There is nothing to prevent,” said I; “yet even granted that they are not alike, yet if it appears to the person asked the question that they are alike, do you suppose that he will any the less answer what appears to him, whether we forbid him or whether we don’t?” “Is that, then,” said he, “what you are going to do? Are you going to give one of the forbidden answers?” “I shouldn’t be surprised,” I said, “if on reflection that would be my view.” “What then,”

chinese:
他说，“假如我向你提出一个关于正义的答案，和这些全都不同，而且更好，你认为自己该受什么罚？”
“除了无知者理应承受的，还能是什么？”我说，“我想，他应该向知道的人学习。所以，我提议自己承受这个。”
“我喜欢你这份天真，”他说，“但除了‘学习’，你还得交一笔罚金。”
“等我有钱，就交。”我说。“钱在这儿，”格劳孔说，“色拉叙马霍斯，如果拦住你的只是钱，就讲下去吧。我们大家会替苏格拉底凑钱。”
“噢，当然了，”
english: he said, “if I show you another answer about justice differing from all these, a better one—what penalty do you think you deserve?” “Why, what else,” said I, “than that which it befits anyone who is ignorant to suffer? It befits him, I presume, to learn from the one who does know. That then is what I propose that I should suffer.” “I like your simplicity,” said he; “but in addition to ‘learning’you must pay a fine of money.” “Well, I will when I have got it,” I said. “It is there,” said Glaucon: “if money is all that stands in the way, Thrasymachus, go on with your speech. We will all contribute for Socrates.” “Oh yes, of course,”

chinese:
他说，“好让苏格拉底照他一贯的办法，自己设法逃避回答，却盘问别人，反驳别人的答复。”
“可是，朋友，”我说，“一个人首先不知道，也不声称知道；其次，即使对此有一点看法，又被一个有分量的人告诫，不能把自己的任何猜想拿来作答，他还能怎样回答呢？
english:
said he, “so that Socrates may contrive, as he always does, to evade answering himself but may cross-examine the other man and refute his replies.”

“Why, how,” I said, “my dear fellow, could anybody answer if in the first place he did not know and did not even profess to know, and secondly even if he had some notion of the matter, he had been told by a man of weight that he mustn’t give any of his suppositions as an answer?

chinese:
不，还是由你来讲更合理。因为你确实声称自己知道，而且能够说明。别再坚持了，帮我这个忙，作个回答，也别吝惜你的智慧，教教这里的格劳孔和我们其他人吧。”
我这样说了以后，格劳孔和其他人也劝他不要坚持。很明显，色拉叙马霍斯急于发言，好让自己赢得赞誉，因为他相信，对我们的问题，他有一个极好的答案。但他仍然推辞，装作非要我回答不可。终于，他让步了，说道：
english:
Nay, it is more reasonable that you should be the speaker. For you do affirm that you know and are able to tell. Don’t be obstinate, but do me the favor to reply and don’t be chary of your wisdom, and instruct Glaucon here and the rest of us.”

When I had spoken thus Glaucon and the others urged him not to be obstinate. It was quite plain that Thrasymachus was eager to speak in order that he might do himself credit, since he believed that he had a most excellent answer to our question. But he demurred and pretended to make a point of my being the respondent. Finally he gave way and then said,

chinese:
“这就是苏格拉底的智慧：自己不肯教人，却到处向别人学习，甚至连谢意也不表示。”
“色拉叙马霍斯，”我说，“你说我向别人学习，这一点说得对。但说我不表示谢意，就错了。我尽自己的能力答谢，而我的能力只够给予称赞，因为我没有钱。不过，你一作回答，就马上会明白：对那些在我看来讲得好的人，我是多么乐意称赞。
english: “Here you have the wisdom of Socrates, to refuse himself to teach, but go about and learn from others and not even pay thanks therefor.” “That I learn from others,” I said, “you said truly, Thrasymachus. But in saying that I do not pay thanks you are mistaken. I pay as much as I am able. And I am able only to bestow praise. For money I lack. But that I praise right willingly those who appear to speak well you will well know forthwith as soon as you have given your answer.

chinese:
因为我想，你会讲得很好。”
“那就听着，仔细听，”他说，“我主张，正义不是别的，就是强者的利益。怎么样，你为什么不喝彩？不，你什么都肯做，唯独不肯这样。”
“只要让我先懂得你的意思，”我说，“因为我还没领会。你主张正义就是强者的利益，这究竟是什么意思？我想，你不是要说，全力角斗选手玻吕达马斯比我们强壮，牛肉对他有好处，
english: For I think that you will speak well.” “Hearken and hear then,” said he. “I affirm that the just is nothing else than the advantage of the stronger. Well, why don’t you applaud? Nay, you’ll do anything but that.” “Provided only I first understand your meaning,” said I; “for I don’t yet apprehend it. The advantage of the stronger is what you affirm the just to be. But what in the world do you mean by this? I presume you don’t intend to affirm this, that if Polydamas the pancratiast is stronger than we are and the flesh of beeves is advantageous for him,

chinese:
对他的身体有益，所以这种食物对于比他弱的我们，也同样有益而且正义。”
“苏格拉底，你是个丑角，专挑最不利于我论点的意思来理解。”
“决不是，朋友，”我说，“我只是要你把意思说明白些。”
“那么，你不知道吗，”他说，“有些城邦由僭主统治，有些实行民主，有些实行贵族统治？”
“当然知道。”
“在每一种城邦里，有力量、掌握支配地位的，不都是统治的一方吗？”
“当然。”
english: for his body, this viand is also for us who are weaker than he both advantageous and just.” “You’re a buffoon, Socrates, and take my statement in the most detrimental sense.” “Not at all, my dear fellow” said I; “I only want you to make your meaning plainer.” “Don’t you know then,” said he, “that some cities are governed by tyrants, in others democracy rules, in others aristocracy?” “Assuredly.” “And is not this the thing that is strong and has the mastery in each—the ruling party?” “Certainly.”

chinese: “每一种政体都着眼于自己的利益制定法律：民主政体制定民主的法律，僭主政体制定专制的法律，其他政体也同样。它们这样立法，便宣布对被统治者而言，正义就是对它们——对统治者——有利的事；违背这些法律的人，它们就作为违法者、不正义者加以惩罚。所以，先生，在我看来，所有城邦共有的同一正义原则，
english:
“And each form of government enacts the laws with a view to its own advantage, a democracy democratic laws and tyranny autocratic and the others likewise, and by so legislating they proclaim that the just for their subjects is that which is for their—the rulers’—advantage and the man who deviates from this law they chastise as a law-breaker and a wrongdoer.”

This, then, my good sir, is what I understand as the identical principle of justice that obtains in all states —

chinese:
就是现存统治者的利益。我想，你会承认，统治者掌握权力，而且强大。因此，推理正确，结果便是：正义在任何地方都是同一回事，即强者的利益。”
“现在，”我说，“我懂得你的意思了，但它是否真实，我还得设法弄明白。色拉叙马霍斯，对于正义是什么，你的回答也是‘有利之事’，尽管你禁止我这样答。
english: the advantage of the established government. This I presume you will admit holds power and is strong, so that, if one reasons rightly, it works out that the just is the same thing everywhere, the advantage of the stronger.” “Now,” said I, “I have learned your meaning, but whether it is true or not I have to try to learn. The advantageous, then, is also your reply, Thrasymachus, to the question, what is the just—though you forbade me to give that answer.

chinese:
只是你又加上了‘强者的’。”
“你也许觉得这是个微不足道的补充。”他说。“它是不是一个重大的补充，也还不清楚；但我们必须考察你的说法是否真实，这一点很清楚。因为我也承认，正义是某种有利之事，但你要作一个补充，断言它是强者的利益，而我不声称知道，所以我们必须继续考察。”
“那就考察吧。”他说。
“我会的，”我说，“那么请告诉我：你也主张服从统治者是正义的，不是吗？”
english:
But you add thereto that of the stronger.” “A trifling addition perhaps you think it,” he said. “It is not yet clear whether it is a big one either; but that we must inquire whether what you say is true, is clear. For since I too admit that the just is something that is of advantage—but you are for making an addition and affirm it to be the advantage of the stronger, while I don’t profess to know, we must pursue the inquiry.” “Inquire away,” he said.

“I will do so,” said I. “Tell me, then; you affirm also, do you not, that obedience to rulers is just?”

chinese:
“是的。”
“我可以问问吗？各个城邦的统治者绝不会犯错，还是有时也会犯错？”
“他们当然可能犯错。”他说。
“那么，他们尝试立法时，有些法律定得对，有些定得不对，不是吗？”
“我想是的。”
“这里说对，是指有利于他们；说不对，是指不利于他们。你的意思是这样吗？”
“是这样。”
“但无论他们制定什么，被统治者都必须执行，而且这样做就是正义？”
“当然。”
english: “I do.” “May I ask whether the rulers in the various states are infallible or capable sometimes of error?” “Surely,” he said, “they are liable to err.” “Then in their attempts at legislation they enact some laws rightly and some not rightly, do they not?” “So I suppose.” “And by rightly we are to understand for their advantage, and by wrongly to their disadvantage? Do you mean that or not?” “That.” “But whatever they enact must be performed by their subjects and is justice?” “Of course.”

chinese:
“那么，照你的理论，正义不只是做对强者有利的事，也包括相反的、对他不利的事。”
“你说什么？”他回答。“我想，正是你自己说的话。我们再仔细看看。我们不是已经同意，统治者向被统治者下命令时，有时会误判自己的利益；而统治者无论命令什么，被统治者执行就是正义吗？这不是已经承认了吗？”
“我想承认过。”他答道。
english: “Then on your theory it is just not only to do what is the advantage of the stronger but also the opposite, what is not to his advantage.” “What’s that you’re saying?” he replied. “What you yourself are saying, I think. Let us consider it more closely. Have we not agreed that the rulers in giving orders to the ruled sometimes mistake their own advantage, and that whatever the rulers enjoin is just for the subjects to perform? Was not that admitted?” “I think it was,” he replied.

chinese: “那么，”我说，“你就得认为，自己已经承认，做不利于统治者、也就是不利于强者的事，也是正义：当统治者无意中命令别人去做对自己有害的事，而你又断言，别人照他命令的去做就是正义时，便是这样。最智慧的色拉叙马霍斯，这岂不是必然推出一个结论：正义恰恰就是做与你所说的相反的事？因为在这种情况下，弱者受命去做的，无疑正是不利于强者、优越者的事。”
english: “Then you will have to think,” I said, “that to do what is disadvantageous to the rulers and the stronger has been admitted by you to be just in the case when the rulers unwittingly enjoin what is bad for themselves, while you affirm that it is just for the others to do what they enjoined. In that way does not this conclusion inevitably follow, my most sapient Thrasymachus, that it is just to do the very opposite of what you say? For it is in that case surely the disadvantage of the stronger or superior that the inferior are commanded to perform.”

chinese:
“是啊，凭宙斯起誓，苏格拉底，”玻勒马霍斯说，“没有比这更确凿的了。”
“当然，”克勒托丰插话说，“如果由你替他作证。”
“还需要什么证人？”玻勒马霍斯说，“色拉叙马霍斯自己承认，统治者有时命令别人做对自己有害的事，却仍说被统治者这样做是正义。”
“玻勒马霍斯，那是因为色拉叙马霍斯提出，服从统治者的命令是正义。”
“是的，克勒托丰，但他也提出，强者的利益就是正义。
english: “Yes, by Zeus, Socrates,” said Polemarchus, “nothing could be more conclusive.” “Of course,” said Cleitophon, breaking in, “if you are his witness.” “What need is there of a witness?” Polemarchus said. “Thrasymachus himself admits that the rulers sometimes enjoin what is evil for themselves and yet says that it is just for the subjects to do this.” “That, Polemarchus, is because Thrasymachus laid it down that it is just to obey the orders of the rulers.” “Yes, Cleitophon, but he also took the position that the advantage of the stronger is just.

chinese:
提出这两个前提以后，他又承认，强者有时命令弱者、也就是他们的被统治者，去做不利于统治者的事。根据这些承认，正义就不只是强者的利益，也同样是它的反面。”
“噢，”克勒托丰说，“他所说的强者利益，是强者认为有利于自己的事。弱者必须做的是这个；他的主张是，这才是正义。”
“他并不是这样说的。”
english: And after these two assumptions he again admitted that the stronger sometimes bid the inferior and their subjects do what is to the disadvantage of the rulers. And from these admissions the just would no more be the advantage of the stronger than the contrary.” “O well,” said Cleitophon, “by the advantage of the superior he meant what the superior supposed to be for his advantage. This was what the inferior had to do, and that this is the just was his position.” “That isn’t what he said,”

chinese:
玻勒马霍斯答道。“不要紧，玻勒马霍斯，”我说，“如果色拉叙马霍斯现在是这个意思，我们就按照这个意思理解他。

“那么，色拉叙马霍斯，请告诉我，你原本想说的是：正义就是强者看来有利于自己的事，不管实际上是否有利？我们可以说，这是你的意思吗？”
“完全不是，”他说，“你以为，一个人犯错时，我还把犯错的他叫作强者吗？”
“我确实以为你是这个意思，”我回答，“因为你同意，统治者并非绝不犯错，有时也会出错。”
english:
replied Polemarchus. “Never mind, Polemarchus,” said I, “but if that is Thrasymachus’s present meaning, let us take it from him in that sense.

So tell me, Thrasymachus, was this what you intended to say, that the just is the advantage of the superior as it appears to the superior whether it really is or not? Are we to say this was your meaning?” “Not in the least,” he said. “Do you suppose that I call one who is in error a superior when he errs?” “I certainly did suppose that you meant that,” I replied, “when you agreed that rulers are not infallible but sometimes make mistakes.”

chinese: “苏格拉底，那是因为你的论证像个讼棍。拿最近的例子说：一个人在处理病人的事上出错，你会就他的错误，称他为医生吗？一个人在计算时出错，你会在他出错时，就这个错误，称他为计算者吗？然而，我们照字面说话时确实这样说：医生错了，计算者错了，教师错了。但我认为，实情是这些人中的每一个，
english: “That is because you argue like a pettifogger, Socrates. Why, to take the nearest example, do you call one who is mistaken about the sick a physician in respect of his mistake or one who goes wrong in a calculation a calculator when he goes wrong and in respect of this error? Yet that is what we say literally—we say that the physician erred and the calculator and the schoolmaster. But the truth, I take it, is, that each of these

chinese: 只要他还是我们所称呼的那种人，就决不会出错；所以，既然你如此拘泥于精确，那么精确地说，没有一个有技艺的人会出错。一个人出错，是因为他的知识离开了他；也就是在他不再是技艺者的时候。因此，技艺者、智者或统治者，在他确实作为统治者的时候，不会犯错，尽管人人都会使用医生犯错、统治者出错这样的说法。那么，你必须按这种宽松的说法，理解我刚才给你的回答。但最准确的说法是另一种：统治者，
english:
in so far as he is that which we entitle him never errs; so that, speaking precisely, since you are such a stickler for precision, no craftsman errs. For it is when his knowledge abandons him that he who goes wrong goes wrong—when he is not a craftsman. So that no craftsman, wise man, or ruler makes a mistake then when he is a ruler, though everybody would use the expression that the physician made a mistake and the ruler erred.”

It is in this loose way of speaking, then, that you must take the answer I gave you a little while ago. But the most precise statement is that other, that the ruler

chinese:
就其作为统治者而言，并不犯错；既然不犯错，他就制定最有利于自己的规定，而被统治者必须照做。所以，正如我一开始的意思，我说正义就是做有利于强者的事。”
“那么，色拉叙马霍斯，”我说，“在你看来，我的论证方式像个讼棍？”
“正是。”他说。“你认为，我问那个问题，是蓄意找你的麻烦，想用不公平的办法胜过你？”
“不是认为，是知道，”他说，“而且你从中得不到什么，因为你偷偷摸摸也赢不了我；
english:
in so far forth as ruler does not err, and not erring he enacts what is best for himself, and this the subject must do, so that, even as I meant from the start, I say the just is to do what is for the advantage of the stronger.”

“So then, Thrasymachus,” said I, “my manner of argument seems to you pettifogging?” “It does,” he said. “You think, do you, that it was with malice aforethought and trying to get the better of you unfairly that I asked that question?” “I don’t think it, I know it,” he said, “and you won’t make anything by it, for you won’t get the better of me by stealth and ,

chinese:
若不能偷袭，正面辩论你又没有力量击败我。”
“好心人，”我说，“我连试都不会试。不过，为了不让我们之间再发生这类事情，请明确一下你在什么意义上使用统治者、强者这些词。你指的是通常所谓的统治者，还是刚才对我说的严格意义上的统治者？也就是作为强者，他的利益是弱者应当正义地为之行动的目标？”
“我指的是最严格意义上的统治者，”他说，“现在，你有本事，就拿你的吹毛求疵和讼棍伎俩来反对这点吧。
english: failing stealth, you are not of the force to beat me in debate.” “Bless your soul,” said I, “I wouldn’t even attempt such a thing. But that nothing of the sort may spring up between us again, define in which sense you take the ruler and stronger. Do you mean the so-called ruler or that ruler in the precise sense of whom you were just now telling us, and for whose advantage as being the superior it will be just for the inferior to act?” “I mean the ruler in the very most precise sense of the word,” he said. “Now bring on against this your cavils and your shyster’s tricks if you are able.

chinese:
我不求你手下留情。不过，你会发现自己做不到。”
“怎么，”我说，“你以为我疯到会去捋狮子的胡须，还向色拉叙马霍斯耍讼棍的伎俩吗？”
“你刚才就试过，”他说，“尽管你只是个微不足道的家伙。”
“这类话说得有些过头了，”我说，“不过，请告诉我：你刚才说的那个严格意义上的医生，是挣钱、收取诊金的人，还是医治病人的人？请记住，要说真正的医生。”
“医治病人的人。”他回答。“那么，真正称得上舵手的人，是水手的统领，还是一名水手？”
english: I ask no quarter. But you’ll find yourself unable.” “Why, do you suppose,” I said, “that I am so mad to try to try to beard a lion and try the pettifogger on Thrasymachus?” “You did try it just now,” he said, “paltry fellow though you be.” “Something too much of this sort of thing,” said I. “But tell me, your physician in the precise sense of whom you were just now speaking, is he a moneymaker, an earner of fees, or a healer of the sick? And remember to speak of the physician who is really such.” “A healer of the sick,” he replied. “And what of the lot—the pilot rightly so called—is he a ruler of sailors or a sailor?”

chinese:
“水手的统领。”
“我想，我们不必把他实际上也在船上航行这件事算进来，也不能因此把他叫作水手。因为他之所以被称作舵手，不在于航行本身，而在于他的技艺和对水手的统领。”
“是的。”他说。“那么，他们各自不都有某种对自己有利的东西吗？”
“正是。”
“而且，”我说，“技艺天然存在的目的，不正是发现并提供对各自对象有利的东西吗？”
“是的，正为此。”
“那么，对每一种技艺来说，除了尽可能完善，还有别的利益吗？”
english: “A ruler of sailors.” “We don’t, I fancy, have to take into account the fact that he actually sails in the ship, nor is he to be denominated a sailor. For it is not in respect of his sailing that he is called a pilot but in respect of his art and his ruling of the sailors.” “True,” he said. “Then for each of them is there not a something that is for his advantage?” “Quite so.” “And is it not also true,” said I, “that the art naturally exists for this, to discover and provide for each his advantage?” “Yes, for this.” “Is there, then, for each of the arts any other advantage than to be perfect as possible?”

chinese:
“你这个问题是什么意思？”
“就好像，”我说，“你问我，身体只要是身体就足够了，还是另有需要，我会回答：‘当然另有需要。医术之所以被发明，正因为身体有缺陷，而有缺陷并不令人满意。因此，为身体提供有益的东西，就是这门技艺被创设的目的。’你认为这样回答正确吗？”
english: “What do you mean by that question?” “Just as if,” I said, “you should ask me whether it is enough for the body to be the body or whether it stands in need of something else, I would reply, ‘By all means it stands in need. That is the reason why the art of medicine has now been invented, because the body is defective and such defect is unsatisfactory. To provide for this, then, what is advantageous, that is the end for which the art was devised.’ Do you think that would be a correct answer, or not?”

chinese: “正确。”他说。“那么再看：医术本身有缺陷或不足吗？别的技艺是否也需要某种德性、品质或优良之处，就像眼睛需要视力、耳朵需要听力，因此需要某门技艺来照管它们，考虑并提供有助于实现这些功能的东西？也就是说，技艺本身是否存在某种缺陷，每门技艺都需要另一门技艺考虑它的利益，而那门负责考虑的技艺又需要另一门，如此无穷延续？还是技艺会照顾自己的利益？
english: “Correct,” he said. “But how about this? Is the medical art itself defective or faulty, or has any other art any need of some virtue, quality, or excellence—as the eyes of vision, the ears of hearing, and for this reason is there need of some art over them that will consider and provide what is advantageous for these very ends—does there exist in the art itself some defect and does each art require another art to consider its advantage and is there need of still another for the considering art and so on ad infinitum, or will the art look out for its own advantage?

chinese:
或者，实情是：它既不需要自己，也不需要另一门技艺来考虑它的利益、弥补它的不足？因为任何技艺本身都不含有缺陷或错误。技艺所应该寻求的，也只是它的对象的利益，而不是别的东西的利益。只要每门技艺精确而完整地是它本身，技艺自身就不受损害、不掺杂坏处，而是正确的。请按照这种精确的用法考虑：是不是这样？”
“看来是这样。”他说。“那么，医术，”我说，
english: Or is it a fact that it needs neither itself nor another art to consider its advantage and provide against its deficiency? For there is no defect or error at all that dwells in any art. Nor does it befit an art to seek the advantage of anything else than that of its object. But the art itself is free from all harm and admixture of evil, and is right so long as each art is precisely and entirely that which it is. And consider the matter in that precise way of speaking. Is it so or not?” “It appears to be so,” he said. “Then medicine,” said I,

chinese:
“考虑的不是医术的利益，而是身体的利益？”
“是的。”
“骑术考虑的也不是骑术的利益，而是马的利益。其他技艺也都不照顾自身——因为自身并无这种需要——而是照顾其对象的利益。”
“似乎如此。”他回答。“可是，色拉叙马霍斯，技艺确实统领自己的对象，比自己的对象更强。”他很勉强地承认了。“那么，没有一门技艺考虑或命令的是强者的利益；每一门技艺考虑和命令的，都是弱者的利益，
english: “does not consider the advantage of medicine but of the body?” “Yes.” “Nor horsemanship of horsemanship but of horses, nor does any other art look out for itself—for it has no need—but for that of which it is the art.” “So it seems,” he replied. “But surely, Thrasymachus, the arts do hold rule and are stronger than that of which they are the arts.” He conceded this but it went very hard. “Then no art considers or enjoins the advantage of the stronger but every art that of the weaker

chinese: 也就是受它统领的对象的利益。”他虽想争辩，终于也被迫承认了这一点。他同意后，我便说：“那么，我们能否认吗？医生就其作为医生而言，寻求或吩咐的，不是医生的利益，而是病人的利益。因为我们已经同意，‘精确地说’，医生是身体的统领和管理者，不是挣钱者。我们同意过这一点吗？”他表示同意。“同样，‘精确意义的’舵手，是水手的统领，
english: which is ruled by it.” This too he was finally brought to admit though he tried to contest it. But when he had agreed—“Can we deny, then,” said I, “that neither does any physician in so far as he is a physician seek or enjoin the advantage of the physician but that of the patient? For we have agreed that the physician, ‘precisely’ speaking, is a ruler and governor of bodies and not a moneymaker. Did we agree on that?” He assented. “And so the ‘precise’ pilot is a ruler of sailors,

chinese: 而不是一名水手？”这一点也得到承认。“那么，这样的舵手和统领，考虑和吩咐的，不是舵手的利益，而是他所统领的水手的利益。”他勉强同意了。“所以，”我说，“色拉叙马霍斯，任何担任统治职务的人，只要就其作为统治者而言，考虑和命令的都不是自身利益，而是被他统治、由他施展技艺加以服务的人的利益。他在一切言行中，注视的都是那个对象，以及对那对象有益而合适的事情。”
english: not a sailor?” That was admitted. “Then that sort of a pilot and ruler will not consider and enjoin the advantage of the pilot but that of the sailor whose ruler he is.” He assented reluctantly. “Then,” said I, “Thrasymachus, neither does anyone in any office of rule in so far as he is a ruler consider and enjoin his own advantage but that of the one whom he rules and for whom he exercises his craft, and he keeps his eyes fixed on that and on what is advantageous and suitable to that in all that he says and does.”

chinese:
讨论进行到这里，人人都看出，他给正义下的公式已经倒转过来。色拉叙马霍斯没有回答，却说：“告诉我，苏格拉底，你有保姆吗？”
“什么意思？”我说，“你为什么不回答我，却问这种问题？”
“因为，”他说，“她让自己的小鼻涕虫到处流着鼻涕，明明很需要，却不给你擦干净脸。她连牧人与羊的区别都不能让你懂得。”
“请问，你凭什么这样想？”我说。“因为你以为牧羊人
english: When we had come to this point in the discussion and it was apparent to everybody that his formula of justice had suffered a reversal of form, Thrasymachus, instead of replying, said, “Tell me, Socrates, have you got a nurse?” “What do you mean?” said I. “Why didn’t you answer me instead of asking such a question?” “Because,” he said, “she lets her little ‘snotty’ run about drivelling and doesn’t wipe your face clean, though you need it badly, if she can’t get you to know the difference between the shepherd and the sheep.” “And what, pray, makes you think that?” said I. “Because you think that the shepherds

chinese: 和牧牛人考虑的是羊和牛的好处，喂肥、照料它们时，所图的竟会是主人和自己利益之外的东西。同样，你似乎以为我们城邦的统治者——我说真正的统治者——对被统治者的想法，和一个人对羊的态度有什么不同；又以为他们日日夜夜想的，会不是
english: and the neat-herds are considering the good of the sheep and the cattle and fatten and tend them with anything else in view than the good of their masters and themselves; and by the same token you seem to suppose that the rulers in our cities, I mean the real rulers, differ at all in their thoughts of the governed from a man’s attitude towards his sheep or that they think of anything else night and day than

chinese: 自己的利益从何而来。你对正义、正义之事、不正义和不正义之事的理解，偏离实情太远了，竟不知道正义和正义之事，说到底就是别人的好处，也就是强者和统治者的利益，而损害却由服从、侍奉的被统治者自己承担。不正义恰好相反，它统治着那些无论怎样说都单纯而正义的人；这些人在被统治时，做着有利于强者的事，通过侍奉使他幸福，
english: the sources of their own profit. And you are so far out concerning the just and justice and the unjust and injustice that you don’t know that justice and the just are literally the other fellow’s good—the advantage of the stronger and the ruler, but a detriment that is all his own of the subject who obeys and serves; while injustice is the contrary and rules those who are simple in every sense of the word and just, and they being thus ruled do what is for his advantage who is the stronger and make him happy

chinese: 却丝毫没有使自己幸福。单纯的苏格拉底，你必须这样看这件事：正义者与不正义者交往，结局总是吃亏。先看商业往来，只要两人合伙经营，到了拆伙时，你决不会发现正义者比不正义者多得，反而总是他吃亏。再看他们与城邦的关系：缴纳直接税或捐款时，财产相同，正义者交得多，另一人交得少；而有分配时，
english: in serving him, but themselves by no manner of means. And you must look at the matter, my simple-minded Socrates, in this way: that the just man always comes out at a disadvantage in his relation with the unjust. To begin with, in their business dealings in any joint undertaking of the two you will never find that the just man has the advantage over the unjust at the dissolution of the partnership but that he always has the worst of it. Then again, in their relations with the state, if there are direct taxes or contributions to be paid, the just man contributes more from an equal estate and the other less, and when there is a distribution

chinese: 一个人得利很多，另一个人一无所得。他们各自担任公职，也同样如此。且不说其他损失，正义者肯定要因疏于照料而使自己的事务陷入混乱；又因坚持正义，不能从城邦那里获利；此外，他不愿用不正义的方式为亲友效劳，还会得罪他们。相反，不正义者得到的全是与这些相反的好处。当然，我指的是刚才说过的那种人，
english:
the one gains much and the other nothing. And so when each holds office, apart from any other loss the just man must count on his own affairs falling into disorder through neglect, while because of his justice makes no profit from the state, and thereto he will displease his friends and his acquaintances by his unwillingness to serve them unjustly. But to the unjust man all the opposite advantages accrue.”

I mean, of course, the one I was just speaking of,

chinese: 有能力大规模占取便宜的人。因此，你若要判断，对他本人来说，不正义比正义有利多少，就该考察这种人。要理解这件事，最容易的办法，是转向最彻底的不正义：它使作恶者最幸福，使受害者和不愿亲自作恶的人最悲惨。这就是僭主统治，它既用隐秘的手段，也用暴力，夺走别人的东西，无论神圣的还是世俗的、私人的还是公共的，不是一点点夺取，而是一举夺尽。
english: the man who has the ability to overreach on a large scale. Consider this type of man, then, if you wish to judge how much more profitable it is to him personally to be unjust than to be just. And the easiest way of all to understand this matter will be to turn to the most consummate form of injustice which makes the man who has done the wrong most happy and those who are wronged and who would not themselves willingly do wrong most miserable. And this is tyranny, which both by stealth and by force takes away what belongs to others, both sacred and profane, both private and public, not little by little but at one swoop.

chinese: 只要分别犯下其中任何一种不正义之事，作恶者若没有逃过察觉，就要受罚，并蒙受最大的耻辱。人们把单独做这些不正义之事的人叫作劫掠神庙者、绑架者、入室盗贼、骗子和窃贼。可是，一个人不仅夺取公民的财产，连公民本人也绑走、奴役时，别人却不再用这些羞辱性的名称称他，而是宣布他幸福而有福。如此说的，不只是本城公民，
english: For each several part of such wrongdoing the malefactor who fails to escape detection is fined and incurs the extreme of contumely; for temple-robbers, kidnappers, burglars, swindlers, and thieves the appellations of those who commit these partial forms of injustice. But when in addition to the property of the citizens men kidnap and enslave the citizens themselves, instead of these opprobrious names they are pronounced happy and blessed not only by their fellow-citizens

chinese: 还有所有听说那个人实行了完整、彻底的不正义的人。因为，谴责不正义者之所以责骂，并不是害怕自己做不正义之事，而是害怕自己遭受不正义。因此，苏格拉底，只要规模足够大，不正义就比正义更强大、更自由、更能支配。正如我开头所说，正义是强者的利益；不正义之事却给自己带来收益，有利于自己。”
english: but by all who hear the story of the man who has committed complete and entire injustice. For it is not the fear of doing but of suffering wrong that calls forth the reproaches of those who revile injustice. Thus, Socrates, injustice on a sufficiently large scale is a stronger, freer, and a more masterful thing than justice, and, as I said in the beginning, it is the advantage of the stronger that is the just, while the unjust is what profits man’s self and is for his advantage.”

chinese: 色拉叙马霍斯像澡堂里泼水的人，把这一大股话突然浇进我们耳朵以后，就想离开。但在座的人不肯，坚持要他留下，为自己的话作出说明。我尤其恳切地挽留，说：“色拉叙马霍斯，你真让我惊讶。把这样一套学说抛给我们，难道你就要走，不留下好好教我们，或自己学明白事情究竟是否如此吗？你以为自己试图决定的是小事，
english: After this Thrasymachus was minded to depart when like a bathman he had poured his speech in a sudden flood over our ears. But the company would not suffer him and were insistent that he should remain and render an account of what he had said. And I was particularly urgent and said, “I am surprised at you, Thrasymachus; after hurling such a doctrine at us, can it be that you propose to depart without staying to teach us properly or learn yourself whether this thing is so or not? Do you think it is a small matter that you are attempting to determine

chinese:
而不是整个人生应当怎样过，怎样才会让我们每个人活得最有价值吗？”
“怎么，我否认了这一点吗？”色拉叙马霍斯说。“看来你是这样，”我说，“不然就是丝毫不在乎我们，所以并不关心：我们不知道你声称知道的事，会因此生活得更坏，还是更好。朋友，请竭力也让我们弄明白：
english:
and not the entire conduct of life that for each of us would make living most worth while?” “Well, do I deny it?” said Thrasymachus. “You seem to,” said I, “or else to care nothing for us and so feel no concern whether we are going to live worse or better lives in our ignorance of what you affirm that you know.”

Nay, my good fellow, do your best to make the matter clear to us also:

chinese: 你给这样一群人任何益处，都不会是一笔坏投资。因为就我自己而言，我告诉你，我并没有被说服。我也不认为不正义比正义更有利，即使让它自由施展，不阻挡它的意愿，也不认为如此。先生，假定某人不正义，并且能实行不正义，因为他或者不被发现，或者能用暴力维持自己的行为，我仍然不会因此相信，不正义比正义更有利。
english: it will be no bad investment for you—any benefit that you bestow on such company as this. For I tell you for my part that I am not convinced, neither do I think that injustice is more profitable than justice, not even if one gives it free scope and does not hinder it of its will. But, suppose, sir, a man to be unjust and to be able to act unjustly either because he is not detected or can maintain it by violence, all the same he does not convince me that it is more profitable than justice.

chinese:
我们中间也许还有人这样想，并非只有我一个。所以，朋友，请说服我们，让我们充分相信：我们偏爱正义而不选不正义，是判断错了。”
“我怎样才能说服你？”他说，“如果刚才说的都不能使你信服，我还能替你做什么？要我把论证拿起来，硬塞进你脑袋里吗？”
“千万不要！”我说，“别这样。不过，首先，你说了一件事，就坚持它；如果改变立场，就公开改变，不要试图蒙混我们。
english: Now it may be that there is someone else among us who feels in this way and that I am not the only one. Persuade us, then, my dear fellow, convince us satisfactorily that we are ill advised in preferring justice to injustice.” “And how am I to persuade you?” he said. “If you are not convinced by what I just now was saying, what more can I do for you? Shall I take the argument and ram it into your head?” “Heaven forbid!” I said, “don’t do that. But in the first place when you have said a thing stand by it, or if you shift your ground change openly and don’t try to deceive us.

chinese: 可现在，色拉叙马霍斯，你看——让我们回到前面的例子——你起初按真正的意义理解医生，后来却不肯保持一致，精确地坚持真正牧人的概念。你似乎认为，他作为牧人放羊时，考虑的不是羊最大的好处，而是像个即将赴宴的食客，考虑美味佳肴；或者考虑卖掉它们，
english: But, as it is, you see, Thrasymachus—let us return to the previous examples—you see that while you began by taking the physician in the true sense of the word, you did not think fit afterwards to be consistent and maintain with precision the notion of the true shepherd, but you apparently think that he herds his sheep in his quality of shepherd not with regard to what is best for the sheep but as if he were a banqueter about to be feasted with regard to the good cheer or again with a view to the sale of them

chinese: 仿佛他是挣钱者，而不是牧人。然而，牧人的技艺所关心的，无疑只是怎样为它照看的对象提供最好的东西。因为，只要它丝毫不失为牧人的技艺，它自身的事务、自身最好的状态，就已完全得到保障。同样，我以为我们刚才也被迫承认：每一种统治，就其作为统治而言，考虑的只是受它统治和照料的对象的最大好处，
english: as if he were a money-maker and not a shepherd. But the art of the shepherd surely is concerned with nothing else than how to provide what is best for that over which is set, since its own affairs, its own best estate, are entirely sufficiently provided for so long as it in nowise fails of being the shepherd’s art. And in like manner I supposed that we just now were constrained to acknowledge that every form of rule in so far as it is rule considers what is best for nothing else than that which is governed and cared for by it,

chinese:
无论公共统治还是私人管理，都是如此。怎么，你以为我们城邦的统治者和官员——真正的统治者——是自愿任职、实行统治的吗？”
“我不是以为，”他说，“我完全知道他们就是这样。”
“可是，色拉叙马霍斯，其他形式的管理又如何呢？你没看见，没有人自愿选择担任管理职务，他们都要求报酬。这不就意味着，担任职务所带来的好处，不是归他们，而是归他们所管理的人吗？
english:
alike in political and private rule. Why, do you think that the rulers and holders of office in our cities—the true rulers—willingly hold office and rule?” “I don’t think,” he said, “I know right well they do.”

“But what of other forms of rule, Thrasymachus? Do you not perceive that no one chooses of his own will to hold the office of rule, but they demand pay, which implies that not to them will benefit accrue from their holding office but to those whom they rule?

chinese:
请告诉我这一点：我们通常不都是说，各门技艺彼此不同，是因为它们的能力或功能不同吗？朋友，为了使我们能得出结果，请不要违背自己的真实想法回答。”
“嗯，是的，”他说，“正是这个使它们不同。”“每门技艺给予我们的益处，不也是它特有的，而非共同的？譬如医术给予健康，航海技艺给予海上的安全，其他技艺也一样。”
“当然。”
“取得报酬的技艺，不也给予报酬吗？因为那就是它的功能。
english: For tell me this: we ordinarily say, do we not, that each of the arts is different from others because its power or function is different? And, my dear fellow, in order that we may reach some result, don’t answer counter to your real belief. ” “Well, yes,” he said, “that is what renders it different.” “And does not each art also yield us benefit that is peculiar to itself and not general, as for example medicine health, the pilot’s art safety at sea, and the other arts similarly?” “Assuredly.” “And does not the wage-earner’s art yield wage? For that is its function.

chinese:
你会把医术和航海技艺认作同一种吗？或者，照你提出的要求，作‘精确’的区分：一个舵手因航海对身体有益而恢复了健康，你并不会因此就把他的技艺叫作医术，对不对？”
“当然不会。”他说。“我想，同样，一个人在挣钱时身体健康，你也不会把取得报酬叫作医术。”
“当然不会。”
english: Would you identify medicine and the pilot’s art? Or if you please to discriminate ‘precisely’ as you proposed, none the more if a pilot regains his health because a sea voyage is good for him, no whit the more, I say, for this reason do you call his art medicine, do you?” “Of course not,” he said. “Neither, I take it, do you call wage-earning medicine if a man earning wages is in health.” “ Surely not.”

chinese:
“那么再看这一点：一个人在治疗时取得了报酬，你会因此把医术叫作取得报酬的技艺吗？”
“不会。”他说。“我们不是已经同意，每门技艺所产生的益处，是它所特有的吗？”
“就算是吧。”他说。“那么，各种技艺者共同得到的任何一般性好处，显然来自他们都运用了另外某种相同的东西。”
“看来如此。”他说。“而我们说，技艺者之所以得到挣钱的好处，是因为他们另外施展了取得报酬的技艺。”他勉强同意了。“那么，这项好处，
english: “But what of this? Do you call medicine wage-earning, if a man when giving treatment earns wages?” “No,” he said. “And did we not agree that the benefit derived from each art is peculiar to it?” “So be it,” he said. “Any common or general benefit that all craftsmen receive, then, they obviously derive from their common use of some further identical thing.” “It seems so,” he said. “And we say that the benefit of earning wages accrues to the craftsmen from their further exercise of the wage-earning art.” He assented reluctantly. “Then the benefit,

chinese:
也就是取得报酬，并不是每个人从他自己的技艺中得到的。倘若要‘严格地’考察，医术带来健康，取得报酬的技艺带来酬金；建筑术带来房屋，伴随它的取得报酬的技艺带来酬金。其他技艺也都如此，各自完成自己的工作，使自己所负责的对象受益；但要是不另外加上报酬，技艺者本人从这门技艺中能得到什么益处吗？”
“显然没有。”他说。“那么，他无偿工作的时候，也就没有给别人带来益处吗？”
english: the receiving of wages does not accrue to each from his own art. But if we are to consider it ‘precisely’ medicine produces health but the fee-earning art the pay, and architecture a house but the fee-earning art accompanying it the fee, and so with all the others, each performs its own task and benefits that over which it is set, but unless pay is added to it is there any benefit which the craftsman receives from the craft?” “Apparently not,” he said. “Does he then bestow no benefit either when he works for nothing?”

chinese:
“当然还是带来了。”
“色拉叙马霍斯，这样一来岂不是立刻就清楚了：任何技艺或职务，都不为它自身谋利益；正如我们早已说过的，它为自己的对象谋取并规定有益的事，考虑的是那个较弱者的利益，而不是较强者的利益？所以，色拉叙马霍斯朋友，我刚才才说，没有人自愿选择承担统治和职务，把别人的麻烦接过来理顺，人人都要求为此取得报酬，
english:
“I’ll say he does.” “Then, Thrasymachus, is not this immediately apparent, that no art or office provides what is beneficial for itself—but as we said long ago it provides and enjoins what is beneficial to its subject, considering the advantage of that, the weaker, and not the advantage the stronger?”

That was why, friend Thrasymachus, I was just now saying that no one of his own will chooses to hold rule and office and take other people’s troubles in hand to straighten them out, but everybody expects pay for that,

chinese:
因为一个人要正确地施展技艺，按这门技艺发号施令，他所做的、所规定的，绝不是最有利于自己的事，而是最有利于对象的事。因此看来，要有人肯承担统治，就必须给他们报酬：或者是金钱，或者是荣誉，或者在他们拒绝时施以惩罚。”
“苏格拉底，这话是什么意思？”格劳孔说，“那两种报酬我认得，可你说的惩罚，还把它说成一种报酬，我就不明白了。”
“那么，”我说，“最好的人所得到的报酬，你还不明白，
english:
because he who is to exercise the art rightly never does what is best for himself or enjoins it when he gives commands according to the art, but what is best for the subject. That is the reason, it seems, why pay must be provided for those who are to consent to rule, either in form of money or honor or a penalty if they refuse.”

“What do you mean by that, Socrates?” said Glaucon. “The two wages I recognize, but the penalty you speak of and described as a form of wage I don’t understand.” “Then,” said I, “you don’t understand the wages of the best men

chinese:
最优秀的人在同意任职、统治的时候，正是为了这种报酬。你不知道，贪图荣誉、贪图金钱，大家说来是可耻的，实际上也的确可耻吗？”
“我知道。”他说。“好，”我说，“所以，好人不愿意为了金钱或荣誉去统治。他们不愿意公开为统治的服务收取报酬，被叫作雇工；也不愿意凭职务暗中取得钱财，被叫作贼；同样，他们也不为了荣誉，
english: for the sake of which the finest spirits hold office and rule when they consent to do so. Don’t you know that to be covetous of honor and covetous of money is said to be and is a reproach?” “I do,” he said. “Well, then,” said I, “that is why the good are not willing to rule either for the sake of money or of honor. They do not wish to collect pay openly for their service of rule and be styled hirelings nor to take it by stealth from their office and be called thieves, nor yet for the sake of honor,

chinese: 因为他们不贪图荣誉。所以，必须用某种强制和惩罚迫使他们去统治，他们才会同意任职。也许正因如此，主动求取官职而不等别人来迫使自己，被看作可耻的事。而最大的惩罚，就是自己不肯任职、统治，就会受一个比自己更坏的人统治。在我看来，比较好的人之所以任职，正是害怕这一点。他们承担职务，不是指望享受，也不是把它当作好事，而是当作不得不承受的苦差；因为他们无法把这事交给比自己更好的人，
english: for they are not covetous of honor. So there must be imposed some compulsion and penalty to constrain them to rule if they are to consent to hold office. That is perhaps why to seek office oneself and not await compulsion is thought disgraceful. But the chief penalty is to be governed by someone worse if a man will not himself hold office and rule. It is from fear of this, as it appears to me, that the better sort hold office when they do, and then they go to it not in the expectation of enjoyment nor as to a good thing, but as to a necessary evil and because they are unable to turn it over to better men than themselves

chinese: 或与自己同样好的人。我们可以大胆地说，要是有一个城邦，其中尽是好人，那么大家争着免除任职责任，会像现在争着任职一样热切。在那里就会显明：真正的统治者，的的确确，生来所谋求的并非自己的利益，而是被统治者的利益。因此，任何明智的人都会宁愿由别人使自己受益，而不愿费心去使别人受益。所以，对于这一点，我
english: or to their like. For we may venture to say that, if there should be a city of good men only, immunity from office-holding would be as eagerly contended for as office is now, and there it would be made plain that in very truth the true ruler does not naturally seek his own advantage but that of the ruled; so that every man of understanding would rather choose to be benefited by another than to be bothered with benefiting him. This point then I

chinese:
绝不同意色拉叙马霍斯所说的，正义就是强者的利益。不过，这留待另一个时候再说。眼下色拉叙马霍斯的另一项主张，在我看来要重大得多：他说不正义的人的生活，比正义的人的生活更好。格劳孔，你选择哪一种说法？”我问，“哪一种在你看来更真实？”
“我说，正义的人的生活更有益。”他回答。
english: by no means concede to Thrasymachus, that justice is the advantage of the superior. But that we will reserve for another occasion. A far weightier matter seems to me Thrasymachus’s present statement, his assertion that the life of the unjust man is better than that of the just. Which now do you choose, Glaucon?” said I, “and which seems to you to be the truer statement?” “That the life of the just man is more profitable, I say,” he replied.

chinese:
“色拉叙马霍斯刚才为不正义的人的生活列举的种种好处，你都听见了吗？”我说。
“听见了，”他说，“可是我没有被说服。”
“那么，假如我们能找到办法，你愿不愿意让我们试着说服他，说明他说的不是真的？”
“当然愿意。”他说。“那么，如果我们发表一篇相对的演说，也来一一列举做正义之人的好处，他再回应，我们再反驳，就得把双方演说中列出的好处数一数、量一量，
english: “Did you hear,” said I, “all the goods that Thrasymachus just now enumerated for the life of the unjust man?” “I heard,” he said, “but I am not convinced.” “Do you wish us then to try to persuade him, supposing we can find a way, that what he says is not true?” “Of course I wish it,” he said. “If then we oppose him in a set speech enumerating in turn the advantages of being just and he replies and we rejoin, we shall have to count up and measure the goods listed in the respective speeches

chinese:
立刻就得找裁判来替我们作决定。但要是像前面的讨论一样，在探究中彼此说定，各自承认哪些事，我们自己就既是裁判，也是辩论者。”
“正是如此。”他说。“哪种办法你更喜欢？”我说。“这一种。”他说。
“那么，来吧，色拉叙马霍斯，”我说，“回到开头，回答我们。你主张，完美而彻底的不正义，比彻底的正义更有益。”
english:
and we shall forthwith be in need of judges to decide between us. But if, as in the preceding discussion, we come to terms with one another as to what we admit in the inquiry, we shall be ourselves both judges and pleaders.” “Quite so,” he said. “Which method do you like best?” said I. “This one,” he said.

“Come then, Thrasymachus,” I said, “go back to the beginning and answer us. You affirm that perfect and complete injustice is more profitable than justice that is complete.”

chinese:
“我主张这个，”他说，“也已经告诉过你理由。”
“那么请告诉我，关于它们，你在这一点上怎么说。我想，你把其中一个叫作德性，另一个叫作恶德吧？”
“当然。”
“正义是德性，不正义是恶德？”
“真会想啊，你这天真的人！我明明说不正义有利，正义无利。”
“那么，究竟怎么说呢？”
“恰好相反。”他回答。“什么！正义是恶德？”
“不是，而是最高贵的单纯，或者说心地善良。”
“那么，你把不正义叫作心地恶劣吗？”
english: “I affirm it,” he said, “and have told you my reasons.” “Tell me then how you would express yourself on this point about them. You call one of them, I presume, a virtue and the other a vice?” “Of course.” “Justice the virtue and injustice the vice?” “It is likely, you innocent, when I say that injustice pays and justice doesn’t pay.” “But what then, pray?” “The opposite,” he replied. “What! justice vice?” “No, but a most noble simplicity or goodness of heart.” “Then do you call injustice badness of heart?”

chinese:
“不，而是判断高明。”
“色拉叙马霍斯，你也认为不正义的人聪明而善好吗？”
“是的，只要他们能够做到彻底的不正义，”他说，“能够把城邦和各族的人置于自己的支配之下。不过，你大概以为我指的是偷钱袋的人。那类事情当然也有利可图，”他说，“只要不被发觉。然而这种事不值得算进去，值得算的，只有我刚才说的那一种。”
english: “No, but goodness of judgement.” “Do you also, Thrasymachus, regard the unjust as intelligent and good?” “Yes, if they are capable of complete injustice,” he said, “and are able to subject to themselves cities and tribes of men. But you probably suppose that I mean those who take purses. There is profit to be sure even in that sort of thing,” he said, “if it goes undetected. But such things are not worth taking into the account, but only what I just described.”

chinese:
“你在这件事上的意思，我并非不明白，”我说，“但让我吃惊的是，你竟然把不正义列在德性和智慧这一边，把正义列在相反的一边。”
“我确实这样分。”他说。“朋友，”我说，“这可是个更难应付的主张。你若走到这一步，我就很难知道怎样回答了。因为，如果你像另外一些辩论者那样，主张不正义有利，却承认它败坏、可耻，我们就还有机会根据通常承认的道理展开论辩。可如今，你显然打算主张它光荣而强大；我们原先归给正义的那些其他品质，
english:
“I am not unaware of your meaning in that,” I said; “but this is what surprised me, that you should range injustice under the head of virtue and wisdom, and justice in the opposite class.” “Well, I do so class them,” he said. “That,” said I, “is a stiffer proposition, my friend, and if you are going as far as that it is hard to know what to answer.”

For if your position were that injustice is profitable yet you conceded it to be vicious and disgraceful as some other disputants do, there would be a chance for an argument on conventional principles. But, as it is, you obviously are going to affirm that it is honorable and strong and you will attach to it all the other qualities

chinese:
你也都会归给不正义，因为你连把它归入德性和智慧一类都毫不退缩。”
“你真是一位货真价实的预言家。”他回答。“好吧，”我说，“只要我认为你说的就是你所想的，我就不该退缩，而应顺着这场探究的道理追问到底。色拉叙马霍斯，现在我完全相信，你不是在‘拿我们开玩笑’，而是在告诉我们，你对于真实情况究竟持有什么看法。”
“我信不信这个，对你有什么区别？”他说，“你为什么不检验这个论证呢？”
english: that we were assigning to the just, since you don’t shrink from putting it in the category of virtue and wisdom.” “You are a most veritable prophet,” he replied. “Well,” said I, “I mustn’t flinch from following out the logic of the inquiry, so long as I conceive you to be saying what you think. For now, Thrasymachus, I absolutely believe that you are not ‘mocking’ us but telling us your real opinions about the truth.” “What difference does it make to you,” he said, “whether I believe it or not?” “Why don’t you test the argument?”

chinese:
“没有区别，”我说，“不过，除了你已经说的，我还想让你告诉我这一点：你认为正义的人会想要占另一个正义的人的上风，超过他吗？”
“绝不会，”他说，“不然，他就不再是那样一个讨人喜欢的傻好人了。”
“他会想要超过正义的行动，越出它的界限吗？”
“也不会。”他回答。“可他会怎样对待不正义的人呢？他会认为占不正义的人的上风、超过他，是恰当而正义的，还是不会？”
“会的，”他说，“可他没有这个本事。”
“我问的不是这一点，”我说，
english: “No difference,” said I, “but here is something I want you to tell me in addition to what you have said. Do you think the just man would want to overreach or exceed another just man?” “By no means,” he said; “otherwise he would not be the delightful simpleton that he is.” “And would he exceed or overreach or go beyond the just action?” “Not that either,” he replied. “But how would he treat the unjust man—would he deem it proper and just to outdo, overreach, or go beyond him or would he not?” “He would,” he said, “but he wouldn’t be able to.” “That is not my question,” I said,

chinese:
“而是说，正义的人既不要求、也不想要超过正义的人，只想超过不正义的人，是不是如此？”
“是这样。”他回答。“那么，不正义的人呢？他会要求占正义的人和正义的行动的上风，超过他们吗？”
“当然，”他说，“因为他要求超过一切，占过一切的上风。”
“那么，不正义的人也会想要超过不正义的人和不正义的行动；他的一切努力，就是要在每件事情上为自己取得最多。”
“是这样。”
“我们这样说吧，”我说，“正义的人不求占同类的上风，只求占不同类的上风；而不正义的人，则对两者都如此。”
english:
“but whether it is not the fact that the just man does not claim and wish to outdo the just man but only the unjust?” “That is the case,” he replied. “How about the unjust then? Does he claim to overreach and outdo the just man and the just action?” “Of course,” he said, “since he claims to overreach and get the better of everything.” “Then the unjust man will overreach and outdo also both the unjust man and the unjust action, and all his endeavor will be to get the most in everything for himself.” “That is so.”

“Let us put it in this way,” I said; “the just man does not seek to take advantage of his like but of his unlike, but the unjust man of both.”

chinese:
“说得好极了。”他说。“而不正义的人聪明而善好，正义的人两者都不是。”
“这也对。”他说。“那么，不正义的人也就类似聪明而善好的人，正义的人却不类似，是不是？”我说。
“当然，”他说，“他既然是这种人，就会类似这种人；另一个人则不会。”
“很好。那么，各人类似什么样的人，他自己也就是什么样的人。”
“你还能怎么想？”他说。“好吧，色拉叙马霍斯，
english: “Admirably put,” he said. “But the unjust man is intelligent and good and the just man neither.” “That, too, is right,” he said. “Is it not also true,” I said, “that the unjust man is like the intelligent and good and the just man is not?” “Of course,” he said, “being such he will be like to such and the other not.” “Excellent. Then each is such as that to which he is like.” “What else do you suppose?” he said. “Very well, Thrasymachus,

chinese:
你是否承认，有人懂音乐，有人不懂音乐？”
“承认。”
“其中谁有知识，谁没有知识？”
“我想，懂音乐的人有知识，不懂音乐的人没有知识。”
“那么，他在有知识的事情上是好的，在没有知识的事情上是坏的，岂不是吗？”
“是的。”
“医生也一样吗？”
“一样。”
“那么，朋友，你认为一个懂音乐的人给里拉琴调音时，在绷紧或放松琴弦方面，会想要超过另一个懂音乐的人，或要求并认为应该胜过他吗？”
“我不这么认为。”
“但他会想要超过不懂音乐的人吗？”
“必然会。”他说。“那么，懂医术的人呢？
