english: “Certainly.” “That the rulers must be the elder and the ruled the younger is obvious.” “It is.” “And that the rulers must be their best?” “This too.” “And do not the best of the farmers prove the best farmers?” “Yes.” “And in this case, since we want them to be the best of the guardians, must they not be the best guardians, the most regardful of the state?” “Yes.” “They must then to begin with be intelligent in such matters and capable,

chinese:
还必须关切城邦的利益？”
“是这样。”
“但一个人最有可能关切的，是他所爱的东西。”
“必然如此。”
“而且，一个人最有可能爱的，是他认为与自己的利益一致的东西；他相信，它兴盛，自己也兴盛；它若不兴盛，自己也遭到相反的命运。”
“是这样。”他说。
“那么，我们必须从其余护卫者中挑选这样的人：据我们的观察，他们在整个一生中，最倾向于热切地去做自己认为
english: and furthermore careful of the interests of the state?” “That is so.” “But one would be most likely to be careful of that which he loved.” “Necessarily.” “And again, one would be most likely to love that whose interests he supposed to coincide with his own, and thought that when it prospered, he too would prosper and if not, the contrary.” “So it is,” he said. “Then we must pick out from the other guardians such men as to our observation appear most inclined through the entire course of their lives to be zealous to do what they think

chinese:
有利于城邦的事情，而最不可能同意做与之相反的事情。”
“这样的选择很合适。”他说。
“那么我想，我们必须在他们人生的每一阶段观察他们，看他们是否始终在心中保存、护卫这个信念：必须去做最有利于城邦的事；看他们是否无论受到诱惑还是强迫，都不会不知不觉地把这个信念逐出灵魂。”
“你说的‘逐出’是什么意思？”他问。
“我来说明，”我说，“在我看来，一种信念离开心智，要么是自愿的，要么是非自愿的。
english:
for the interest of the state, and who would be least likely to consent to do the opposite.” “That would be a suitable choice,” he said. “I think, then, we shall have to observe them at every period of life, to see if they are conservators and guardians of this conviction in their minds and never by sorcery nor by force can be brought to expel from their souls unawares this conviction that they must do what is best for the state.” “What do you mean by the ‘expelling’?” he said.

“I will tell you,” said I; “it seems to me that the exit of a belief from the mind is either voluntary or involuntary.

chinese:
一个人学到了更正确的东西，错误的信念便自愿离去；而任何真实信念的离去，都是非自愿的。”
“自愿的这一种，”他说，“我明白；非自愿的，还需要你指教。”
“怎么，”我说，“你不同意我吗？人失去好的东西是非自愿的，摆脱坏的东西则是自愿的。对于真实受到欺骗，不是坏事吗？拥有真实，不是好事吗？你不认为，对存在的事物持有符合其所是的意见，就是拥有真实吗？”
“是的，”他说，“你说得对，我同意，人失去真实的意见是非自愿的。”
“而这种失去，不是通过偷窃、诱惑或强迫发生的吗？”
“这回我又不明白了。”他说。
“我一定是在用悲剧的高调说话，”我说，
english: Voluntary is the departure of the false belief from one who learns better, involuntary that of every true belief.” “The voluntary,” he said, “I understand, but I need instruction about the involuntary.” “How now,” said I, “don’t you agree with me in thinking that men are unwillingly deprived of good things but willingly of evil? Or is it not an evil to be deceived in respect of the truth and a good to possess truth? And don’t you think that to opine the things that are is to possess the truth?” “Why, yes,” said he, “you are right, and I agree that men are unwillingly deprived of true opinions.” “And doesn’t this happen to them by theft, by the spells of sorcery or by force?” “I don’t understand now either,” he said. “I must be talking in high tragic style,” I said;

chinese:
“所谓意见被偷走的人，我指的是被说服的人和遗忘的人；因为在一种情形中，时间使他们不知不觉地失去信念；在另一种情形中，论说使他们如此。现在我想，你明白了吧？”
“明白了。”
“那么，所谓受到强制或逼迫的人，我指的是某种痛苦或苦难迫使他们改变了想法的人。”
“这点我也明白，你说得对。”
“至于受到诱惑的人，
english: “by those who have their opinions stolen from them I mean those who are over-persuaded and those who forget, because in the one case time, in the other argument strips them unawares of their beliefs. Now I presume you understand, do you not?” “Yes.” “Well, then, by those who are constrained or forced I mean those whom some pain or suffering compels to change their minds.” “That too I understand and you are right.” “And the victims of sorcery

chinese:
我相信，你也会说，他们就是被快乐迷住，或被某种恐惧吓住，因而改变意见的人。”
“是的，”他说，“一切欺骗看来都像是在心智上施加魔法。”
“那么，正如我刚才所说，我们必须寻找最善于护卫内在信念的人：他们应当做的，是任何时候都做自己认为最有利于城邦的事。因此，我们必须从童年起就观察他们，给他们安排最容易使人忘记这一原则或受到欺骗的任务；对于记忆牢固、
english:
I am sure you too would say are they who alter their opinions under the spell of pleasure or terrified by some fear.” “Yes,” he said: “everything that deceives appears to cast a spell upon the mind.”

“Well then, as I was just saying, we must look for those who are the best guardians of the indwelling conviction that what they have to do is what they at any time believe to be best for the state. Then we must observe them from childhood up and propose them tasks in which one would be most likely to forget this principle or be deceived, and he whose memory is sure

chinese:
不会被迷惑的人，我们要接纳；另一种人，则必须从名单上划去。不是这样吗？”
“是的。”
“此外，我们必须让他们经历劳苦、疼痛和竞赛，在这些事情中观察同样的品质。”
“对。”他说。
“那么，”我说，“我们不还必须设置第三种竞赛式的考验，针对诱惑，并从中观察他们吗？正如人们把小马带到嘈杂喧闹中，看看它们是否容易受惊，我们也必须趁这些人年幼时，把他们带进恐惧之中，
english: and who cannot be beguiled we must accept and the other kind we must cross off from our list. Is not that so?” “Yes.” “And again we must subject them to toils and pains and competitions in which we have to watch for the same traits.” “Right,” he said. “Then,” said I, “must we not institute a third kind of competitive test with regard to sorcery and observe them in that? Just as men conduct colts to noises and uproar to see if they are liable to take fright, so we must bring these lads while young into fears

chinese: 再把他们引入快乐之中；我们考验他们，要比人们用火验金更加仔细，看看这个人是否不受这种魔法影响，始终保持镇定，妥善护卫自己和所受的教养，在一切处境中维持自身真正的节奏与和谐，保持那种使他对自己和城邦最有用的品格。如果一个人在童年、少年和成年都能承受考验，
english:
and again pass them into pleasures, testing them much more carefully than men do gold in the fire, to see if the man remains immune to such witchcraft and preserves his composure throughout, a good guardian of himself and the culture which he has received, maintaining the true rhythm and harmony of his being in all those conditions, and the character that would make him most useful to himself and to the state.”

And he who as boy, lad, and man endures the test

chinese:
经历考验之后依然完好无损，我们就必须立他为城邦的统治者和护卫者；在他生前给予奖赏，死后则分配给他最高的安葬礼遇和其他纪念。至于另一种人，我们必须拒绝。格劳孔，”我说，“这就是我对于挑选、任命统治者和护卫者的总体想法，只勾画了轮廓，还没有详尽展开。”
“我也认为，”他说，“大致应当如此。”
“那么，把这些人称为
english: and issues from it unspoiled we must establish as ruler over our city and its guardian, and bestow rewards upon him in life, and in death the allotment of the supreme honors of burial-rites and other memorials. But the man of the other type we must reject. Such,” said I, “appears to me, Glaucon, the general notion of our selection and appointment of rulers and guardians as sketched in outline, but not drawn out in detail.” “I too,” he said, “think much the same.” “Then would it not truly

chinese:
完全意义上的护卫者，监视外部的敌人和内部的朋友，使内部的人不愿作恶、外部的人不能加害，不是最恰当的吗？而把那些我们刚才称为护卫者的年轻人，叫作辅助者，帮助执行统治者的命令。”
“我认为是的。”他回答。
“那么，”我说，“我们怎样才能编出刚才谈过的那种适时有用的虚假故事，
english:
be most proper to designate these as guardians in the full sense of the word, watchers against foemen without and friends within, so that the latter shall not wish and the former shall not be able to work harm, but to name those youths whom we were calling guardians just now, helpers and aids for the decrees of the rulers?” “I think so,” he replied.

“How, then,” said I, “might we contrive one of those opportune falsehoods of which we were just now speaking,

chinese:
用一个高贵的谎言，尽可能说服统治者本人；即使做不到，也说服城邦里的其他人呢？”
“你指什么样的虚构？”他问。
“并不是什么前所未有的东西，”我说，“而是一种腓尼基故事。据诗人断言，而且他们也已使人相信，这样的事情从前在世间许多地方发生过；但在我们的时代没有发生，或许也不大可能发生，要使人相信，得费很大一番劝说。”
“你的样子像是害怕说出自己的想法。”他说。
“等我说了，你就会觉得，我的畏缩很有理由。”我说。
english: so as by one noble lie to persuade if possible the rulers themselves, but failing that the rest of the city?” “What kind of a fiction do you mean?” said he. “Nothing unprecedented,” said I, “but a sort of Phoenician tale, something that has happened ere now in many parts of the world, as the poets aver and have induced men to believe, but that has not happened and perhaps would not be likely to happen in our day and demanding no little persuasion to make it believable.” “You act like one who shrinks from telling his thought,” he said. “You will think that I have right good reason for shrinking when I have told,” I said.

chinese:
“说吧，”他说，“不要怕。”
“好吧，我说。可是，我还是几乎不知道，该拿出怎样的胆量、找到怎样的言辞，先去说服统治者本人和士兵，再说服城邦里的其余人，让他们相信：我们对他们进行的一切训练和教育，实际上只是他们想象的事情，仿佛梦里经历的一样；而真正的情形是，那时他们都在地下，自身在那里受到塑造和养育，
english: “Say on,” said he, “and don’t be afraid.” “Very well, I will. And yet I hardly know how to find the audacity or the words to speak and undertake to persuade first the rulers themselves and the soldiers and then the rest of the city, that in good sooth all our training and educating of them were things that they imagined and that happened to them as it were in a dream; but that in reality at that time they were down within the earth being molded and fostered themselves while

chinese:
他们的武器和其他装备也在那里制作。等到他们完全造成，大地作为母亲，把他们生了出来。因此，如今他们应当把自己的国土当作母亲和养育者，关怀她，保卫她，使她免遭任何攻击；并把其他公民看作自己的兄弟，同样是这片大地的孩子。”
“难怪，”他说，“你说出自己的谎言之前那么难为情。”
“这本来就很自然，”
english:
their weapons and the rest of their equipment were being fashioned. And when they were quite finished the earth as being their mother delivered them, and now as if their land were their mother and their nurse they ought to take thought for her and defend her against any attack and regard the other citizens as their brothers and children of the self-same earth.” “It is not for nothing,” he said, “that you were so bashful about coming out with your lie.”

“It was quite natural that I should be,”

chinese: 我说，“不过，还是听听故事的其余部分吧。我们将在故事里说：你们城邦中所有人虽然都是兄弟，神在塑造你们时，却在适合统治的人的生成中掺入黄金，因此他们最为珍贵；在辅助者中掺入白银，在农夫和其他工匠中掺入铁和铜。你们既然都是亲属，虽然大多数时候会生出与自己同类的孩子，
english: I said; “but all the same hear the rest of the story. While all of you in the city are brothers, we will say in our tale, yet God in fashioning those of you who are fitted to hold rule mingled gold in their generation, for which reason they are the most precious—but in the helpers silver, and iron and brass in the farmers and other craftsmen. And as you are all akin, though for the most part you will breed after your kinds,

chinese: 但也有时会出现：金质的父亲生出银质的儿子，银质的父亲生出金质的后代，其他类别也同样会彼此生出。因此，神给统治者的第一条、最重要的命令就是：对于任何其他事情，都不应像对后代灵魂中这些金属的混合那样，严密护卫、专心观察。如果他们生出的儿子掺有铜或铁，
english: it may sometimes happen that a golden father would beget a silver son and that a golden offspring would come from a silver sire and that the rest would in like manner be born of one another. So that the first and chief injunction that the god lays upon the rulers is that of nothing else are they to be such careful guardians and so intently observant as of the intermixture of these metals in the souls of their offspring, and if sons are born to them with an infusion of brass or iron

chinese: 他们在处置这些孩子时，决不能动怜悯之心，而必须按照每个人的天性给予相称的地位，把他们送到工匠或农夫中去。反过来，如果工匠或农夫生出的孩子，成分中意外地含有金或银，统治者就应当尊重他们，命他们升到较高的位置：有的任护卫者，有的任辅助者。还要说，有一道神谕指出：当铁质或铜质的人成为护卫者时，城邦便会覆灭。你能想出什么办法，让他们相信这个故事吗？”
english: they shall by no means give way to pity in their treatment of them, but shall assign to each the status due to his nature and thrust them out among the artisans or the farmers. And again, if from these there is born a son with unexpected gold or silver in his composition they shall honor such and bid them go up higher, some to the office of guardian, some to the assistanceship, alleging that there is an oracle that the state shall then be overthrown when the man of iron or brass is its guardian. Do you see any way of getting them to believe this tale?”

chinese:
“不，不能让这些人自己相信，”他说，“但我能想出办法，让他们的儿子、后继者和其余后来的人相信。”
“那么，”我说，“即便如此，也会有好的效果，使他们更愿意关心城邦，彼此关怀。我想我明白你的意思。这件事就让它顺着传统流传下去吧。”
“不过，让我们给这些大地之子配上武器，在统治者率领下把他们带出来。到达以后，他们必须在城邦中寻找最适合扎营的地点，
english:
“No, not these themselves,” he said, “but I do, their sons and successors and the rest of mankind who come after.” “Well,” said I, “even that would have a good effect making them more inclined to care for the state and one another. For I think I apprehend your meaning. XXII. And this shall fall out as tradition guides.”

“But let us arm these sons of earth and conduct them under the leadership of their rulers. And when they have arrived they must look out for the fairest site in the city for their encampment,

chinese:
从那个位置，既最能压制内部对法律的反抗，又能抵御外来的攻击，仿佛防止狼袭击羊圈。扎营并向适当的诸神献祭以后，他们就必须营造自己的住处，不是吗？”
“是的。”他说。
“这些住处必须能够冬天御寒，夏天也适用？”
“当然。我想你说的是他们的房屋。”
“是的，”我说，“是士兵的房屋，不是生意人的房屋。”
english: a position from which they could best hold down rebellion against the laws from within and repel aggression from without as of a wolf against the fold. And after they have encamped and sacrificed to the proper gods they must make their lairs, must they not?” “Yes,” he said. “And these must be of a character keep out the cold in winter and be sufficient in summer?” “Of course. For I presume you are speaking of their houses.” “Yes,” said I, “the houses of soldiers not of money-makers.”

chinese:
“你这样区分，是什么意思？”他问。
“我试着解释，”我说，“牧人饲养狗，是为了帮助自己看护羊群；但若把狗养成这样一种习性和天性：因为不守规矩、饥饿或其他恶劣的状况，狗反过来攻击羊、伤害羊，与其说像狗，不如说像狼——这当然是世上最荒唐、最可耻的事情。”
“确实可怕。”他说。
english: “What distinction do you intend by that?” he said. “I will try to tell you,” I said. “It is surely the most monstrous and shameful thing in the world for shepherds to breed the dogs who are to help them with their flocks in such wise and of such a nature that from indiscipline or hunger or some other evil condition the dogs themselves shall attack the sheep and injure them and be likened to wolves instead of dogs.” “A terrible thing, indeed,” he said.

chinese:
“那么，我们不必须尽一切可能防备辅助者用这种方式对待公民，仗着自己更强大，从善意的助手变成凶暴的主人吗？”
“必须。”他说。
“而如果他们所受的教育确实良好，不就已经具备最主要的防护了吗？”
“他们所受的教育当然是好的。”他说。
“亲爱的格劳孔，”我说，“这一点，我们还不能恰当地断言；但我们刚才说的那一点，可以断言：
english: “Must we not then guard by every means in our power against our helpers treating the citizens in any such way and, because they are the stronger, converting themselves from benign assistants into savage masters?” “We must,” he said. “And would they not have been provided with the chief safeguard if their education has really been a good one?” “But it surely has,” he said. “That,” said I, “dear Glaucon, we may not properly affirm, but what we were just now saying we may,

chinese:
如果他们要拥有最能使自己温和地对待彼此、对待所保护之人的东西，就必须受到正确的教育，无论这种教育究竟是什么。”
“这说得对。”他说。
“此外，一个深思熟虑的人还会主张：除了这种教育，为他们提供的房屋和财产，也应当使他们不受妨碍，能最好地完成护卫者自己的工作，而且不至于刺激他们侵害其他公民。”
english: that they must have the right education, whatever it is, if they are to have what will do most to make them gentle to one another and to their charges.” “That is right,” he said. “In addition, moreover, to such an education a thoughtful man would affirm that their houses and the possessions provided for them ought to be such as not to interfere with the best performance of their own work as guardians and not to incite them to wrong the other citizens.”

chinese:
“他这样主张是对的。”
“那么，”我说，“请考虑：如果他们要成为那样的人，他们的住处和生活方式，不就必须大致如下吗？第一，除了绝对必需的东西，任何人都不得拥有私人财产。第二，任何人都不得拥有不许所有人随意进入的住宅或库房。他们的食物，数量应当是节制而勇敢的战争运动员所必需的，
english: “He will rightly affirm that.” “Consider then,” said I, “whether, if that is to be their character, their habitations and ways of life must not be something after this fashion. In the first place, none must possess any private property save the indispensable. Secondly, none must have any habitation or treasure-house which is not open for all to enter at will. Their food, in such quantities as are needful for athletes of war sober and brave,

chinese: 由其他公民按照约定供给，作为护卫工作的报酬；分量应当计算好，使一年结束时既无剩余，也无短缺。他们应当像出征的士兵一样，共同用餐，集体生活。我们会告诉他们：诸神赐予的神圣金银，始终存在于他们灵魂中；他们不需要凡人的金属，虔敬也不允许他们取得凡俗黄金，把它与那天赐的财富混合，使后者受到污染。因为，围绕众人的
english:
they must receive as an agreed stipend from the other citizens as the wages of their guardianship, so measured that there shall be neither superfluity at the end of the year nor any lack. And resorting to a common mess like soldiers on campaign they will live together.”

Gold and silver, we will tell them, they have of the divine quality from the gods always in their souls, and they have no need of the metal of men nor does holiness suffer them to mingle and contaminate that heavenly possession with the acquisition of mortal gold, since many impious deeds have been done about

chinese: 货币，已经发生了许多不敬神的行为，而居于他们内心的金银却没有沾染污垢。因此，在全城居民中，唯独他们不得经手、触摸金银，不得与金银同处一屋，不得把金银饰物挂在身上，也不得用金银器皿饮酒。这样生活，他们便能保全自己，也保全城邦。但是，一旦他们为自己取得私有的土地、房屋和钱币，他们就会成为产业主和农夫，而不再是护卫者；他们会从
english: the coin of the multitude, while that which dwells within them is unsullied. But for these only of all the dwellers in the city it is not lawful to handle gold and silver and to touch them nor yet to come under the same roof with them, nor to hang them as ornaments on their limbs nor to drink from silver and gold. So living they would save themselves and save their city. But whenever they shall acquire for themselves land of their own and houses and coin, they will be house-holders and farmers instead of guardians, and will be transformed

chinese:
同胞的辅助者，变成同胞的敌人和主人。他们将在仇恨别人和被别人仇恨、算计别人和被别人算计之中度过一生，比起外面的敌人，更害怕里面的公民；就在这时，他们已经使自己和城邦驶上即将覆舟的航路。由于所有这些理由，”我说，“让我们宣布：护卫者在住处和其他方面的安排，必须如此，并据此立法。不是吗？”
“完全如此。”格劳孔说。
english: from the helpers of their fellow citizens to their enemies and masters, and so in hating and being hated, plotting and being plotted against they will pass their days fearing far more and rather the townsmen within than the foemen without—and then even then laying the course of near shipwreck for themselves and the state. For all these reasons,” said I, “let us declare that such must be the provision for our guardians in lodging and other respects and so legislate. Shall we not?” “By all means,” said Glaucon.

chinese: 阿德曼托斯插话说：“苏格拉底，要是有人指责你，说你并没有让这些人过上很幸福的生活，而且这还是他们自己造成的，你怎么答辩？城邦实际上属于他们，可他们却不能像普通人那样享用它：拥有田地，建造宽敞漂亮的房屋，置办相称的家具，以私人的祭献求得神的恩惠，款待宾客，也享有你刚才所说的金银等财物，以及那些希望过得幸福的人通常拥有的一切。人们甚至可以说，他们只是闲居在城里，
english:
And Adeimantus broke in and said, “What will be your defence, Socrates, if anyone objects that you are not making these men very happy, and that through their own fault? For the city really belongs to them and yet they get no enjoyment out of it as ordinary men do by owning lands and building fine big houses and providing them with suitable furniture and winning the favor of the gods by private sacrifices and entertaining guests and enjoying too those possessions which you just now spoke of, gold and silver and all that is customary for those who are expecting to be happy?”

But they seem, one might say, to be established in idleness in the city,

chinese:
恰似受雇的兵士，除了守卫，什么也不做。”
我说：“是的，而且他们只凭供给的伙食服役，并不像别人那样在伙食之外另得报酬。因此，他们即使想自费出游也办不到，不能给恋人送礼，不能像那些被认为幸福的人一样，随自己的心愿在其他方面花钱。这些以及许多类似的指责，你还没有说到呢。”
他说：“好，那就把这些也算上。”
english: exactly like hired mercenaries, with nothing to do but keep guard.” “Yes,” said I, “and what is more, they serve for board-wages and do not even receive pay in addition to their food as others do, so that they will not even be able to take a journey on their own account, if they wish to, or make presents to their mistresses, or spend money in other directions according to their desires like the men who are thought to be happy. These and many similar counts of the indictment you are omitting.” “Well,” said he, “assume these counts too.”

chinese:
“那么，你是在问，我们该怎样答辩？”
“是的。”
“我想，循着原来的道路，我们就能找到回答。我们会说，这些人以这样的方式生活，即使成为最幸福的人，也不值得我们惊讶。不过，我们建立城邦时着眼的目标，并不是使某一个阶层格外幸福，而是使整个城邦尽可能幸福。我们认为，在这样组织起来的城邦中，最有可能找到正义，正如在治理最坏的城邦中可以找到不正义；
english: “What then will be our apology you ask?” “Yes.” “By following the same path I think we shall find what to reply. For we shall say that while it would not surprise us if these men thus living prove to be the most happy, yet the object on which we fixed our eyes in the establishment of our state was not the exceptional happiness of any one class but the greatest possible happiness of the city as a whole. For we thought that in a state so constituted we should be most likely to discover justice as we should injustice

chinese: 辨清了两者，我们就能裁定这场长久探究的问题。因此，我们首先要做的，是塑造一个幸福城邦的模型；我们没有在其中单独划出一个小阶层，规定它必须幸福，而是要求整个城邦幸福。至于相反的城邦，我们稍后再来考察。譬如我们正在给一尊雕像着色，有个人走过来批评，说我们没有把最漂亮的颜料用在雕像最漂亮的部分，因为眼睛是最美的部分，我们却把它涂成黑色，而没有涂成紫色——
english: in the worst governed state, and that when we had made these out we could pass judgement on the issue of our long inquiry. Our first task then, we take it, is to mold the model of a happy state—we are not isolating a small class in it and postulating their happiness, but that of the city as a whole. But the opposite type of state we will consider presently. It is as if we were coloring a statue and someone approached and censured us, saying that we did not apply the most beautiful pigments to the most beautiful parts of the image, since the eyes, which are the most beautiful part, have not been painted with purple but with black—

chinese: 我们会认为，下面的答复是合理的：朋友，不要指望我们把眼睛涂得美得完全不像眼睛，也不要对其他部分作这样的要求。你应当考察，我们是否给每个部分配上了适合它的颜色，从而使整体美好。因此，在眼前的事情上，你也不能要求我们给卫士附加一种幸福，结果让他们变成什么都可以，却偏偏不再是卫士。
english: we should think it a reasonable justification to reply, ‘Don’t expect us, quaint friend, to paint the eyes so fine that they will not be like eyes at all, nor the other parts. But observe whether by assigning what is proper to each we render the whole beautiful.’ And so in the present case you must not require us to attach to the guardians a happiness that will make them anything but guardians.

chinese: 同样，我们也可以让农民穿上华服、佩戴黄金，吩咐他们高兴时才去耕田；可以让陶工在炉火旁依次斜躺在宴榻上，饮酒祝颂、尽情吃喝，把陶轮放在身边，想做陶器时才动一动。我们也可以用这种办法让其他所有人幸福，于是整个城邦都幸福了。但你不要劝我们这样做，
english:
For in like manner we could clothe the farmers in robes of state and deck them with gold and bid them cultivate the soil at their pleasure, and we could make the potters recline on couches from left to right before the fire drinking toasts and feasting with their wheel alongside to potter with when they are so disposed, and we can make all the others happy in the same fashion, so that thus the entire city may be happy.”

But urge us not to this,

chinese: 因为一旦听从这种劝告，农民就不再是农民，陶工不再是陶工，组成城邦的其他各类人也都不能保持各自的本分。不过，对其他人来说，事情还没有那么严重。鞋匠即使变坏、被惯坏，冒充自己已经不是的工匠，对城邦也不构成很大的危险。可是，法律和城邦的卫士如果只是看起来像卫士，实际却不是，你要知道，他们会把整个城邦彻底毁掉；另一方面，也唯有他们，才对城邦的良好治理和幸福起决定作用。因此，如果我们正在培养真正的卫士，
english: since, if we yield, the farmer will not be a farmer nor the potter a potter, nor will any other of the types that constitute state keep its form. However, for the others it matters less. For cobblers who deteriorate and are spoiled and pretend to be the workmen that they are not are no great danger to a state. But guardians of laws and of the city who are not what they pretend to be, but only seem, destroy utterly, I would have you note, the entire state, and on the other hand, they alone are decisive of its good government and happiness. If then we are forming true guardians

chinese: 培养自由的守护者、最不可能损害共同体的人，而赞同另一种理想的人心目中想的，却是农民和幸福的宴饮者，仿佛大家聚在节庆场合而不是公民共同体，那么，他所想的就是别的东西，而不是城邦。你应当考虑，我们设置卫士，究竟是为了让他们自身得到尽可能大的幸福，还是要看整个城邦能否产生这种幸福；至于这些辅助者和卫士，
english: and keepers of our liberties, men least likely to harm the commonwealth, but the proponent of the other ideal is thinking of farmers and ‘happy’ feasters as it were in a festival and not in a civic community, he would have something else in mind than a state. Consider, then, whether our aim in establishing the guardians is the greatest possible happiness among them or whether that is something we must look to see develop in the city as a whole, but these helpers and guardians

chinese:
则应当用约束和劝导，使他们去做那些能让自己在本职工作中成为最好工匠的事情；其余的人也都一样。这样，当整个城邦发展起来，得到良好安排时，就让每个阶层享有与其本性相称的那一份幸福。”
他说：“好，我认为你说得对。”
我说：“那么，对于与此相关的另一点，你也会认为我说得有道理吗？”
“是什么？”
“你来考察，
english:
are to be constrained and persuaded to do what will make them the best craftsmen in their own work, and similarly all the rest. And so, as the entire city develops and is ordered well, each class is to be left, to the share of happiness that its nature comports.”

“Well,” he said, “I think you are right.” “And will you then,” I said, “also think me reasonable in another point akin to this?” “What pray?” “Consider whether

chinese:
其他工匠也是否会被下面这两种原因败坏，以至于把手艺完全毁掉。”
“哪两种原因？”
我说：“财富和贫穷。”
“怎么回事？”
“是这样：你认为一个陶工富裕起来以后，还愿意用心钻研自己的手艺吗？”
他说：“完全不会。”
“他会变得比从前更加懒惰、更加疏忽吗？”
“会懒散得多。”
“这样，他就成了一个更差的陶工？”
“而且差得多。”
“反过来，如果他因为贫穷，置办不起工具和从事这门技艺所需的其他东西，
english: these are the causes that corrupt other craftsmen too so as positively to spoil them.” “What causes?” “Wealth and poverty,” said I. “How so?” “Thus! do you think a potter who grew rich would any longer be willing to give his mind to his craft?” “By no means,” said he. “But will he become more idle and negligent than he was?” “Far more.” “Then he becomes a worse potter?” “Far worse too.” “And yet again, if from poverty he is unable to provide himself with tools and other requirements of his art,

chinese:
他的作品就会更差；由他教出来的儿子或其他人，也会成为较差的工匠。”
“当然。”
“那么，无论贫穷还是财富，都会使技艺的产品变坏，也使工匠变坏？”
“看来如此。”
“看来，我们的卫士又有一类事情必须防备了，要尽一切力量，不让它们在自己毫不知情时溜进城邦。”
“是什么？”
english: the work that he turns out will be worse, and he will also make inferior workmen of his sons or any others whom he teaches.” “Of course.” “From both causes, then, poverty and wealth, the products of the arts deteriorate, and so do the artisans?” “So it appears.” “Here, then, is a second group of things it seems that our guardians must guard against and do all in their power to keep from slipping into the city without their knowledge.” “What are they?”

chinese:
我说：“财富和贫穷。前者带来奢侈、懒惰和变乱；后者除了变乱，还带来卑陋和手艺低劣的弊病。”
他说：“确实如此。不过，苏格拉底，这里有一点你得想想：我们的城邦没有财富，怎样能够作战？尤其是当它不得不与一个强大而富有的城邦交战时。”
我说：“显然，同一个这样的城邦作战会相当困难，但同两个作战反而容易些。”
english: “Wealth and poverty,” said I, “since the one brings luxury, idleness and innovation, and the other illiberality and the evil of bad workmanship in addition to innovation.” “Assuredly,” he said; “yet here is a point for your consideration, Socrates, how our city, possessing no wealth, will be able to wage war, especially if compelled to fight a large and wealthy state.” “Obviously,” said I, “it would be rather difficult to fight one such, but easier to fight two.”

chinese:
他说：“这是什么意思？”
我说：“你先告诉我：如果他们不得不打仗，他们是不是以受过训练的战争选手的身份，同富人作战？”
他说：“是的，这倒是真的。”
“那么，阿德曼托斯，请回答我：一个技艺上训练充分的拳击手，能不能轻易地同两个不懂拳击的肥胖富人对打？”
他说：“如果同时打两个，也许不行。”
我说：“即使准许他后退，
english: “What did you mean by that?” he said. “Tell me first,” I said, “whether, if they have to fight, they will not be fighting as athletes of war against men of wealth?” “Yes, that is true,” he said. “Answer me then, Adeimantus. Do you not think that one boxer perfectly trained in the art could easily fight two fat rich men who knew nothing of it?” “Not at the same time perhaps,” said he. “Not even,” said I, “if he were allowed to retreat

chinese:
再转身击打先追上来的那一个，而且在烈日和闷热之中反复这样做，也不行吗？这样的拳击手，难道不能打倒好几个这样的对手？”
他说：“当然；他真能做到，也不足为奇。”
“那么，你是否认为，富人在拳击方面的技巧和练习，比他们在战争技艺方面的还要多？”
他说：“我认为是的。”
“于是，我们这些受过训练的选手，很可能能够轻易地与两倍、三倍于自己的人交战。”
他说：“我只好承认这一点，因为我相信你说得对。”
english: and then turn and strike the one who came up first, and if he repeated the procedure many times under a burning and stifling sun? Would not such a fighter down even a number of such opponents?” “Doubtless,” he said; “it wouldn’t be surprising if he did.” “Well, don’t you think that the rich have more of the skill and practice of boxing than of the art of war?” “I do,” he said. “It will be easy, then, for our athletes in all probability to fight with double and triple their number.” “I shall have to concede the point,” he said, “for I believe you are right.”

chinese:
“再说，如果他们派使者到另一个城邦，说出实际的情形：我们不使用金银，法律也不准我们使用，你们却可以；那么请与我们共同作战，敌人的战利品都归你们——你认为，听到这样一个建议，还有谁会选择同强健精瘦的猎犬作战，而不借助猎犬去对付肥嫩的羊群？”
“我想不会。”
“不过，还得想一想：如果把其他城邦的全部财富，
english: “Well then, if they send an embassy to the other city and say what is in fact true: ‘We make no use of gold and silver nor is it lawful for us but it is for you: do you then join us in the war and keep the spoils of the enemy,’—do you suppose any who heard such a proposal would choose to fight against hard and wiry hounds rather than with the aid of the hounds against fat and tender sheep?” “I think not.” “Yet consider whether the accumulation

chinese:
都集中在一个城邦里，会不会危及这个没有财富的城邦？”
我说：“你真是天真得可爱，竟以为除了我们正在建立的城邦以外，其他任何一个也能恰当地称作一个城邦。”
他说：“为什么？那我们该怎么称呼？”
我说：“对它们必须使用复数的说法。因为它们每一个都是许多个城邦，而不是一个，正如那个游戏里所说的那样。至少有两个相互敌对的城邦：富人的城邦
english:
of all the wealth of other cities in one does not involve danger for the state that has no wealth.” “What happy innocence,” said I, “to suppose that you can properly use the name city of any other than the one we are constructing.” “Why, what should we say?” he said. “A greater predication,” said I, “must be applied to the others. For they are each one of them many cities, not a city, as it goes in the game.”

There are two at the least at enmity with one another, the city of the rich

chinese: 和穷人的城邦；而这两个内部，又各有许多个。如果你把它们当作一个来对待，就完全弄错了；如果当作许多个，向一个派别许诺另一个派别的财产、权力，甚至他们的人身，你就总会敌人少、盟友多。只要你的城邦始终遵照我们刚定下的秩序，实行有节制的治理，它就会是最强大的城邦。我说的并不是名声上最大，而是实际上最大，即使它只有一千名防卫者。因为一个具有这种规模、
english: and the city of the poor, and in each of these there are many. If you deal with them as one you will altogether miss the mark, but if you treat them as a multiplicity by offering to the one faction the property, the power, the very persons of the other, you will continue always to have few enemies and many allies. And so long as your city is governed soberly in the order just laid down, it will be the greatest of cities. I do not mean greatest in repute, but in reality, even though it have only a thousand defenders. For a city of this size

chinese:
又真正统一的城邦，你无论在希腊人还是其他民族中，都不容易找到；至于徒具统一外表的，你却会找到许多，它们的规模还大上很多倍。还是说，你的看法不同？”
他说：“不，我的看法确实相同。”
“那么，这岂不是我们统治者规定城邦适当规模的最好尺度和准则？他们应当划出与这种规模相称的领土，不再寻求更多。”
“这个尺度是什么？”
我说：“我认为，只要城邦在成长时还愿意保持统一，就让它成长；超过这点就不行。”
english:
that is really one you will not easily discover either among Greeks or barbarians—but of those that seem so you will find many and many times the size of this. Or do you think otherwise?” “No, indeed I don’t,” said he.

“Would not this, then, be the best rule and measure for our governors of the proper size of the city and of the territory that they should mark off for a city of that size and seek no more?” “What is the measure?” “I think,” said I, “that they should let it grow so long as in its growth it consents to remain a unity, but no further.”

chinese:
他说：“很好。”
“那么，我们是不是还该给卫士加上这样一项嘱咐：想尽办法守护城邦，使它既不过小，也不只是外表庞大，而是规模充分，并且统一？”
他说：“这项嘱咐，对他们来说也许容易做到。”
我说：“还有一项，也许比这个更容易，就是我们先前说过的：如果卫士生下禀赋低劣的孩子，就必须把他送到其他阶层去；
english: “Excellent,” he said. “Then is not this still another injunction that we should lay upon our guardians, to keep guard in every way that the city shall not be too small, nor great only in seeming, but that it shall be a sufficient city and one?” “That behest will perhaps be an easy one for them,” he said. “And still easier, haply,” I said, “is this that we mentioned before when we said that if a degenerate offspring was born to the guardians he must be sent away to the other classes,

chinese:
同样，如果其他阶层生下禀赋优越的孩子，就必须把他编入卫士之中。这些话的用意，也包括其余公民应被安排从事适合他们天性的工作，一人一职，好让每个人履行自己的功能，成为一个人而不是许多个人；整个城邦也因此成为统一体，而不是许多彼此分离的部分。”
他说：“是啊，这比上一项还算小事。”
我说：“好阿德曼托斯，我们加给他们的，并不像人们以为的那样，是许多困难的嘱咐，
english: and likewise if a superior to the others he must be enrolled among the guardians; and the purport of all this was that the other citizens too must be sent to the task for which their natures were fitted, one man to one work, in order that each of them fulfilling his own function may be not many men, but one, and so the entire city may come to be not a multiplicity but a unity.” “Why yes,” he said, “this is even more trifling than that.” “These are not, my good Adeimantus, as one might suppose, numerous and difficult injunctions that

chinese:
而都是容易的，只要他们守住人们所说的那一件大事——或者，不说大事，就说足以成事的一件吧。”
他说：“是什么？”
我回答：“他们的教育和养育。因为，如果正确的教育使他们成为明理的人，那么这类事情，他们就都容易自己发现；还有一些我们现在略而不谈的原则，例如妻子、婚姻、
english:
we are imposing upon them, but they are all easy, provided they guard, as the saying is, the one great thing—or instead of great let us call it sufficient.” “What is that?” he said.

“Their education and nurture,” I replied. “For if a right education makes of them reasonable men they will easily discover everything of this kind—and other principles that we now pass over, as that the possession of wives and marriage,

chinese:
孩子的生育，以及所有诸如此类的事情，都应尽可能按照那句谚语，成为朋友共有的东西。”
他说：“是的，那样最好。”
我说：“而且，城邦一旦有了良好的开端，就会仿佛沿着一个循环不断成长。我是说，良好的养育和教育，如果能维持下去，就会在城邦里造就良好的天性；良好天性的人再接受这样的教育，就会成长得比前人更好，
english: and the procreation of children and all that sort of thing should be made as far as possible the proverbial goods of friends that are common.” “Yes, that would be the best way,” he said. “And, moreover,” said I, “the state, if it once starts well, proceeds as it were in a cycle of growth. I mean that a sound nurture and education if kept up creates good natures in the state, and sound natures in turn receiving an education of this sort develop into better men than their predecessors

chinese:
既更适合其他工作，也更能生育优良的后代，正如其他动物的情形一样。”
他说：“很可能。”
我说：“因此，简要说来，城邦的监督者必须牢牢把握这一点，提防它在不知不觉间败坏。他们必须处处警惕违背既定秩序的诗乐与体育革新，尽其所能防止这种事情。当听见有人说：
‘人们最为赞赏的歌，
是歌者唇边最新流转的那一首。’（《奥德赛》1.351）
他们应当戒备，
english:
both for other purposes and for the production of offspring as among animals also.” “It is probable,” he said. “To put it briefly, then,” said I, “it is to this that the overseers of our state must cleave and be watchful against its insensible corruption. They must throughout be watchful against innovations in music and gymnastics counter to the established order, and to the best of their power guard against them, fearing when anyone says that ‘
That song is most regarded among men
Which hovers newest on the singer’s lips, ’

chinese:
免得有人误以为，诗人赞美的不是新的歌曲，而是一种新的歌唱方式。我们不能赞美这一类事情，也不该认定这就是诗人的意思。音乐变成一种新的类型，是必须警惕的事情，因为它关系到我们全部的命运。音乐的调式从来不会改变而不动摇最根本的政治和社会规范；达蒙这样说，我也深信如此。”
阿德曼托斯说：“把我也算在深信这一点的人中吧。”
english: lest haply it be supposed that the poet means not new songs but a new way of song and is commending this. But we must not praise that sort of thing nor conceive it to be the poet’s meaning. For a change to a new type of music is something to beware of as a hazard of all our fortunes. For the modes of music are never disturbed without unsettling of the most fundamental political and social conventions, as Damon affirms and as I am convinced.” “Set me too down in the number of the convinced,” said Adeimantus.

chinese:
我说：“那么，看来，我们的卫士必须在这里，在诗乐之中，建立他们的哨所和岗亭。”
他说：“确实，这种不守法度的风气，很容易不被察觉地混进来。”
我说：“是啊，因为人们以为它不过是一种游戏，不会造成伤害。”
他说：“它也确实不会造成别的伤害，不过是逐渐渗透，悄悄漫入人的性格和活动；再从那里长大，侵袭人与人的事务往来；又从这些关系出发，
english: “It is here, then,” I said, “in music, as it seems, that our guardians must build their guard-house and post of watch.” “It is certain,” he said, “that this is the kind of lawlessness that easily insinuates itself unobserved.” “Yes,” said I, “because it is supposed to be only a form of play and to work no harm.” “Nor does it work any,” he said, “except that by gradual infiltration it softly overflows upon the characters and pursuits of men and from these issues forth grown greater to attack their business dealings, and from these relations

chinese:
苏格拉底，肆意地侵犯法律和政制，最终颠覆一切公共和私人的事务。”
我说：“那么，事情就是这样吗？”
他说：“我想是的。”
“所以，正如我们一开始所说，年轻人必须参加更守法度的游戏。因为，如果游戏不守法度，孩子们也同样不守法度，
english:
it proceeds against the laws and the constitution with wanton licence, Socrates, till finally it overthrows all things public and private.” “Well,” said I, “are these things so?” “I think so,” he said.

“Then, as we were saying in the beginning, our youth must join in a more law-abiding play, since, if play grows lawless and the children likewise,

chinese:
他们就不可能成长为性情严肃、具有守法精神的人。”
他说：“当然。”
“由此我们可以推想：当孩子们在最初的游戏中，通过诗乐浸染了法律和秩序的精神，就会发生与先前设想相反的结果。这种精神在一切事情上伴随着他们，扶助他们成长，并把在另一种城邦中被毁坏的东西恢复、重新建立起来。”
他说：“的确。”
“那么，这样的人就会自己重新发现那些看起来微不足道、却被前人全部废弃的惯例。”
“哪一类惯例？”
“例如，
english: it is impossible that they should grow up to be men of serious temper and lawful spirit.” “Of course,” he said. “And so we may reason that when children in their earliest play are imbued with the spirit of law and order through their music, the opposite of the former supposition happens—this spirit waits upon them in all things and fosters their growth, and restores and sets up again whatever was overthrown in the other type of state.” “True, indeed,” he said. “Then such men rediscover for themselves those seemingly trifling conventions which their predecessors abolished altogether.” “Of what sort?” “Such things as

chinese:
年轻人在长者面前适当地保持安静，为长者让路，在长者面前起立，尽心侍奉父母；还有头发的修剪、衣服的式样、鞋履的款式，以及整个身体的举止，一切诸如此类的事情。你不这样认为吗？”
“我认为是的。”
“不过，把这些制定成法律，我想却是愚蠢的。因为这样的法律，只在口头和纸上制定出来，人们不会遵守，也不能持久。”
“怎么可能持久呢？”
我说：“总之，阿德曼托斯，一个人最初所受教育的方向，很可能决定
english: the becoming silence of the young in the presence of their elders; the giving place to them and rising up before them, and dutiful service of parents, and the cut of the hair and the garments and the fashion of the foot-gear, and in general the deportment of the body and everything of the kind. Don’t you think so?” “I do.” “Yet to enact them into laws would, I think, be silly. For such laws are not obeyed nor would they last, being enacted only in words and on paper.” “How could they?” “At any rate, Adeimantus,” I said, “the direction of the education from whence one starts is likely to determine

chinese:
后来发展的性质。相似的东西，不是总会招来相似的东西吗？”
“当然。”
“我想，我们会说，最后形成的结果，是一个完整而强有力的善的整体，或者它的反面。”
他说：“当然。”
我说：“因此，就我而言，正是由于这些理由，我不愿再试着为此类事情立法。”
他说：“很有道理。”
我说：“可是，天哪，事务往来又怎样呢？人们在集市上相互进行的交易——
english: the quality of what follows. Does not like ever summon like?” “Surely.” “And the final outcome, I presume, we would say is one complete and vigorous product of good or the reverse.” “Of course,” said he. “For my part, then,” I said, “for these reasons I would not go on to try to legislate on such matters.” “With good reason,” said he. “But what, in heaven’s name,” said I, “about business matters, the deals that men make with one another in the agora—

chinese:
还有，如果你愿意，也包括同工匠订立的契约，对辱骂和殴打提出的诉讼，起诉书的提交，陪审员的选任，在集市和港口缴付、征收必要的费用，以及一般的市场、城市治安、港口管理等条例，我们该着手为这些事情立法吗？”
他说：“不，向品行端正的人下达这样的命令并不合适。我想，这些事情所需的大多数规定，他们自己很容易发现。”
english: and, if you please, contracts with workmen and actions for foul language and assault, the filing of declarations, the impanelling of juries, the payment and exaction of any dues that may be needful in markets or harbors and in general market, police or harbor regulations and the like, can we bring ourselves to legislate about these?” “Nay, ʼtwould not be fitting,” he said, “to dictate to good and honorable men. For most of the enactments that are needed about these things they will easily, I presume, discover.”

chinese:
“是的，朋友，只要神赐予他们力量，让他们保存住我们已经讨论过的那些立法原则。”
他说：“不然的话，他们就会一生不停地增加、修改这些琐细的法律，指望由此达到最好的结果。”
我说：“你的意思是，这样的公民过的生活，就像那些患着病，却因为缺少节制而不愿放弃有害生活方式的人一样。”
english: “Yes, my friend, provided God grants them the preservation of the principles of law that we have already discussed.” “Failing that,” said he, “they will pass their lives multiplying such petty laws and amending them in the expectation of attaining what is best.” “You mean,” said I, “that the life of such citizens will resemble that of men who are sick, yet from intemperance are unwilling to abandon their unwholesome regimen.”

chinese:
“完全一样。”
我说：“这些人做起事来，确实有趣极了。他们不停地求医，除了把疾病弄得更加复杂、更加严重以外，什么也做不到。可他们总还希望，有人能推荐一种包治百病的药，使自己恢复健康。”
他说：“你把这类病人的情形说得太准了。”
“他们还有一种很有趣的脾气，不是吗？他们最恨的，恰恰是对自己说实话的人：一个人只要不停止酗酒、暴食、纵欲
english: “By all means.” “And truly,” said I, “these latter go on in a most charming fashion. For with all their doctoring they accomplish nothing except to complicate and augment their maladies. And they are always hoping that some one will recommend a panacea that will restore their health.” “A perfect description,” he said, “of the state of such invalids.” “And isn’t this a charming trait in them, that they hate most in all the world him who tells them the truth that until a man stops drinking and gorging and wenching

chinese:
和懒散，无论药物、烧灼、手术，甚至咒语和护符，都不会对他有用。”
他说：“这可不能全算有趣；向说得对的人发怒，既不文雅，也不可爱。”
我说：“看来，你并不欣赏这种人。”
“是的，天哪，我不欣赏。”
“那么，如果整个城邦也像我们刚才所说的那样行事，你也不会赞同吧？你不觉得，这类病人的做法，恰好就是某些城邦的做法吗？
english:
and idling, neither drugs nor cautery nor the knife, no, nor spells nor periapts will be of any avail?” “Not altogether charming,” he said, “for there is no grace or charm in being angry with him who speaks well.” “You do not seem to be an admirer of such people,” said I. “No, by heaven, I am not.”

“Neither then, if an entire city, as we were just now saying, acts in this way, will it have your approval, or don’t you think that the way of such invalids is precisely that of those cities

chinese:
这些城邦治理不善，却预先警告公民，不许触动城邦的整体政制，谁敢尝试就处死谁；然而，谁能最投其所好地为这种治理服务，向它献媚，迎合它的欲望，并巧妙地使它满足，它就把谁看作好人，看作在重大事情上有智慧的人，并乐于给他荣誉。”
他说：“是的，我认为两者的做法完全相同；我一点也不赞同。”
english: which being badly governed forewarn their citizens not to meddle with the general constitution of the state, denouncing death to whosoever attempts that—while whoever most agreeably serves them governed as they are and who curries favor with them by fawning upon them and anticipating their desires and by his cleverness in gratifying them, him they will account the good man, the man wise in worthwhile things, the man they will delight to honor?” “Yes,” he said, “I think their conduct is identical, and I don’t approve it in the very least.”

chinese:
“再说那些愿意并且热切地为这种城邦服务的人呢？你不佩服他们的勇气，以及那种轻松的不负责任吗？”
他说：“我佩服，不过有一种人例外：他们真的受了蒙骗，因为受大众赞扬，就以为自己确实是政治家。”
“你这是什么意思？你不能体谅这些人吗？一个人本来不懂测量，周围一大群同样不懂的人，却一致断言他有四肘高，
english: “And what again of those who are willing and eager to serve such states? Don’t you admire their valiance and light-hearted irresponsibility?” “I do,” he said, “except those who are actually deluded and suppose themselves to be in truth statesmen because they are praised by the many.” “What do you mean? Can’t you make allowances for the men? Do you think it possible for a man who does not know how to measure when a multitude of others equally ignorant assure him that he is four cubits tall

chinese:
你认为他能不相信自己真有这么高吗？”
他说：“不能，我认为办不到。”
“那么，就别对他们太苛刻。他们制定、修改我们刚才所说的那种法律，总指望找到一个办法，消除商业以及我所说的其他事务里的欺诈，实在是世上最有趣的景象。他们看不见，自己其实是在试图砍掉九头蛇的一颗头。”
english: not to suppose this to be the fact about himself?” “Why no,” he said, “I don’t think that.” “Then don’t be harsh with them. For surely such fellows are the most charming spectacle in the world when they enact and amend such laws as we just now described and are perpetually expecting to find a way of putting an end to frauds in business and in the other matters of which I was speaking because they can’t see that they are in very truth trying to cut off a Hydra’s head.”

chinese:
他说：“确实，他们所做的正是如此。”
我说：“所以，我不认为真正的立法者应当在城邦的法律和政制中，费力规定这类事情，无论这个城邦治理得好还是坏。在治理坏的城邦中，这些规定没有用，什么也办不到；在治理好的城邦中，其中有些规定，任何人都能发现，其余的则会从我们已经描述过的生活实践中自然产生。”
english: “Indeed,” he said, “that is exactly what they are doing.” “I, then,” said I, “should not have supposed that the true lawgiver ought to work out matters of that kind in the laws and the constitution either of an ill-governed or a well-governed state—in the one because they are useless and accomplish nothing, in the other because some of them anybody could discover and others will result spontaneously from the pursuits already described.”

chinese:
他说：“那么，还有哪一部分立法留给我们？”
我回答：“没有什么留给我们了；不过，还有最重要、最美好、最首要的规定，要留给德尔斐的阿波罗。”
他说：“是什么？”
“建立神庙、举行祭献，以及敬奉神、神灵和英雄的其他仪式；还有安葬死者，以及为了让另一个世界的居民对我们友善，必须向他们履行的礼仪。
english: “What part of legislation, then,” he said, “is still left for us?” And I replied, “For us nothing, but for the Apollo of Delphi, the chief, the fairest and the first of enactments.” “What are they?” he said. “The founding of temples, and sacrifices, and other forms of worship of gods, daemons, and heroes; and likewise the burial of the dead and the services we must render to the dwellers in the world beyond to keep them gracious.

chinese:
因为，对这些事情，我们一无所知；如果我们明智，那么在建立城邦时，就不该把它们交给别的任何人，也不该采用祖先之神以外的其他解释者。这位神，坐在大地的中央、世界的脐部，给出自己的解释；在这些事情上，他为全人类解释祖传的宗教。”
他回答：“说得很好；我们就该这样做。”
english: For of such matters we neither know anything nor in the founding of our city if we are wise shall we entrust them to any other or make use of any other interpreter than the God of our fathers. For this God surely is in such matters for all mankind the interpreter of the religion of their fathers who from his seat in the middle and at the very navel of the earth delivers his interpretation.” “Excellently said,” he replied; “and that is what we must do.”

chinese:
我说：“那么，阿里斯顿之子，你的城邦终于可以算是建立起来了。接下来，我们得从哪里找来足够的光亮，由你亲自察看，也请你的兄弟、玻勒马霍斯和其余的人来帮忙，看能不能找出正义和不正义在这个城邦的什么地方，它们相互区别在哪里；还要看，一个想要幸福的人，究竟必须具有其中哪一种，无论所有神和人是否知道他的状况。”
格劳孔说：“别这样说，你答应过，要亲自继续这项寻找，
english: “At last, then, son of Ariston,” said I, “your city may be considered as established. The next thing is to procure a sufficient light somewhere and to look yourself, and call in the aid of your brother and of Polemarchus and the rest, if we may in any wise discover where justice and injustice should be in it, wherein they differ from one another and which of the two he must have who is to be happy, alike whether his condition is known or not known to all gods and men.” “Nonsense,” said Glaucon, “you promised that you would carry on the search yourself,

chinese:
而且承认，如果不尽一切力量援助正义，就是不虔敬的。”
我说：“你提醒得对，我必须这样做；不过，你们也必须帮忙。”
他说：“好，我们会的。”
我说：“我希望可以用下面的办法找到。我认为，我们的城邦如果确实建立得当，就应当在完整意义上是善的。”
他说：“必然如此。”
“那么，显然它应当是智慧、勇敢、节制而且正义的。”
“显然。”
“因此，如果我们在它之中找出了其中的某些品质，剩下的就是尚未找到的那一种？”
english: admitting that it would be impious for you not to come to the aid of justice by every means in your power.” “A true reminder,” I said, “and I must do so, but you also must lend a hand.” “Well,” he said, “we will.” “I expect then,” said I, “that we shall find it in this way. I think our city, if it has been rightly founded is good in the full sense of the word.” “Necessarily,” he said. “Clearly, then, it will be wise, brave, sober, and just.” “Clearly.” “Then if we find any of these qualities in it, the remainder will be that which we have not found?”

chinese:
“当然。”
“拿其他任意四种东西来说：如果我们在一个对象里寻找其中的一种，先认出了要找的东西，那就够了；但如果我们先认出了另外三种，这也会使我们知道所寻找的东西，因为显然，它只能是剩下的那一种。”
他说：“对。”
“所以，既然这些品质共有四种，我们也必须用同样的方法来寻找。”
“显然。”
“而且，
english: “Surely.” “Take the case of any four other things. If we were looking for any one of them in anything and recognized the object of our search first, that would have been enough for us, but if we had recognized the other three first, that in itself would have made known to us the thing we were seeking. For plainly there was nothing left for it to be but the remainder.” “Right,” he said. “And so, since these are four, we must conduct the search in the same way.” “Clearly.” “And, moreover,

chinese:
我想我首先清楚看见的是智慧；看来，这里有一点奇特。”
他说：“什么？”
“我想，我们所描述的城邦确实是智慧的，因为它善于谋划，对吗？”
“是的。”
“善于谋划本身，当然是一种知识。人们凭知识而不是无知，才能谋划得好。”
“显然。”
“可是，城邦中有许多种各不相同的知识或学问。”
“当然。”
“那么，一个城邦是不是由于其中木匠的知识，
english: the first thing that I think I clearly see therein is the wisdom, and there is something odd about that, it appears.” “What?” said he. “Wise in very deed I think the city that we have described is, for it is well counselled, is it not?” “Yes.” “And surely this very thing, good counsel, is a form of wisdom. For it is not by ignorance but by knowledge that men counsel well.” “Obviously.” “But there are many and manifold knowledges or sciences in the city.” “Of course.” “Is it then owing to the science of her carpenters that

chinese:
才被称为智慧、善于谋划的呢？”
“绝不是；凭那个，它只能叫作善于营造的城邦。”
“那么，城邦也不能因为懂得怎样把木制器具做得最好，而被称为智慧的？”
“不能，我同意。”
“是因为制造铜器的知识，或其他诸如此类的知识吗？”
他说：“都不是。”
“也不是因为懂得从土地上生产作物；凭那种知识，它得到的名称是善于农耕。”
“我想是的。”
我说：“那么，在我们刚建立的城邦中，是否有一种知识存在于某些公民那里，它所谋划的并不是城邦中的某一种特定事情，
english: a city is to be called wise and well advised?” “By no means for that, but rather mistress of the arts of building.” “Then a city is not to be styled wise because of the deliberations of the science of wooden utensils for their best production?” “No, I grant you.” “Is it, then, because of that of brass implements or any other of that kind?” “None whatsoever,” he said. “Nor yet because of the science of the production of crops from the soil, but the name it takes from that is agricultural.” “I think so.” “Then,” said I, “is there any science in the city just founded by us residing in any of its citizens which does not take counsel about some particular thing

chinese:
而是整个城邦，以及怎样改善城邦内部的关系和它同其他城邦的关系？”
“当然有。”
我说：“那是什么知识？存在于谁那里？”
“就是守护或治理的知识，存在于那些统治者那里；我们刚才把他们称为完整意义上的卫士。”
“那么，城邦由于这种知识，会得到什么称谓？”
他说：“善于谋划，而且真正智慧。”
我说：“那么，你认为，
english: in the city but about the city as a whole and the betterment of its relations with itself and other states?” “Why, there is.” “What is it,” said I, “and in whom is it found?” “It is the science of guardianship or government and it is to be found in those rulers to whom we just now gave the name of guardians in the full sense of the word.” “And what term then do you apply to the city because of this knowledge?” “Well advised,” he said, “and truly wise.” “Which class, then,” said I,

chinese:
在我们的城邦中，哪一类人数更多：金属工匠，还是这些真正的卫士？”
他说：“工匠多得多。”
“在所有具有专门知识、因而得到特定称谓的群体中，这些统治者是不是人数最少的一群？”
“少得多。”
“那么，一个依照自然原则建立的城邦，是凭它人数最少的阶层、最微小的部分，以及存在于这个领导和统治部分中的智慧，才使整个城邦成为智慧的。看来，
english:
“do you suppose will be the more numerous in our city, the smiths or these true guardians?” “The smiths, by far,” he said. “And would not these rulers be the smallest of all the groups of those who possess special knowledge and receive distinctive appellations?” “By far.”

“Then it is by virtue of its smallest class and minutest part of itself, and the wisdom that resides therein, in the part which takes the lead and rules, that a city established on principles of nature would be wise as a whole. And as it appears

chinese:
这一类人在本性上就是最少的；他们所分享的那种知识，在一切知识中，独有它配称为智慧。”
他说：“完全正确。”
“于是，我们不知怎么就找到了四种品质中的一种：它是什么，以及它在城邦中的位置。”
他说：“我当然认为，这一点已经找得足够清楚了。”
“再说，要看出勇敢是什么，以及它存在于城邦的哪个部分、城邦由此被称为勇敢，也没有困难。”
“怎么说？”
我说：“一个人，
english:
these are by nature the fewest, the class to which it pertains to partake of the knowledge which alone of all forms of knowledge deserves the name of wisdom.” “Most true,” he said. “This one of our four, then, we have, I know not how, discovered, the thing itself and its place in the state.” “I certainly think,” said he, “that it has been discovered sufficiently.”

“But again there is no difficulty in seeing bravery itself and the part of the city in which it resides for which the city is called brave.” “How so?” “Who,” said I,

chinese:
在把城邦称为怯懦或勇敢时，会把眼光放在除保卫城邦、为它作战的部分以外的其他地方吗？”
他说：“绝不会。”
我说：“我想，是因为其他居民的怯懦或勇敢，并不决定城邦具有哪一种品质。”
“不决定。”
“那么，城邦也是凭它的一部分而具有勇敢的，因为这一部分拥有一种品质，能在一切情况下保持这样一种信念：
english: “in calling a city cowardly or brave would fix his eyes on any other part of it than that which defends it and wages war in its behalf?” “No one at all,” he said. “For the reason, I take it,” said I, “that the cowardice or the bravery of the other inhabitants does not determine for it the one quality or the other.” “It does not.” “Bravery too, then, belongs to a city by virtue of a part of itself owing to its possession in that part of a quality that under all conditions will preserve the conviction

chinese:
应当害怕的，正是立法者在教育中教给他们的那些事物和那类事物。这是不是你所说的勇敢？”
他回答：“我没有完全听懂你的意思；请再说一遍。”
我说：“我所说的勇敢，是一种保持。”
“保持什么？”
“保持法律通过教育所确立的、关于可怕事物的信念：什么以及哪一类事情应当害怕。我说‘一切情况下’，是说勇敢的人在痛苦、
english: that things to be feared are precisely those which and such as the lawgiver inculcated in their education. Is not that what you call bravery?” “I don’t altogether understand what you said,” he replied; “but say it again.” “A kind of conservation,” I said, “is what I mean by bravery.” “What sort of a conservation?” “The conservation of the conviction which the law has created by education about fearful things—what and what sort of things are to be feared. And by the phrase ‘under all conditions’ I mean that the brave man preserves it both in pain

chinese:
快乐、欲望和恐惧中，都保持着它，不把它从灵魂中驱逐出去。如果你愿意，我可以用一个比喻说明。”
“我愿意。”
“你知道，染工要把羊毛染成不易褪色的紫色时，先从各种颜色的羊毛中挑选出白色的，然后认真地进行预处理，使它尽可能充分地着色。处理完毕后，只有在那时，才把它浸入染料。
english: and pleasures and in desires and fears and does not expel it from his soul. And I may illustrate it by a similitude if you please.” “I do.” “You are aware that dyers when they wish to dye wool so as to hold the purple hue begin by selecting from the many colors there be the one nature of the white and then give it a careful preparatory treatment so that it will take the hue in the best way, and after the treatment, then and then only, dip it in the dye.

chinese:
按照这种方法染过的东西，颜色就会牢固；无论用不用碱液洗涤，都不能洗掉它的色泽。但是，如果采取别的方法，无论把其他颜色的羊毛浸入染料，还是把白羊毛未经处理就浸入，你知道会怎样。”
他说：“我知道，颜色会褪掉，样子很可笑。”
我说：“那么，你可以用这个比喻来理解，我们在选拔战士、用诗乐
english:
And things that are dyed by this process become fast-colored and washing either with or without lyes cannot take away the sheen of their hues. But otherwise you know what happens to them, whether anyone dips other colors or even these without the preparatory treatment.” “I know,” he said, “that they present a ridiculous and washed-out appearance.”

“By this analogy, then,” said I, “you must conceive what we too to the best of our ability were doing when we selected our soldiers and educated them in music

chinese: 和身体训练教育他们时，正在尽力做什么。我们这样安排，唯一的目的，就是让他们被说服，像接受染料一样接受我们的法律；凭着合适的天性和养育，使他们关于应当害怕的事情以及一切其他事情的信念，都能牢牢着色，不被那些具有可怕洗涤力量的碱液洗掉。其中，快乐比任何洗涤剂或清洁剂
english: and exercises of the body. The sole aim of our contrivance was that they should be convinced and receive our laws like a dye as it were, so that their belief and faith might be fast-colored both about the things that are to be feared and all other things because of the fitness of their nature and nurture, and that so their dyes might not be washed out by those lyes that have such dread power to scour our faiths away, pleasure more potent than any detergent or abstergent

chinese:
更有力量，痛苦、恐惧和欲望也比任何碱液更有效。因此，我把灵魂中的这种力量——始终不失地保持关于什么应当害怕、什么不应当害怕的正确而合乎法律的信念——称为勇敢，也愿意把它当作勇敢，除非你有不同的意见。”
他说：“没有，完全没有。我想，对于同样的事情，如果只是未经教育而形成的正确意见，例如可能在野兽或奴隶身上出现的那一种，你会认为它同法律几乎没有关系，甚至毫无关系，也会给它另一个名称，而不叫勇敢。”
english: to accomplish this, and pain and fear and desire more sure than any lye. This power in the soul, then, this unfailing conservation of right and lawful belief about things to be and not to be feared is what I call and would assume to be courage, unless you have something different to say.” “No, nothing,” said he; “for I presume that you consider mere right opinion about the same matters not produced by education, that which may manifest itself in a beast or a slave, to have little or nothing to do with law and that you would call it by another name than courage.”

chinese:
我说：“完全正确。”
他说：“那么，我接受这个，认为它就是勇敢。”
我说：“接受吧，不过要有所限定：这是公民的勇敢。这样你就说对了。另找一个时候，如果你愿意，我们可以把它讨论得更充分。现在我们寻找的不是这个，而是正义；为这项探究，我相信我们已经做得足够了。”
他说：“你说得很对。”
english: “That is most true,” said I. “Well then,” he said, “I accept this as bravery.” “Do so,” said I, “and you will be right with the reservation that it is the courage of a citizen. Some other time, if it please you, we will discuss it more fully. At present we were not seeking this but justice; and for the purpose of that inquiry I believe we have done enough.” “You are quite right,” he said.

chinese:
我说：“我们还得在城邦里辨明两样东西：节制，以及整个探究所寻找的正义。”
“正是。”
“要是有一个办法，能使我们不必再费心考察节制，就找到正义，那就好了。”
他说：“就我而言，我既不知道有这样的办法，也不希望先找到正义，如果那意味着我们就不继续考察节制。倘若你愿意使我高兴，请先考察这个，再考察那个。”
我说：“我如果不愿意，
english: “Two things still remain,” said I, “to make out in our city, soberness and the object of the whole inquiry, justice.” “Quite so.” “If there were only some way to discover justice so that we need not further concern ourselves about soberness.” “Well, I, for my part,” he said, “neither know of any such way nor would I wish justice to be discovered first if that means that we are not to go on to the consideration of soberness. But if you desire to please me, consider this before that.” “It would certainly

chinese:
那实在太不应该了。”
他说：“那就继续探究吧。”
我回答：“必须继续。从眼下看来，它比其他德性更像一种协调与和谐。”
“怎么说？”
“节制是一种美好的秩序，是对某些快乐和欲望的控制。人们使用‘自己的主人’这个说法来描述它，虽然我不知道他们究竟怎样理解；还有一些类似说法，仿佛也把我们引向同一条线索。是不是这样？”
“当然。”
“可是，‘自己的主人’这个说法岂不有些荒唐？做自己主人的人，也就是受自己支配的人，
english:
be very wrong of me not to desire it,” said I. “Go on with the inquiry then,” he said. “I must go on,” I replied, “and viewed from here it bears more likeness to a kind of concord and harmony than the other virtues did.” “How so?” “Soberness is a kind of beautiful order and a continence of certain pleasures and appetites, as they say, using the phrase ‘master of himself’ I know not how; and there are other similar expressions that as it were point us to the same trail. Is that not so?” “Most certainly.”

“Now the phrase ‘master of himself’ is an absurdity, is it not? For he who is master of himself would also be subject to himself,

chinese:
受自己支配的人，也就是自己的主人，因为这些说法指的都是同一个人。”
“当然。”
我说：“不过，在我看来，这种说法想表达的是：一个人的灵魂内部有较好的部分，也有较坏的部分；所谓自我掌握，就是由本性上较好的部分控制较坏的部分。无论如何，这是一个赞美的词。但如果由于不良养育或某种交往，较少的较好部分被数量众多的较坏部分支配，我想，我们的言语
english: and he who is subject to himself would be master. For the same person is spoken of in all these expressions.” “Of course.” “But,” said I, “the intended meaning of this way of speaking appears to me to be that the soul of a man within him has a better part and a worse part, and the expression self-mastery means the control of the worse by the naturally better part. It is, at any rate, a term of praise. But when, because of bad breeding or some association, the better part, which is the smaller, is dominated by the multitude of the worse, I think that our speech

chinese:
就会把它当作可耻的事来责备，把处于这种情形的人称为不能自制、放纵无度的人。”
他说：“看来如此。”
我说：“现在，把眼光转向我们新建的城邦，你会发现其中存在着两种情形中的一种。如果较好者统治较坏者，就应该叫作节制、自我掌握，那么你会说，把我们的城邦称为自己的主人，是恰当的。”
他说：“我正在察看；确实如你所说。”
“此外，各种纷杂的
english: censures this as a reproach, and calls the man in this plight unselfcontrolled and licentious.” “That seems likely,” he said. “Turn your eyes now upon our new city,” said I, “and you will find one of these conditions existent in it. For you will say that it is justly spoken of as master of itself if that in which the superior rules the inferior is to be called sober and self-mastered.” “I do turn my eyes upon it,” he said, “and it is as you say.” “And again, the mob of motley

chinese:
欲望、快乐和痛苦，主要见于孩子、女人、奴隶，以及那些徒具自由人名义的卑下群众之中。”
“完全如此。”
“而那些简单、适度的欲望，能够在理性和正确意见的帮助下，由思量来引导的，你只会在少数人身上见到；他们有最好的天性，也受过最好的教育。”
他说：“确实。”
“在你的城邦里，难道不也能看见这种情形吗？人数众多的群众的欲望，
english: appetites and pleasures and pains one would find chiefly in children and women and slaves and in the base rabble of those who are freemen in name.” “By all means.” “But the simple and moderate appetites which with the aid of reason and right opinion are guided by consideration you will find in few and those the best born and best educated.” “True,” he said. “And do you not find this too in your city and a domination there of the desires

chinese:
受到少数较好者的欲望和智慧的支配。”
他说：“我看得见。”
“那么，如果有哪一个城邦配称为快乐和欲望的主人，配称为能够自我掌握的，这个城邦就当得起这个名称。”
他说：“完全当得起。”
“在这些方面，它不也应该叫作节制的吗？”
他说：“确实。”
“再说，如果有哪一个城邦，
english:
in the multitude and the rabble by the desires and the wisdom that dwell in the minority of the better?” “I do,” he said.

“If, then, there is any city that deserves to be described as master of its pleasures and desires and self-mastered, this one merits that designation.” “Most assuredly,” he said. “And is it not also to be called sober in all these respects?” “Indeed it is,” he said. “And yet again, if there is any city in which

chinese:
统治者和被统治者对于谁应当统治意见一致，那一定就是在这个城邦。你不这样认为吗？”
“我完全这样认为。”他说。
“那么，当他们处在这种状态时，你会说节制这种德性属于哪一类公民？属于统治者，还是被统治者？”
“我想两者都有。”他说。
“那么你看，”我说，“我们刚才把节制看成一种和谐，那个直觉不是没有道理吧？”
“为什么？”
“因为它的作用和勇敢、智慧不同。后两者各自存在于一个不同的部分，
english:
the rulers and the ruled are of one mind as to who ought to rule, that condition will be found in this. Don’t you think so?” “I most emphatically do,” he said. “In which class of the citizens, then, will you say that the virtue of soberness has its seat when this is their condition? In the rulers or in the ruled?” “In both, I suppose,” he said. “Do you see then,” said I, “that our intuition was not a bad one just now that discerned a likeness between soberness and a kind of harmony?” “Why so?”

“Because its operation is unlike that of courage and wisdom, which residing in separate parts

chinese: 分别使城邦成为智慧的和勇敢的。节制却不是这样：它确实贯穿整个音阶，使最强者、最弱者和居中者同唱一个调子；这里的强弱，无论按智慧衡量，还是你愿意的话按力量衡量，或者按人数、财富以及其他类似标准衡量，都是如此。所以，把这种一致称为节制，是十分恰当的：它是天性上较优的部分和较劣的部分
english: respectively made the city, the one wise and the other brave. That is not the way of soberness, but it extends literally through the entire gamut throughout, bringing about the unison in the same chant of the strongest, the weakest and the intermediate, whether in wisdom or, if you please, in strength, or for that matter in numbers, wealth, or any similar criterion. So that we should be quite right in affirming this unanimity to be soberness, the concord of the naturally superior and inferior

chinese:
对于谁应当统治的一致意见，无论在城邦还是在个人中都是这样。”
“我完全同意。”他说。
“很好，”我说，“依照我们目前所能作出的判断，我们已经在城邦中辨认出这三种德性。那么，赋予城邦另一种德性的那个剩余者，究竟是什么？因为显然，剩下的就是正义。”
“显然。”
“那么，格劳孔，现在我们该像猎人一样，把猎物藏身的灌木丛围住，仔细守望，免得正义溜走，从我们的眼前
english: as to which ought to rule both in the state and the individual.” “I entirely concur,” he said. “Very well,” said I. “We have made out these three forms in our city to the best of our present judgement. What can be the remaining form that would give the city still another virtue? For it is obvious that the remainder is justice.” “Obvious.” “Now then, Glaucon, is the time for us like huntsmen to surround the covert and keep close watch that justice may not slip through and get away from us and vanish

chinese:
消失。它显然就在这一带什么地方。睁大眼睛，尽力把它找出来吧；也许你会比我先看到，给我指出来。”
“但愿我能如此，”他说，“不过，我想，如果你把我当作一个能跟随你、认出你所指之物的人，这就已经很好地利用我了。”
“那就祈求成功，”我说，“跟我一起走吧。”
“我会的，你只管带路。”他说。
“说真的，”我说，“这里似乎是个难以进入的地方，藏在深深的阴影里。”
“确实是片黑暗的丛林，不容易搜寻。”
english: from our sight. It plainly must be somewhere hereabouts. Keep your eyes open then and do your best to descry it. You may see it before I do and point it out to me.” “Would that I could,” he said; “but I think rather that if you find in me one who can follow you and discern what you point out to him you will be making a very fair use of me.” “Pray for success then,” said I, “and follow along with me.” “That I will do, only lead on,” he said. “And truly,” said I, “it appears to be an inaccessible place, lying in deep shadows.” “It certainly is a dark covert, not easy to beat up.”

chinese:
“尽管如此，我们仍须往前走。”
“是的，往前走。”
这时我看见了一点踪迹，便叫起来：“格劳孔，我想我们找到它的足迹了，我相信它逃不掉了。”
“听到这话真高兴。”他说。
“说真的，”我说，“我们实在太迟钝了。”
“怎么说？”
“好朋友，从一开始，这东西似乎就一直在我们脚边滚来滚去，我们却看不见，简直可笑极了，就像
english: “But all the same on we must go.” “Yes, on.” And I caught view and gave a hulloa and said, “Glaucon, I think we have found its trail and I don’t believe it will get away from us.” “I am glad to hear that,” said he. “Truly,” said I, “we were slackers indeed.” “How so?” “Why, all the time, bless your heart, the thing apparently was tumbling about our feet from the start and yet we couldn’t see it, but were most ludicrous, like

chinese:
有人寻找自己手里拿着的东西一样。我们没有把眼睛转向它，反而向远处张望；也许正因如此，它才逃过了我们的注意。”
“你是什么意思？”他问。
“我的意思是，”我回答，“我们似乎一直在谈论它、听人谈论它，却没有理解自己的话，也没有意识到，我们在某种意义上谈的正是它。”
“对于一个急切想听答案的人来说，”他说，“这段开场白可真长。”
english: people who sometimes hunt for what they hold in their hands. So we did not turn our eyes upon it, but looked off into the distance, which perhaps was the reason it escaped us.” “What do you mean?” he said. “This,” I replied, “that it seems to me that though we were speaking of it and hearing about it all the time we did not understand ourselves or realize that we were speaking of it in a sense.” “That is a tedious prologue,” he said, “for an eager listener.”

chinese:
“那么听着，”我说，“看看我的话有没有道理。我想，我们在建立城邦之初提出的那个普遍要求，就是正义，或者正义的某种形式。你记得，我们当时规定过，而且常常说，每一个人都应在城邦中承担一种最适合自己天性的工作。”
“是的，我们这样说过。”
“还有，各做自己的事，不多管别人的事，就是正义；
english: “Listen then,” said I, “and learn if there is anything in what I say. For what we laid down in the beginning as a universal requirement when we were founding our city, this I think, or some form of this, is justice. And what we did lay down, and often said, you recall, was that each one man must perform one social service in the state for which his nature is best adapted.” “Yes, we said that.” “And again that to do one’s own business and not to be a busybody is justice,

chinese:
这句话我们从许多人那里听到过，自己也常常说。”
“确实如此。”
“那么，我的朋友，”我说，“如果在某种意义上理解，正义似乎就是这条各做自己的事的原则。你知道我是怎样推断出来的吗？”
“不知道，请讲。”他说。
“我想，我们考察了节制、勇敢和智慧以后，城邦里剩下的就是这种德性；它使其他德性能够在城邦里生长，并且在它们产生以后，只要它自身还在，就使它们得以保存。我几乎不必再提醒你，
english: is a saying that we have heard from many and have often repeated ourselves.” “We have.” “This, then,” I said, “my friend, if taken in a certain sense appears to be justice, this principle of doing one’s own business. Do you know whence I infer this?” “No, but tell me,” he said. “I think that this is the remaining virtue in the state after our consideration of soberness, courage, and intelligence, a quality which made it possible for them all to grow up in the body politic and which when they have sprung up preserves them as long as it is present. And I hardly need to remind you that

chinese:
我们说过，找到其他三种德性之后，剩下的就是正义。”
“这个结论不可避免。”他说。
“再说，”我说，“假如要我们判断，究竟什么东西存在于城邦之中，最能使它成为一个好的城邦，这会很难决定：是统治者和被统治者意见一致，是军人始终保存法律所培养的对于什么可怕、什么不可怕的信念，是卫士所具有的警觉的智慧，
english: we said that justice would be the residue after we had found the other three.” “That is an unavoidable conclusion,” he said. “But moreover,” said I, “if we were required to decide what it is whose indwelling presence will contribute most to making our city good, it would be a difficult decision whether it was the unanimity of rulers and ruled or the conservation in the minds of the soldiers of the convictions produced by law as to what things are or are not to be feared, or the watchful intelligence

chinese:
还是这一条原则才是城邦良好的首要原因——儿童、妇女、奴隶、自由人、工匠、统治者和被统治者，每个人都只做自己的那一件事，而不样样插手、多管闲事？”
“确实难以决定。”他说。
“那么，城邦中的每个人都做自己工作的这条原则，对于城邦优良的贡献，可以与智慧、节制和勇敢相匹敌。”
“确实可以。”他说。
“而你难道不应把这个在造就城邦德性方面与它们相匹敌的原则，称为正义吗？”
english: that resides in the guardians, or whether this is the chief cause of its goodness, the principle embodied in child, woman, slave, free, artisan, ruler, and ruled, that each performed his one task as one man and was not a versatile busybody.” “Hard to decide indeed,” he said. “A thing, then, that in its contribution to the excellence of a state vies with and rivals its wisdom, its soberness, its bravery, is this principle of everyone in it doing his own task.” “It is indeed,” he said. “And is not justice the name you would have to give to the principle that rivals these as conducing to the virtue of state?”

chinese:
“当然。”
“如果这样还不能使你信服，也从另一个角度想想。你不是要把城邦中的诉讼交给统治者裁决吗？”
“当然。”
“他们裁决时的主要目的，不就是使人既不占有别人的东西，也不被夺去自己的东西吗？”
“除此之外，没有别的目的。”
“因为他们认为这样是正义的？”
“是的。”
“那么，从这个角度看，拥有自己的东西，做属于自己的
english:
“By all means.” “Consider it in this wise too if so you will be convinced. Will you not assign the conduct of lawsuits in your state to the rulers?” “Of course.” “Will not this be the chief aim of their decisions, that no one shall have what belongs to others or be deprived of his own? Nothing else but this.” “On the assumption that this is just?” “Yes.”

“From this point of view too, then, the having and doing

chinese:
事情，也可以承认就是正义。”
“是这样。”
“现在看看你是否同意我：木匠去做鞋匠的工作，鞋匠去做木匠的工作，或者他们交换彼此的工具和荣誉，甚至同一个人想把两份工作都做了——这些不同职能的混淆，你认为会给城邦带来很大的损害吗？”
“不会很大。”他说。
“但是，假如一个天性适合做工匠或某种谋利职业的人，
english: of one’s own and what belongs to oneself would admittedly be justice.” “That is so.” “Consider now whether you agree with me. A carpenter undertaking to do the work of a cobbler or a cobbler of a carpenter or their interchange of one another’s tools or honors or even the attempt of the same man to do both—the confounding of all other functions would not, think you, greatly injure a state, would it?” “Not much,” he said. “But when I fancy one who is by nature an artisan or some kind of money-maker

chinese:
受到财富、所能支配的选票、身体力量或其他类似优势的诱惑和鼓动，试图进入军人阶层；或者一个军人试图进入议政者和卫士的阶层，而他的天性并不适合；他们交换彼此的工具和荣誉，或者同一个人试图同时承担所有这些职能——那么，我想，你也会认为，这种替代和干预会毁掉城邦。”
“当然。”
“所以，城邦中这三个阶层互相干预彼此的事务，彼此替代，
english: tempted and incited by wealth or command of votes or bodily strength or some similar advantage tries to enter into the class of the soldiers or one of the soldiers into the class of counsellors and guardians, for which he is not fitted, and these interchange their tools and their honors or when the same man undertakes all these functions at once, then, I take it, you too believe that this kind of substitution and meddlesomeness is the ruin of a state.” “By all means.” “The interference with one another’s business, then, of three existent classes and the substitution of the one for the other

chinese:
是对城邦最大的损害，把它称为最能伤害城邦的事情，再恰当不过。”
“正是这样。”
“而对自己的城邦危害最大的事情，你不就会判定为不正义吗？”
“当然。”
“那么，这就是不正义。
“再倒过来说，谋利者、辅助者和卫士这三个阶层各司其职，在城邦中各做自己的工作，正好与刚才的情形相反；这就是正义，并且使城邦成为正义的城邦。”
english:
is the greatest injury to a state and would most rightly be designated as the thing which chiefly works it harm.” “Precisely so.” “And the thing that works the greatest harm to one’s own state, will you not pronounce to be injustice?” “Of course.” “This, then, is injustice.”

“Again, let us put it in this way. The proper functioning of the money-making class, the helpers and the guardians, each doing its own work in the state, being the reverse of that just described, would be justice and would render the city just.”

chinese:
“我认为事情正是这样，不会是别的样子。”他说。
“我们还不要把它确定得这么死，”我说，“如果把这个形式应用到个人身上，它在那里也可以被接受为正义的定义，那么我们再承认这一点；否则还能说什么呢？但如果不行，我们就得另找。现在，让我们把这项探究进行到底：我们曾经设想，如果找到某个包含正义的较大事物，在那里观察它，就能更容易地在个人身上发现正义的性质。
english: “I think the case is thus and no otherwise,” said he. “Let us not yet affirm it quite fixedly,” I said, “but if this form when applied to the individual man, accepted there also as a definition of justice, we will then concede the point—for what else will there be to say? But if not, then we will look for something else. But now let us work out the inquiry in which we supposed that, if we found some larger thing that contained justice and viewed it there, we should more easily discover its nature in the individual man.

chinese: 我们也同意，这个较大的事物就是城邦，所以我们尽可能建立了最好的城邦，清楚地知道，正义当然可以在一个好的城邦里找到。那么，现在必须把我们自以为在那里看见的东西，转回个人身上；如果得到证实，那就很好。如果在个人身上出现不同的东西，我们就要重新回到
english:
And we agreed that this larger thing is the city, and so we constructed the best city in our power, well knowing that in the good city it would of course be found. What, then, we thought we saw there we must refer back to the individual and, if it is confirmed, all will be well.”

But if something different manifests itself in the individual, we will return again

chinese:
城邦，在那里检验。这样把两者并排考察，相互摩擦，也许就能像钻木取火一样，使正义的火花迸发；它一旦显现，我们就可以在心中把它确立起来。”
“嗯，”他说，“这方法似乎很妥当，我们就该这样做。”
“那么，”我说，“一个东西，无论大或小，你都给它同一个名称；就使它们得到同一名称的那一点而言，它们是不同的，还是相同的？”
“相同的。”他说。
“那么，一个正义的人，
english: to the state and test it there and it may be that, by examining them side by side and rubbing them against one another, as it were from the fire-sticks we may cause the spark of justice to flash forth, and when it is thus revealed confirm it in our own minds.” “Well,” he said, “that seems a sound method and that is what we must do.” “Then,” said I, “if you call a thing by the same name whether it is big or little, is it unlike in the way in which it is called the same or like?” “Like,” he said. “Then a just man too

chinese:
就正义的形式本身而言，也不会与一个正义的城邦不同，而会与它相同。”
“是的，相同。”
“我们认为，城邦之所以正义，是因为其中三种天性不同的部分各司其职；它之所以节制、勇敢和智慧，又是由于这三个部分具有某些其他状态和习性。”
“不错。”他说。
“那么，我的朋友，我们也可以期待，个人的灵魂之中具有这同样的几个形式，
english: will not differ at all from a just city in respect of the very form of justice, but will be like it.” “Yes, like.” “But now the city was thought to be just because three natural kinds existing in it performed each its own function, and again it was sober, brave, and wise because of certain other affections and habits of these three kinds.” “True,” he said. “Then, my friend, we shall thus expect the individual also to have these same forms

chinese:
并且由于这些部分与城邦中的相应部分处在相同的状态，而有理由获得同样的名称。”
“必然如此。”他说。
“哎呀，”我说，“我们又卷入一个小小的探究了：灵魂自身究竟有没有这三个形式？”
“在我看来，这可一点也不小，”他说，“因为苏格拉底，也许那句‘美好的事情是困难的’确实说得对。”
“看来如此。”我说。
english: in his soul, and by reason of identical affections of these with those in the city to receive properly the same appellations.” “Inevitable,” he said. “Goodness gracious,” said I, “here is another trifling inquiry into which we have plunged, the question whether the soul really contains these three forms in itself or not.” “It does not seem to me at all trifling,” he said, “for perhaps, Socrates, the saying is true that ’fine things are difficult.’” “Apparently,” said I;

chinese:
“而且，格劳孔，我得告诉你，依我看，使用我们目前讨论的方法，绝不能精确把握这个问题；另有一条更长、更艰难的道路通向它。不过，我们也许可以按照前面讨论和探究的精度，继续谈下去。”
“我们可以满足于此吗？”他说，“就我而言，眼下这样已经很满意了。”
“我也完全满意。”我回答。
“那就请你不要厌倦，”他说，“继续探究吧。”
“那么，”
english: “and let me tell you, Glaucon, that in my opinion we shall never in the world apprehend this matter from such methods as we are now employing in discussion. For there is another longer and harder way that conducts to this. Yet we may perhaps discuss it on the level of previous statements and inquiries.” “May we acquiesce in that?” he said. “I for my part should be quite satisfied with that for the present.” “And I surely should be more than satisfied,” I replied. “Don’t you weary then,” he said, “but go on with the inquiry.” “Is it not, then,”

chinese: 我说，“有一点我们不能不承认：城邦里的各种形式和品质，也存在于我们每个人之中。它们不可能从其他地方进入城邦。若说城邦中的激情并不是来自那些据说富有激情的个人，那是荒唐的，例如色雷斯、斯基泰以及一般北方地区的居民；爱好知识的品质，主要会被归给我们生活的地方；
english:
said I, “impossible for us to avoid admitting this much, that the same forms and qualities are to be found in each one of us that are in the state? They could not get there from any other source.”

It would be absurd to suppose that the element of high spirit was not derived in states from the private citizens who are reputed to have this quality as the populations of the Thracian and Scythian lands and generally of northern regions; or the quality of love of knowledge, which would chiefly be attributed to the region where we dwell,

chinese:
至于爱财，我们大概会说，腓尼基人和埃及人很可能具有这种品质。”
“当然可以这样说。”他回答。
“那么，”我说，“事情就是如此，认识这一点并不困难。”
“一点也不困难。”
“可是，一旦问到我们做这些事究竟凭的是同一个东西，还是三个不同的东西各做一事——用我们自身的一个部分学习，用另一个部分发怒，用第三个部分欲求饮食、
english:
or the love of money which we might say is not least likely to be found in Phoenicians and the population of Egypt.” “One certainly might,” he replied. “This is the fact then,” said I, “and there is no difficulty in recognizing it.” “Certainly not.”

“But the matter begins to be difficult when you ask whether we do all these things with the same thing or whether there are three things and we do one thing with one and one with another—learn with one part of ourselves, feel anger with another, and with yet a third desire the pleasures of nutrition

chinese:
生殖以及同类的快乐，还是每一次开始活动时，都由整个灵魂来做这些事情——问题就困难起来了。真正难以妥善判定的是这一点。”
“我也这样想。”他说。
“那么，让我们试着这样划清界限，判定它们是不是同一个东西。”
“怎样做？”
“显然，同一个东西，不会在同一时间、同一方面、对同一对象，做出或承受相反的事情。因此，如果我们在灵魂的活动中发现这些相反的情形，
english: and generation and their kind, or whether it is with the entire soul that we function in each case when we once begin. That is what is really hard to determine properly.” “I think so too,” he said. “Let us then attempt to define the boundary and decide whether they are identical with one another in this way.” “How?” “It is obvious that the same thing will never do or suffer opposites in the same respect in relation to the same thing and at the same time. So that if ever we find these contradictions in the functions of the mind

chinese:
就可以知道，起作用的不是同一个东西，而是多个东西。”
“很好。”
“那么，请考察我的话。”
“请讲。”他回答。
“同一个东西，能在同一时间、同一方面，既静止又运动吗？”
“绝不可能。”
“我们还应理解得更精确一些，免得讨论下去发生争执。假如有人说，一个站着不动，却活动着手和头的人，是同一个人同时静止又运动，我想，我们不会认为这种说法准确；应当说，他的一部分静止，另一部分运动。不是这样吗？”
english: we shall know that it was not the same thing functioning but a plurality.” “Very well.” “Consider, then, what I am saying.” “Say on,” he replied. “Is it possible for the same thing at the same time in the same respect to be at rest and in motion?” “By no means.” “Let us have our understanding still more precise, lest as we proceed we become involved in dispute. If anyone should say of a man standing still but moving his hands and head that the same man is at the same time at rest and in motion we should not, I take it, regard that as the right way of expressing it, but rather that a part of him is at rest and a part in motion. Is not that so?”

chinese:
“是的。”
“假如反驳的人还要更巧妙地开玩笑，说陀螺的尖固定在一个点上旋转时，整个陀螺既静止又运动，其他围绕同一地点作圆周运动的东西也都如此，我们就要否定这种说法，因为这些情形中的静止和运动，并不是就物体的同一个部分而言。我们会说，
english: “It is.” “Then if the disputant should carry the jest still further with the subtlety that tops at any rate stand still as a whole at the same time that they are in motion when with the peg fixed in one point they revolve, and that the same is true of any other case of circular motion about the same spot—we should reject the statement on the ground that the repose and the movement in such cases were not in relation to the same parts of the objects, but we would say

chinese:
它们有一条直轴和一个圆周；就直轴而言，它们静止，因为轴没有向任何一边倾斜；就圆周而言，它们作圆周运动。但是，如果在旋转时，直轴向右、向左、向前或向后倾斜，那么它们就完全不能说是静止了。”
“这样说才对。”他说。
“所以，这一类说法不会扰乱我们，也不会使我们更相信，同一个东西能够在同一时间、同一方面、同一关系中，承受、处于或做出相反的事情。”
english:
that there was a straight line and a circumference in them and that in respect of the straight line they are standing still since they do not incline to either side, but in respect of the circumference they move in a circle; but that when as they revolve they incline the perpendicular to right or left or forward or back, then they are in no wise at rest.” “And that would be right,” he said.

“No such remarks then will disconcert us or any whit the more make us believe that it is ever possible for the same thing at the same time in the same respect and the same relation to suffer, be, or do opposites.”

chinese:
“我肯定不会因此动摇。”他说。
“尽管如此，”我说，“为免不得不把这一类反对意见全部冗长地考察一遍，确信它们都是错误的，我们就先以这个原则为假设继续讨论；但要约定，如果它以后显出并非如此，那么从这个假设得出的一切结论也就都作废。”
“我们应该这样做。”他说。
english: “They will not me, I am sure,” said he. “All the same,” said I, “that we may not be forced to examine at tedious length the entire list of such contentions and convince ourselves that they are false, let us proceed on the hypothesis that this is so, with the understanding that, if it ever appear otherwise, everything that results from the assumption shall be invalidated.” “That is what we must do,” he said.

chinese:
“那么，”我说，“你会不会把赞同和反对、追求和拒绝、拥抱和排斥看成彼此相反？这些以及一切类似的事情，不都属于相反的动作或感受吗？把它们称为动作还是感受，都没有关系。”
“没有关系，”他说，“它们确实相反。”
“那么，”我说，“口渴、饥饿以及一般的欲望，还有同意和意愿，难道不也应归入
english: “Will you not then,” said I, “set down as opposed to one another assent and dissent, and the endeavor after a thing to the rejection of it, and embracing to repelling—do not these and all things like these belong to the class of opposite actions or passions; it will make no difference which?” “None,” said he, “but they are opposites.” “What then,” said I, “of thirst and hunger and the appetites generally, and again consenting and willing, would you not put them all somewhere in the classes

chinese:
刚才所说的某一类吗？例如，你会不会说，一个有所欲求的人的灵魂，或者努力追求所欲之物，或者把希望获得的东西拉向自己、加以拥抱；又或者，只要它愿意得到某种东西，就仿佛有人向它提问似的，自己对自己点头赞同，力求取得它？”
“我会这样说。”他说。
“至于不愿意、不同意、不欲求，我们不是应该把它们归入灵魂拒绝、排斥某物的活动，
english: just described? Will you not say, for example, that the soul of one who desires either strives for that which he desires or draws towards its embrace what it wishes to accrue to it; or again, in so far as it wills that anything be presented to it, nods assent to itself thereon as if someone put the question, striving towards its attainment?” “I would say so,” he said. “But what of not-willing and not consenting nor yet desiring, shall we not put these under the soul’s rejection and repulsion from itself and

chinese:
总之，归入与前面那些事情相反的一类吗？”
“当然。”
“既然如此，我们可以说欲望自成一类，其中最明显的就是我们所谓的口渴和饥饿吗？”
“可以。”他说。
“一个是对饮料的欲望，另一个是对食物的欲望，不是吗？”
“是的。”
“那么，口渴就其为口渴而言，除了我们所说的灵魂对饮料的欲求，还会欲求别的东西吗？我的意思是，口渴本身是渴望热饮、冷饮、多饮、少饮，或者总之，某种具有特定性质的饮料吗？还是说，只有在口渴之外又加上热，
english: generally into the opposite class from all the former?” “Of course.” “This being so, shall we say that the desires constitute a class and that the most conspicuous members of that class are what we call thirst and hunger?” “We shall,” said he. “Is not the one desire of drink, the other of food?” “Yes.” “Then in so far as it is thirst, would it be of anything more than that of which we say it is a desire in the soul? I mean is thirst thirst for hot drink or cold or much or little or in a word for a draught of any particular quality, or is it the fact that if heat

chinese:
它才进一步成为对冷饮的欲望；加上冷，才成为对热饮的欲望？同样，如果由于程度大而很渴，就会渴望大量饮料；程度小，就渴望少量。但口渴本身绝不会欲求别的东西，只会欲求它天性所指向的饮料本身；饥饿对于食物也是如此。”
“是这样，”他说，“每种欲望本身，只是对它天性所指向的东西的欲望；那些修饰语，则属于某种具有特定性质的欲望。”
english: is attached to the thirst it would further render the desire—a desire of cold, and if cold of hot? But if owing to the presence of muchness the thirst is much it would render it a thirst for much and if little for little.
