But mere thirst will never be desire of anything else than that of which it is its nature to be, mere drink, and so hunger of food.” “That is so,” he said; “each desire in itself is of that thing only of which it is its nature to be. The epithets belong to the quality—such or such.”

chinese:
“所以，”我说，“我们不要让人趁我们不留意，用这样的反驳把我们弄乱：每个人欲求的不是饮料，而是好的饮料，不是食物，而是好的食物；因为，他们会说，人人都欲求好的东西，所以，口渴既然是欲望，就应该是对好的饮料，或者不论其对象是什么，对好的对象的欲望；其他欲望也都如此。”
“嗯，”他说，“这个反驳似乎也有一些道理。”
“不过，”我说，“我几乎不必提醒你，
english: “Let no one then,” said I, “disconcert us when off our guard with the objection that everybody desires not drink but good drink and not food but good food, because (the argument will run) all men desire good, and so, if thirst is desire, it would be of good drink or of good whatsoever it is; and so similarly of other desires.” “Why,” he said, “there perhaps would seem to be something in that objection.” “But I need hardly remind you,” said I,

chinese:
在那些相对于某物而言的事物中，带有特定限定的事物，对应于带有特定限定的对象；仅就其自身而言的事物，对应的也只是对象自身。”
“我不明白。”他说。
“你不明白，”我说，“较大的东西，必定是比某个东西大吗？”
“当然明白。”
“不就是比那个较小的东西大吗？”
“是的。”
“而大得多的东西，是比小得多的东西大得多，对吗？”
“是的。”
“我们还可以补充：曾经较大的，是比曾经较小的大；将来较大的，是比将来较小的大？”
“当然。”
english: “that of relative terms those that are somehow qualified are related to a qualified correlate, those that are severally just themselves to a correlate that is just itself.” “I don’t understand,” he said. “Don’t you understand,” said I, “that the greater is such as to be greater than something?” “Certainly.” “Is it not than the less?” “Yes.” “But the much greater than the much less. Is that not so?” “Yes.” “And may we add the one time greater than the one time less and that which will be greater than that which will be less?” “Surely.”

chinese:
“同样，较多相对于较少，双倍相对于一半，以及一切类似情形；还有，较重相对于较轻，较快相对于较慢，热相对于冷，以及这一类的一切情形，不都如此吗？”
“当然。”
“那么，各种知识呢？情形不也一样吗？知识本身，只以可知者本身为对象，或者说，以我们必须承认与知识相对应的那个东西为对象；但某种特定的知识，则以某种特定的事物为对象。
english: “And similarly of the more towards the fewer, and the double towards the half and of all like cases, and again of the heavier towards the lighter, the swifter towards the slower, and yet again of the hot towards the cold and all cases of that kind, does not the same hold?” “By all means.” “But what of the sciences? Is not the way of it the same? Science which is just that, is of knowledge which is just that, or is of whatsoever we must assume the correlate of science to be. But a particular science of a particular kind is of some particular thing of a particular kind.

chinese:
我的意思是这样：因为有一种建造房屋的知识，它与其他知识不同，所以被称为建筑术。”
“当然。”
“这是因为它具有某种性质，而其他知识都没有这种性质，不是吗？”
“是的。”
“而它之所以成为某种特定的知识，不就是因为它以某种特定的事物为对象吗？其他技艺和知识也都如此？”
“是这样。”
“那么，”我说，“如果你现在明白了，就应该说，我先前那句话的意思是：一切相对于某物而言的东西，仅就其自身而言，只与对象自身相对应；
english:
I mean something like this: As there was a science of making a house it differed from other sciences so as to be named architecture.” “Certainly.” “Was not this by reason of its being of a certain kind such as no other of all the rest?” “Yes.” “And was it not because it was of something of a certain kind that it itself became a certain kind of science? And similarly of the other arts and sciences?” “That is so.”

“This then,” said I, “if haply you now understand, is what you must say I then meant, by the statement that of all things that are such as to be of something those that are just themselves only are of things just themselves only,

chinese:
具有某种限定的，则与具有某种限定的对象相对应。我完全不是说，它们与对象具有相同的性质，仿佛研究健康和疾病的知识本身也健康或生病，研究善恶的知识本身也善或恶。我只是说，当知识不再只是关于一般可知对象，而是关于某种特定的事物，例如健康和疾病时，它本身也就成为某种特定的知识，因此不再仅仅叫作知识，而要加上这个特定种类的名称，称为医学。”
“我明白，”他说，“也同意事情如此。”
“那么，回到口渴，”我说，
english:
but things of a certain kind are of things of a kind. And I don’t at all mean that they are of the same kind as the things of which they are, so that we are to suppose that the science of health and disease is a healthy and diseased science and that of evil and good, evil and good. I only mean that as science became the science not of just the thing of which science is but of some particular kind of thing, namely, of health and disease, the result was that it itself became some kind of science and this caused it to be no longer called simply science but with the addition of the particular kind, medical science.” “I understand,” he said, “and agree that it is so.”

“To return to thirst, then,” said I,

chinese:
“你不会把它归入那些相对于某物而言的东西，并且说，它正是在这种关系中才成为它自身的吗？我们现在说的，我想，正是口渴。”
“我会，”他说，“也就是对饮料的欲求。”
“那么，饮料有某种限定，口渴也就有某种限定；但口渴本身既不是对多或少的欲求，也不是对好或坏的欲求，总之，不是对任何特定种类的欲求，而在天性上只是对饮料本身的欲求。”
“完全如此。”
“因此，口渴者的灵魂，就其口渴而言，所愿的无非是饮用，
english: “will you not class it with the things that are of something and say that it is what it is in relation to something—and it is, I presume, thirst?” “I will,” said he, “—namely of drink.” “Then if the drink is of a certain kind, so is the thirst, but thirst that is just thirst is neither of much nor little nor good nor bad, nor in a word of any kind, but just thirst is naturally of just drink only.” “By all means.” “The soul of the thirsty then, in so far as it thirsts, wishes nothing else than to drink, and

chinese:
它渴望这个，冲动也朝向这个。”
“显然。”
“所以，如果它口渴时有什么把它拉回来，那一定是它内部另一个东西，不同于那个口渴、像驱赶野兽一样驱使它去喝的东西。因为我们说过，同一个东西，不可能用自身的同一个部分，在同一时间，对同一对象，作出相反的动作。”
“我们必须承认，不可能。”
“所以我想，说射箭的人双手同时把弓推开又拉近，也不准确；我们应当说，一只手把它推开，另一只手把它拉近。”
english: yearns for this and its impulse is towards this.” “Obviously.” “Then if anything draws it back when thirsty it must be something different in it from that which thirsts and drives it like a beast to drink. For it cannot be, we say, that the same thing with the same part of itself at the same time acts in opposite ways about the same thing.” “We must admit that it does not.” “So I fancy it is not well said of the archer that his hands at the same time thrust away the bow and draw it nigh, but we should rather say that there is one hand that puts it away and another that draws it to.”

chinese:
“当然。”他说。
“那么，我们是否可以说，有些人有时虽然口渴，却不肯喝水？”
“确实可以，”他说，“这样的人很多，也很常见。”
“那么，”我说，“对于他们，我们该作何解释？不是应当说，灵魂中有一个东西命令他们喝，另一个东西禁止他们喝，而这个不同的东西压过了发出喝水命令的东西吗？”
“我想是的。”
“这种阻止行为的力量，出现时不是出于理性的计算，
english: “By all means,” he said. “Are we to say, then, that some men sometimes though thirsty refuse to drink?” “We are indeed,” he said, “many and often.” “What then,” said I, “should one affirm about them?” “Is it not that there is something in the soul that bids them drink and a something that forbids, a different something that masters that which bids?” “I think so.” “And is it not the fact that that which inhibits such actions arises when it arises from the calculations of reason,

chinese:
而那些拉扯、拖曳的冲动，则来自感受和病态吗？”
“看来是的。”
“那么，”我说，“我们有理由认为，它们是两个彼此不同的东西：把灵魂借以计算和推理的部分称为理性部分；把它借以爱欲、饥饿、口渴，并受到其他欲望的激动和刺激的部分，称为无理性的欲望部分，它伴随着种种满足和快乐。”
“这样想不但有道理，”他说，“而且很自然。”
english: but the impulses which draw and drag come through affections and diseases?” “Apparently.” “Not unreasonably,” said I, “shall we claim that they are two and different from one another, naming that in the soul whereby it reckons and reasons the rational and that with which it loves, hungers, thirsts, and feels the flutter and titillation of other desires, the irrational and appetitive—companion of various repletions and pleasures.” “It would not be unreasonable but quite natural,” he said, “for us to think this.”

chinese:
“那么，我们姑且认为，已经把灵魂中实际存在的这两个形式区分出来了。可是，激情，也就是我们借以发怒的那个东西，是第三种，还是在性质上与其中一种相同呢？”
“也许，”他说，“与其中的欲望部分相同。”
“可是，”我说，“我曾听过一个故事，我相信是真的：阿格莱翁之子勒翁提俄斯，从比雷埃夫斯沿北面长墙的外侧往上走，看见刑场上躺着一些尸体。他一方面想去看，另一方面又厌恶、退缩。有一会儿，
english:
“These two forms, then, let us assume to have been marked off as actually existing in the soul. But now the Thumos or principle of high spirit, that with which we feel anger, is it a third, or would it be identical in nature with one of these?” “Perhaps,” he said, “with one of these, the appetitive.”

“But,” I said, “I once heard a story which I believe, that Leontius the son of Aglaion, on his way up from the Peiraeus under the outer side of the northern wall, becoming aware of dead bodies that lay at the place of public execution at the same time felt a desire to see them and a repugnance and aversion, and that for a time

chinese:
他抵抗着欲望，用衣服蒙住头；但最后还是被欲望压倒，睁大眼睛跑到尸体跟前，喊道：‘看吧，你们这些可怜的东西，把这美好的景象看个够吧！’”
“我也听过这个故事。”他说。
“可是，”我说，“这件事分明表示，愤怒有时会同欲望交战，如同一个不同的东西反对另一个东西。”
“是的，确实如此。”他说。
“还有，”我说，“在许多别的场合，我们不是也看到，当欲望迫使一个人违背理性时，
english:
he resisted and veiled his head, but overpowered in despite of all by his desire, with wide staring eyes he rushed up to the corpses and cried, ‘There, ye wretches, take your fill of the fine spectacle!’” “I too,” he said, “have heard the story.” “Yet, surely, this anecdote,” I said, “signifies that the principle of anger sometimes fights against desires as an alien thing against an alien.” “Yes, it does,” he said.

“And do we not,” said I, “on many other occasions observe when his desires constrain a man contrary to his reason

chinese: 他会责骂自己，对内部那个支配他的东西发怒；仿佛两个派别发生内讧，他的激情就成为理性的盟友吗？但在理性轻声说‘你不可以’的时候，激情却与欲望联手反对理性——这样的情形，我想，你不会说曾经在自己身上发现过；我猜，在别人身上也没有。”
english: that he reviles himself and is angry with that within which masters him and that as it were in a faction of two parties the high spirit of such a man becomes the ally of his reason? But its making common cause with the desires against the reason when reason whispers low ‘Thou must not’—that, I think, is a kind of thing you would not affirm ever to have perceived in yourself, nor, I fancy, in anybody else either.”

chinese:
“凭宙斯起誓，没有。”他说。
“再说，一个人如果认为自己做错了，那么他越高尚，即使挨饿、受冻，或者受到种种其他苦楚，只要他认为施加这些的人是在正义地行事，他就越不能对那人发怒，正如我说的，他的激情不肯起来反对那个人。这不是真的吗？”
“是真的。”他说。
“可是，假如一个人认为自己受到了不正义的对待，他的激情不就会沸腾、激烈起来，也会因挨饿、
english: “No, by heaven,” he said. “Again, when a man thinks himself to be in the wrong, is it not true that the nobler he is the less is he capable of anger though suffering hunger and cold and whatsoever else at the hands of him whom he believes to be acting justly therein, and as I say his spirit refuses to be aroused against such a one?” “True,” he said. “But what when a man believes himself to be wronged, does not his spirit in that case seethe and grow fierce (and also because of his suffering hunger,

chinese:
受冻和类似的苦楚而更激烈，成为他所认为正义之事的盟友吗？在高尚的灵魂中，它会坚持并赢得胜利，决不放弃，直到达到目的，或者死亡终结一切，或者像狗被牧人唤回一样，被内在的理性唤回、平息。”
“这个比喻很贴切，”他说，“也印证了我们先前的话：辅助者就像狗，听命于统治者，而统治者就像城邦的牧人。”
“你很好地理解了我的意思。”我说，“可是，你也注意到这一点了吗？”
english: cold and the like) and make itself the ally of what he judges just, and in noble souls it endures and wins the victory and will not let go until either it achieves its purpose, or death ends all, or, as a dog is called back by a shepherd, it is called back by the reason within and calmed.” “Your similitude is perfect,” he said, “and it confirms our former statements that the helpers are as it were dogs subject to the rulers who are as it were the shepherds of the city.” “You apprehend my meaning excellently,” said I. “But do you also take note of this?”

chinese:
“哪一点？”
“我们现在对激情部分的看法，恰好与刚才的猜想相反。那时我们以为它是欲望部分的一部分；现在非但不这样说，反而认为，当灵魂内讧时，它更会站在理性一边。”
“完全如此。”他说。
“那么，它也不同于理性吗？还是它就是理性的一种形式，因而灵魂中只有理性和欲望两类，而不是三类？或者，正如城邦由
english:
“Of what?” “That what we now think about the spirited element is just the opposite of our recent surmise. For then we supposed it to be a part of the appetitive, but now, far from that, we say that, in the factions of the soul, it much rather marshals itself on the side of the reason.” “By all means,” he said.

“Is it then distinct from this too, or is it a form of the rational, so that there are not three but two kinds in the soul, the rational and the appetitive, or just as in the city there were

chinese:
谋利者、辅助者、议政者三个现存的类别构成，灵魂中也有第三类，就是这种激情；除非被恶劣的教育败坏，它天生就是理性的辅助者？”
“我们必须把它看作第三类。”他说。
“是的，”我说，“但前提是，必须证明它不同于理性，正如已经证明它不同于欲望一样。”
“这不难证明，”他说，“从儿童身上就看得出来：他们一出生就充满愤怒和激情；至于理性，
english: three existing kinds that composed its structure, the moneymakers, the helpers, the counsellors, so also in the soul there exists a third kind, this principle of high spirit, which is the helper of reason by nature unless it is corrupted by evil nurture?” “We have to assume it as a third,” he said. “Yes,” said I, “provided it shall have been shown to be something different from the rational, as it has been shown to be other than the appetitive.” “That is not hard to be shown,” he said; “for that much one can see in children, that they are from their very birth chock-full of rage and high spirit, but as for reason,

chinese:
依我看，有些人从来不曾分享它，大多数人也要到很晚才有。”
“凭宙斯起誓，说得很好！”我回答，“而且，从动物身上也能看出，你的话是真的。除了这些例子，还可以加上前面引过的荷马诗句作证：
‘他捶着自己的胸膛，这样责备自己的心。’
（荷马《奥德赛》20.17）
因为荷马在这里清楚地表现出，我们内心
english:
some of them, to my thinking, never participate in it, and the majority quite late.” “Yes, by heaven, excellently said,” I replied; “and further, one could see in animals that what you say is true. And to these instances we may add the testimony of Homer quoted above:‘
He smote his breast and chided thus his heart. ’ For there Homer has clearly represented that in us

chinese:
那个考虑过何者更好、何者更坏的东西，正在责备那个无理发怒的东西，仿佛它们是两个彼此不同的东西。”
“你说得完全正确。”他说。
“那么，”我说，“我们终于艰难地渡过了这片水域，大体同意：在城邦和我们每个人的灵魂中，存在着数量相同的同样几类。”
“是这样。”
“那么，我们先前的设定不就立刻必然随之而来了吗：城邦怎样成为智慧的、凭什么成为智慧的，个人也就同样、凭同一部分成为智慧的？”
“当然。”
“同样，个人怎样成为勇敢的、凭什么成为勇敢的，
english:
which has reflected about the better and the worse as rebuking that which feels unreasoning anger as if it were a distinct and different thing.” “You are entirely right,” he said.

“Through these waters, then,” said I, “we have with difficulty made our way and we are fairly agreed that the same kinds equal in number are to be found in the state and in the soul of each one of us.” “That is so.” “Then does not the necessity of our former postulate immediately follow, that as and whereby the state was wise so and thereby is the individual wise?” “Surely.” “And so whereby and as

chinese:
城邦也同样、凭同一部分成为勇敢的；其他一切德性，两者也以相同的方式具备？”
“必然如此。”
“那么，格劳孔，我想我们也会说，一个人之所以正义，与城邦之所以正义，道理相同。”
“这也完全不可避免。”
“而我们当然没有忘记，城邦之所以正义，是因为其中的三个阶层各自履行自己的职能。”
“我想我们没有忘记。”他说。
“那么，我们也必须记得，我们每个人，凡是内部各个部分
english: the individual is brave, thereby and so is the state brave, and that both should have all the other constituents of virtue in the same way?” “Necessarily.” “Just too, then, Glaucon, I presume we shall say a man is in the same way in which a city was just.” “That too is quite inevitable.” “But we surely cannot have forgotten this, that the state was just by reason of each of the three classes found in it fulfilling its own function.” “I don’t think we have forgotten,” he said. “We must remember, then, that each of us also in whom the several parts within him

chinese:
各做其事的，就是正义的人，也是各管自身事务的人。”
“我们确实必须记得。”他说。
“理性部分既有智慧，又能为整个灵魂作长远考虑，不就应当由它统治，而由激情部分服从它、做它的盟友吗？”
“当然。”
“那么，正如我们说过的，不正是诗乐教育与体育教育的调和，使它们协调一致吗？用美好的言辞和教导强化、
english:
perform each their own task—he will be a just man and one who minds his own affair.” “We must indeed remember,” he said. “Does it not belong to the rational part to rule, being wise and exercising forethought in behalf of the entire soul, and to the principle of high spirit to be subject to this and its ally?” “Assuredly.”

“Then is it not, as we said, the blending of music and gymnastics that will render them concordant, intensifying

chinese:
培育一个部分，用和声和节奏放松、安抚另一个部分，使它变得温和。”
“正是如此。”他说。
“这两个部分受到这样的培养，经过学习和教育，真正学会各做自己的工作以后，就会管理欲望部分。它在我们每个人的灵魂中占据最大部分，而且天性上对财富最不知足。它们会看守它，免得它充满并感染于那些与身体相连的所谓快乐，变得庞大而强壮，不再安守自己的工作，
english: and fostering the one with fair words and teachings and relaxing and soothing and making gentle the other by harmony and rhythm?” “Quite so,” said he. “And these two thus reared and having learned and been educated to do their own work in the true sense of the phrase, will preside over the appetitive part which is the mass of the soul in each of us and the most insatiate by nature of wealth. They will keep watch upon it, lest, by being filled and infected with the so-called pleasures associated with the body and so waxing big and strong, it may not keep to its own work

chinese:
反而试图奴役、统治那些它不应当统治的部分，因而把所有部分的整个生活都颠覆了。”
“当然。”他说。
“那么，这两个部分不也最能替整个灵魂和身体防御外来的敌人吗？一个谋划，另一个作战，听从统治者，凭勇气执行统治者的计划。”
“是这样。”
“那么，我想，我们称每个人为勇敢的，
english: but may undertake to enslave and rule over the classes which it is not fitting that it should, and so overturn the entire life of all.” “By all means,” he said. “Would not these two, then, best keep guard against enemies from without also in behalf of the entire soul and body, the one taking counsel, the other giving battle, attending upon the ruler, and by its courage executing the ruler’s designs?” “That is so.” “Brave, too, then, I take it, we call

chinese:
也是由于他的这个部分：当他的激情在痛苦和快乐之中，仍保持理性传下来的、关于什么可怕和什么不可怕的准则时，他就是勇敢的。”
“对。”他说。
“而称他为智慧的，则是由于他内部那个统治、发布这些命令的小部分；因为它自身具有知识，知道什么对每个部分有利，什么对由三者组成的共同整体有利。”
“当然。”
“再说，他之所以节制，
english: each individual by virtue of this part in him, when, namely, his high spirit preserves in the midst of pains and pleasures the rule handed down by the reason as to what is or is not to be feared.” “Right,” he said. “But wise by that small part that ruled in him and handed down these commands, by its possession in turn within it of the knowledge of what is beneficial for each and for the whole, the community composed of the three.” “By all means.” “And again, was he not sober

chinese:
不就是由于这些部分彼此友爱、协调一致吗？也就是，统治的部分和那两个被统治的部分一致相信，应当由理性统治，并且不起来反对它。”
“节制这种德性，”他说，“无论在城邦还是个人中，确实就是这个，没有别的。”
“至于一个人之所以正义，当然是出于我们反复说过的那个原因，并且以那种方式成为正义的。”
“完全必然。”
“那么，”我说，“我们的正义观念，其轮廓是否有什么地方变得模糊，以至于看起来与它在城邦里显出的样子不同了？”
“我看没有。”他说。
english: by reason of the friendship and concord of these same parts, when, namely, the ruling principle and its two subjects are at one in the belief that the reason ought to rule, and do not raise faction against it?” “The virtue of soberness certainly,” said he, “is nothing else than this, whether in a city or an individual.” “But surely, now, a man is just by that which and in the way we have so often described.” “That is altogether necessary.” “Well then,” said I, “has our idea of justice in any way lost the edge of its contour so as to look like anything else than precisely what it showed itself to be in the state?” “I think not,” he said.

chinese:
“如果我们心里还有什么反对这个定义，”我说，“我们可以用一些日常、普通的检验，来充分证实你的回答和我们自己的信念。”
“什么检验？”
“例如，有人要求我们就那个城邦，以及一个天性和教养都与它协调的人，回答这样的问题：我们是否相信，这样一个人受托保管金银时，会扣留、侵吞这些财物？你认为谁会觉得，他比其他类型的人更可能这样做？”
english:
“We might,” I said, “completely confirm your reply and our own conviction thus, if anything in our minds still disputes our definition—by applying commonplace and vulgar tests to it.” “What are these?”

“For example, if an answer were demanded to the question concerning that city and the man whose birth and breeding was in harmony with it, whether we believe that such a man, entrusted with a deposit of gold or silver, would withhold it and embezzle it, who do you suppose would think that he would be more likely so to act than men of a different kind?”

chinese:
“没有人会。”他说。
“他也会远离亵渎神物、偷窃、在私人生活中背叛同伴，以及在公共生活中背叛城邦吧？”
“会的。”
“此外，他在遵守誓言或其他约定方面，也绝不会失信。”
“他怎么会呢？”
“至于通奸、不孝敬父母、不履行对诸神应尽的侍奉，这些事当然更可能属于其他任何人，而不是这样的人。”
“确实，任何别人都比他更可能。”
english: “No one would,” he said. “And would not he be far removed from sacrilege and theft and betrayal of comrades in private life or of the state in public?” “He would.” “And, moreover, he would not be in any way faithless either in the keeping of his oaths or in other agreements.” “How could he?” “Adultery, surely, and neglect of parents and of the due service of the gods would pertain to anyone rather than to such a man.” “To anyone indeed,”

chinese:
他说。
“这一切的原因，不正是他内部的每个部分，在统治和被统治方面，都做着自己的工作吗？”
“是的，没有别的原因。”
“那么，你还会到别处寻找正义，认为它不同于这种能够造就这样的人和城邦的力量吗？”
“凭宙斯起誓，”他说，“不会。”
“那么，我们的梦已经实现、完成了——也就是我们说过的那个猜想：仿佛某种神意，使我们在建立城邦之初，
english:
he said. “And is not the cause of this to be found in the fact that each of the principles within him does its own work in the matter of ruling and being ruled?” “Yes, that and nothing else.” “Do you still, then, look for justice to be anything else than this potency which provides men and cities of this sort?” “No, by heaven,” he said, “I do not.”

“Finished, then, is our dream and perfected —the surmise we spoke of, that, by some Providence, at the very beginning of our foundation of the state,

chinese:
就碰巧找到了正义的原初原则和某种模型。”
“确实如此。”
“格劳孔，看来那条原则确实是正义的某种影像，所以才有帮助：天性适合做鞋匠的人，应当只做鞋、不做别的；木匠应当做木工，其他人也都如此。但事情的真相似乎是，
english: we chanced to hit upon the original principle and a sort of type of justice.” “Most assuredly.” “It really was, it seems, Glaucon, which is why it helps, a sort of adumbration of justice, this principle that it is right for the cobbler by nature to cobble and occupy himself with nothing else, and the carpenter to practice carpentry, and similarly all others. But the truth of the matter was, as it seems,

chinese: 正义确实属于这一类东西，却不是指外在地各做自己的工作，而是指内在的、真正关乎自己和自己所有的事情。它意味着，一个人不容许灵魂中的各部分去做别的部分的工作，彼此干预、多管闲事；他应当妥善安排真正属于自己的事情，首先支配自己，使内在具有美好的秩序，把这三个部分调和起来，就像把音阶中的低音、高音和中音，
english: that justice is indeed something of this kind, yet not in regard to the doing of one’s own business externally, but with regard to that which is within and in the true sense concerns one’s self, and the things of one’s self—it means that a man must not suffer the principles in his soul to do each the work of some other and interfere and meddle with one another, but that he should dispose well of what in the true sense of the word is properly his own, and having first attained to self-mastery and beautiful order within himself, and having harmonized these three principles, the notes or intervals of three terms quite literally the lowest, the highest, and the mean,

chinese: 以及它们之间可能有的其他音都协调起来。他把这三个部分连接、结合，使自己成为一个统一体，成为一个人而不再是许多人，节制而和谐。只有到了这时，他才去做必须做的事情，无论是获取财富、照顾身体，还是从事政治或私人事务；在所有这些活动中，他把保存并帮助产生这种灵魂状态的行为，看作并称为正义而美好的行为，把指导这种行为的知识
english: and all others there may be between them, and having linked and bound all three together and made of himself a unit, one man instead of many, self-controlled and in unison, he should then and then only turn to practice if he find aught to do either in the getting of wealth or the tendance of the body or it may be in political action or private business, in all such doings believing and naming the just and honorable action to be that which preserves and helps to produce this condition of soul, and wisdom the science

chinese:
称为智慧；把倾向于破坏这种灵魂秩序的行为，看作并称为不正义的行为，把指导这种行为的意见称为愚昧。”
“苏格拉底，你说得完全正确。”
“那么，”我说，“如果我们宣称已经找到了正义的人和城邦，以及其中的正义究竟是什么，我想，我们不会错得很远。”
“确实不会。”他说。
“那我们就这样宣称？”
“就这样宣称。”
“那就如此，”我说，“接下来，我想，我们必须考察不正义。”
“显然。”
english:
that presides over such conduct; and believing and naming the unjust action to be that which ever tends to overthrow this spiritual constitution, and brutish ignorance, to be the opinion that in turn presides over this.”

“What you say is entirely true, Socrates.” “Well,” said I, “if we should affirm that we had found the just man and state and what justice really is in them, I think we should not be much mistaken.” “No indeed, we should not,” he said. “Shall we affirm it, then?” “Let us so affirm.”

“So be it, then,” said I; “next after this, I take it, we must consider injustice.” “Obviously.”

chinese:
“它不应当是这三个部分之间的一种内战吗？它们互相干预、侵犯彼此的职能，其中一个部分反叛整个灵魂，企图取得并不属于它的统治权，而它的天性本来适合服从那个统治部分、做它的仆从。我想，我们会说，大致就是这样；这些部分的混乱、偏离各自应有的道路，就是不正义、放纵、怯懦、愚昧，总而言之，就是一切恶。”
“正是如此。”
english: “Must not this be a kind of civil war of these three principles, their meddlesomeness and interference with one another’s functions, and the revolt of one part against the whole of the soul that it may hold therein a rule which does not belong to it, since its nature is such that it befits it to serve as a slave to the ruling principle? Something of this sort, I fancy, is what we shall say, and that the confusion of these principles and their straying from their proper course is injustice and licentiousness and cowardice and brutish ignorance and, in general, all turpitude.” “Precisely this,”

chinese:
他回答。
“那么，”我说，“既然不正义和正义是这样，做不正义的事、成为不正义的人，以及反过来做正义的事，这些说法的含义，就立刻清楚明白了。”
“怎么说？”
“因为，”我说，“它们之于灵魂，就像有益健康和导致疾病的事情之于身体，两者没有差别。”
“在哪一方面？”他问。
“有益健康的事情产生健康，导致疾病的事情产生疾病。”
“是的。”
“那么，做正义的事，不就产生正义；做不正义的事，就产生不正义吗？”
english: he replied. “Then,” said I, “to act unjustly and be unjust and in turn to act justly the meaning of all these terms becomes at once plain and clear, since injustice and justice are so.” “How so?” “Because,” said I, “these are in the soul what the healthful and the diseaseful are in the body; there is no difference.” “In what respect?” he said. “Healthful things surely engender health and diseaseful disease.” “Yes.” “Then does not doing just acts engender justice and unjust injustice?”

chinese:
“必然如此。”
“而产生健康，就是使身体中的各种成分，按照自然的关系彼此支配、服从；造成疾病，则是使它们违反自然地彼此支配、服从。”
“是的，是这样。”
“同样，在灵魂中产生正义，不就是使各个部分按照自然的关系彼此支配、服从；产生不正义，就是使它们违反自然地彼此支配、服从吗？”
“正是如此。”他说。
“那么，德性看来就是灵魂的一种健康、
english: “Of necessity.” “But to produce health is to establish the elements in a body in the natural relation of dominating and being dominated by one another, while to cause disease is to bring it about that one rules or is ruled by the other contrary to nature.” “Yes, that is so.” “And is it not likewise the production of justice in the soul to establish its principles in the natural relation of controlling and being controlled by one another, while injustice is to cause the one to rule or be ruled by the other contrary to nature?” “Exactly so,” he said. “Virtue, then, as it seems, would be a kind of health

chinese:
美和良好状态，而恶德则是灵魂的疾病、丑陋和衰弱。”
“是的。”
“因此，美好而高尚的活动，不也使人获得德性，丑恶的活动则使人获得恶德吗？”
“必然如此。”
“现在看来，我们终于只剩下这一点要考察了：做正义的事，
english:
and beauty and good condition of the soul, and vice would be disease, ugliness, and weakness.” “It is so.” “Then is it not also true that beautiful and honorable pursuits tend to the winning of virtue and the ugly to vice?” “Of necessity.”

“And now at last, it seems, it remains for us to consider whether it is profitable to do justice

chinese:
从事高尚的活动，成为正义的人，无论别人知道不知道，对自己是否有利；或者，只要逃避惩罚、不被惩戒改善，那么做不正义的事、成为不正义的人，才是有利的。”
“可是，苏格拉底，”他说，“我认为讨论到了这里，再问就荒唐了：身体的组织一旦败坏，即使拥有全世界的饮食、财富和权力，生活也公认无法忍受；而现在，假如我们赖以生活的那个东西，其本性和组织已经紊乱、
english: and practice honorable pursuits and be just, whether one is known to be such or not, or whether injustice profits, and to be unjust, if only a man escape punishment and is not bettered by chastisement.” “Nay, Socrates,” he said, “I think that from this point on our inquiry becomes an absurdity—if, while life is admittedly intolerable with a ruined constitution of body even though accompanied by all the food and drink and wealth and power in the world, we are yet to be asked to suppose that, when the very nature and constitution of that whereby we live is disordered

chinese:
腐败，却还要我们设想，只要一个人能随心所欲，愿意做任何事，唯独不愿做那些使自己摆脱恶与不正义、获得正义和德性的事，他的生活就值得过吗？尤其现在，我们已经说明，这两者就是我们所描述的样子。”
“是的，很荒唐，”我说，“但尽管如此，既然我们已经攀登到这个高度，就不能疲倦，仍要尽可能清楚地考察，事情确实是这样。”
“我们绝不能疲倦。”他说。
english: and corrupted, life is going to be worth living, if a man can only do as he pleases, and pleases to do anything save that which will rid him of evil and injustice and make him possessed of justice and virtue—now that the two have been shown to be as we have described them.” “Yes, it is absurd,” said I; “but nevertheless, now that we have won to this height, we must not grow weary in endeavoring to discover with the utmost possible clearness that these things are so.” “That is the last thing in the world we must do,” he said.

chinese:
“那么，到这里来，”我说，“你就可以看见恶有多少种；我指的是那些值得观察、区分的种类。”
“我跟着你，”他说，“你继续讲吧。”
“说真的，”我说，“讨论既然已经到了这个高度，我仿佛站在一个瞭望点上，看见德性只有一种形式，恶的形式却无穷无尽；不过，其中有四种值得注意。”
“你是什么意思？”他问。
“各种政治制度有多少种具有明确类型的形式，灵魂的性格大概也就有多少种。”
english: “Come up here then,” said I, “that you may see how many are the kinds of evil, I mean those that it is worth while to observe and distinguish.” “I am with you,” he said; “only do you say on.” “And truly,” said I, “now that we have come to this height of argument I seem to see as from a point of outlook that there is one form of excellence, and that the forms of evil are infinite, yet that there are some four among them that it is worth while to take note of.” “What do you mean?” he said. “As many as are the varieties of political constitutions that constitute specific types, so many, it seems likely, are the characters of soul.”

chinese:
“究竟多少种？”
“五种政治制度，”我说，“五种灵魂。”
“请说说它们是什么。”他说。
“我告诉你，”我说，“其中一种政体，就是我们刚才阐述的那一种，但它可以有两个名称。如果统治者中出现一个德性特别卓越的人，就称为王政；如果不止一人，就称为贤人政体。”
“不错。”他说。
“那么，”我说，“这是我所说的形式中的一种。
english: “How many, pray?” “There are five kinds of constitutions,” said I, “and five kinds of soul.” “Tell me what they are,” he said. “I tell you,” said I, “that one way of government would be the constitution that we have just expounded, but the names that might be applied to it are two. If one man of surpassing merit rose among the rulers, it would be denominated royalty; if more than one, aristocracy.” “True,” he said. “Well, then,” I said, “this is one of the forms I have in mind.

chinese:
因为，无论是一群这样的人，还是其中出现的一个人，只要保存了我们所描述的培养和教育，就不会对城邦的法律作出什么值得一提的改变。”
“不大可能改变。”他说。
english: For neither would a number of such men, nor one if he arose among them, alter to any extent worth mentioning the laws of our city—if he preserved the breeding and the education that we have described.” “It is not likely,” he said.
